3.60.s:
3.296
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ ..
bahirveditvamācakṣva puṇyānyasmākamacyuta ..
tvayā hi jñānadānena bhūya eva sma vardhitāḥ .. 1 ..
3.60.d:
3.296
ऋषय ऊचुः ॥
बहिर्वेदित्वमाचक्ष्व पुण्यान्यस्माकमच्युत ॥
त्वया हि ज्ञानदानेन भूय एव स्म वर्धिताः ॥ 1 ॥
3.60.m:
3.296
The sages said:
Tell us, O Acyuta, of the meritorious acts performed outside the sacrificial altar; / for we have been further elevated by you through the gift of knowledge.

3.60.s:
haṃsa uvāca ..
pānīyametatsakalaṃ trailokyaṃ sacarācaram ..
vikāraḥ salilasyedaṃ sthāvaraṃ jaṅgamaṃ tathā ..2..
3.60.d:
हंस उवाच ॥
पानीयमेतत्सकलं त्रैलोक्यं सचराचरम् ॥
विकारः सलिलस्येदं स्थावरं जङ्गमं तथा ॥2॥
3.60.m:
The Haṃsa said:
All this threefold world, with the moving and the unmoving, is water; / this immobile and mobile creation is a transformation of water.

3.60.s:
pānīyena vinā vṛttirloke nāstīha karhicit ..
krimikīṭapataṅgānāṃ jalameva parāyaṇam .. 3 ..
3.60.d:
पानीयेन विना वृत्तिर्लोके नास्तीह कर्हिचित् ॥
क्रिमिकीटपतङ्गानां जलमेव परायणम् ॥ 3 ॥
3.60.m: Without water, there is never any livelihood in this world; / water alone is the ultimate resort of worms, insects, and winged creatures.

3.60.s:
yatrodakaṃ tatra surāḥ sarva eva pratiṣṭhitāḥ ..
yatrodakaṃ tatra tathā ṛṣayaśca mahāvratāḥ .. 4 ..
3.60.d:
यत्रोदकं तत्र सुराः सर्व एव प्रतिष्ठिताः ॥
यत्रोदकं तत्र तथा ऋषयश्च महाव्रताः ॥ 4 ॥
3.60.m: Where there is water, all the gods are established there; / where there is water, the sages of great vows are likewise there.

3.60.s:
durlabhaṃ tacca lokānāṃ paraloke dvijottamāḥ ..
udakena vinā vṛttirnāsti lokadvaye sadā .. 5 ..
3.60.d:
दुर्लभं तच्च लोकानां परलोके द्विजोत्तमाः ॥
उदकेन विना वृत्तिर्नास्ति लोकद्वये सदा ॥ 5 ॥
3.60.m: And that is difficult for people to obtain in the next world, O best of the twice-born; / without water there is never any sustenance in both worlds.

3.60.s:
tadā jalāśayāḥ kāryāḥ puruṣeṇa vipaścitā ..
agniṣṭomasamāḥ kūpāstvaśvamedhasamaṃ saraḥ .. 6 ..
3.60.d:
तदा जलाशयाः कार्याः पुरुषेण विपश्चिता ॥
अग्निष्टोमसमाः कूपास्त्वश्वमेधसमं सरः ॥ 6 ॥
3.60.m: Therefore, reservoirs of water should be constructed by a wise man; / wells are equal to the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice, and a lake is equal to the horse sacrifice.

3.60.s:
kūpaḥ pravṛttapānīyastvardhaṃ harati duṣkṛtam ..
kūpakṛtsvargamāsādya devabhogānsamaśnute .. 7..
3.60.d:
कूपः प्रवृत्तपानीयस्त्वर्धं हरति दुष्कृतम् ॥
कूपकृत्स्वर्गमासाद्य देवभोगान्समश्नुते ॥ 7॥
3.60.m: A well from which water has begun to flow removes half of one's sins; / the maker of a well, having reached heaven, enjoys divine pleasures.

3.60.s:
tatrāpi bhogavaikalyaṃ sthānābhyāsācca kīrtitam ..
daśakūpa samā vāpī tathā ca parikīrtitā .. 8 ..
3.60.d:
तत्रापि भोगवैकल्यं स्थानाभ्यासाच्च कीर्तितम् ॥
दशकूप समा वापी तथा च परिकीर्तिता ॥ 8 ॥
3.60.m: Even there, a deficiency of enjoyment is mentioned due to [remaining in one] place; / and a stepwell is proclaimed to be equal to ten wells.

3.60.s:
kṛtvā taḍāgaṃ ca tathā vāruṇaṃ lokamaśnute ..
daśavarṣasahasrāṇi nalvamātraṃ dvijottamāḥ ..9 ..
3.60.d:
कृत्वा तडागं च तथा वारुणं लोकमश्नुते ॥
दशवर्षसहस्राणि नल्वमात्रं द्विजोत्तमाः ॥9 ॥
3.60.m: And having made a reservoir, one enjoys the world of Varuṇa / for ten thousand years, if it is only a nalva in size, O best of the twice-born.

3.60.s:
tatrāpi puṇyamāpnoti sthānatyāgāttathā bahu ..
gavāṃ pracāre tatkṛtvā golokaṃ prāpnuyād dhruvam .. 3.296.10 ..
3.60.d:
तत्रापि पुण्यमाप्नोति स्थानत्यागात्तथा बहु ॥
गवां प्रचारे तत्कृत्वा गोलोकं प्राप्नुयाद् ध्रुवम् ॥ 3.296.10 ॥
3.60.m: Even there, one attains abundant merit because of leaving that place; / having made it in a pasture for cattle, he surely reaches Goloka.

3.60.s:
śakralokamavāpnoti taḍāgakaraṇātpathi ..
marau taḍāge pānīyaṃ yasya tiṣṭhati vai dvijāḥ ..11..
3.60.d:
शक्रलोकमवाप्नोति तडागकरणात्पथि ॥
मरौ तडागे पानीयं यस्य तिष्ठति वै द्विजाः ॥11॥
3.60.m: One attains the world of Śakra by making a reservoir on a road; / he in whose reservoir water remains in a desert, O twice-born,

3.60.s:
vimānenārkavarṇena brahmalokaṃ sa gacchati ..
prāvṛṭkāle tu pānīyaṃ taḍāge yasya tiṣṭhati .. 12 ..
3.60.d:
विमानेनार्कवर्णेन ब्रह्मलोकं स गच्छति ॥
प्रावृट्काले तु पानीयं तडागे यस्य तिष्ठति ॥ 12 ॥
3.60.m: goes to the world of Brahmā in an aerial chariot shining like the sun; / and he in whose reservoir water remains in the rainy season,

3.60.s:
agniṣṭomaphalaṃ tasya puruṣasya prakīrtitam ..
dvādaśāhe phalaṃ tasya śaratkāle tu yasya vai .. 13 ..
3.60.d:
अग्निष्टोमफलं तस्य पुरुषस्य प्रकीर्तितम् ॥
द्वादशाहे फलं तस्य शरत्काले तु यस्य वै ॥ 13 ॥
3.60.m: the fruit of the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice is proclaimed for that man; / but he whose [reservoir retains water] in autumn receives the fruit of a twelve-day rite;

3.60.s:
gosavasya tu hemante phalaṃ prāpnoti mānavaḥ ..
pauṇḍarīkaphalaṃ tasya śiśire yasya tiṣṭhati..14..
3.60.d:
गोसवस्य तु हेमन्ते फलं प्राप्नोति मानवः ॥
पौण्डरीकफलं तस्य शिशिरे यस्य तिष्ठति॥14॥
3.60.m: a man obtains the fruit of a Gosava sacrifice in the early winter; / he whose [reservoir retains water] in late winter receives the fruit of a Pauṇḍarīka sacrifice;

3.60.s:
vājapeyaphalaṃ tasya vasante yatra ca dvijāḥ ..
aśvamedhaphalaṃ tasya nidāghe yasya tiṣṭhati .. 15 ..
3.60.d:
वाजपेयफलं तस्य वसन्ते यत्र च द्विजाः ॥
अश्वमेधफलं तस्य निदाघे यस्य तिष्ठति ॥ 15 ॥
3.60.m: he receives the fruit of a Vājapeya sacrifice in spring, O twice-born; / and he whose [reservoir retains water] in summer receives the fruit of a horse sacrifice.

3.60.s:
sasyānāṃ secanārthāya nadīvāhe tathā kṛte ..
annadaḥ prāṇadaścaiva trāṇadaśca tathā bhavet ..16..
3.60.d:
सस्यानां सेचनार्थाय नदीवाहे तथा कृते ॥
अन्नदः प्राणदश्चैव त्राणदश्च तथा भवेत् ॥16॥
3.60.m: When a watercourse from a river is likewise made for the irrigation of crops, / one becomes a giver of food, a giver of life, and a giver of protection.

3.60.s:
bhagīrathasya lokāṃstānsamavāpnotyasaṃśayam ..
pānīyaśodhanaṃ kṛtvā pradeśe devanirmite..17..
3.60.d:
भगीरथस्य लोकांस्तान्समवाप्नोत्यसंशयम् ॥
पानीयशोधनं कृत्वा प्रदेशे देवनिर्मिते॥17॥
3.60.m: By purifying water in a place created by the gods, / a man undoubtedly attains the worlds of Bhagīratha.

3.60.s:
puruṣaḥ phalamāpnoti daśagodānajaṃ dvijāḥ ..
dānapāṣāṇaracitaṃ sukhasevyañjalāśayam .. 18 ..
3.60.d:
पुरुषः फलमाप्नोति दशगोदानजं द्विजाः ॥
दानपाषाणरचितं सुखसेव्यञ्जलाशयम् ॥ 18 ॥
3.60.m: A man obtains the fruit produced by the gift of ten cows, O twice-born ones, / [by constructing] a reservoir built with gift-stones that is easy to use.

3.60.s:
purāṇaṃ mānavaḥ kṛtvā nākaloke mahīyate ..
praṇālakānāṃ karaṇāttṛptimāpnotyanuttamām .. 19 ..
3.60.d:
पुराणं मानवः कृत्वा नाकलोके महीयते ॥
प्रणालकानां करणात्तृप्तिमाप्नोत्यनुत्तमाम् ॥ 19 ॥
3.60.m: Having [renovated] an ancient [reservoir], a mortal is honored in the heavenly world; / by making water conduits he attains unsurpassable satisfaction.

3.60.s:
mahatpuṇyamavāpnoti tathā kṛtvāmalaṃ jalam ..
tṛṣṇāpanodanaṃ kṛtvā caikasyāpīha dehinaḥ .. 3.296.20 ..
3.60.d:
महत्पुण्यमवाप्नोति तथा कृत्वामलं जलम् ॥
तृष्णापनोदनं कृत्वा चैकस्यापीह देहिनः ॥ 3.296.20 ॥
3.60.m: Having made water pure in this way, he obtains great merit. / By removing the thirst of even a single embodied being here,

3.60.s:
mahatphalamavāpnoti nākaloke ca modate ..
svabāhukhātaṃ yaḥ kuryāttaḍāgaṃ matimānnaraḥ .. 21 ..
3.60.d:
महत्फलमवाप्नोति नाकलोके च मोदते ॥
स्वबाहुखातं यः कुर्यात्तडागं मतिमान्नरः ॥ 21 ॥
3.60.m: he obtains a great reward and rejoices in heaven. / An intelligent man who constructs a pond dug by his own arms,

3.60.s:
nalvātphalamavāpnoti rājasūyāśvamedhayoḥ ..
nadīsnānamavāpnoti snānaseturjalāśaye ..22..
3.60.d:
नल्वात्फलमवाप्नोति राजसूयाश्वमेधयोः ॥
नदीस्नानमवाप्नोति स्नानसेतुर्जलाशये ॥22॥
3.60.m: for every nalva obtains the fruit of the Rājasūya and Aśvamedha sacrifices. / A bathing dam [built] in a reservoir obtains [the fruit of] bathing in a river.

3.60.s:
vahukhāte tataḥ (naraḥ) snāto gaṅgāsnānamavāpnuyāt..
sarastu puṇyaṃ yaḥ kuryātkiñcittasya jalāśaye..
puṇyāṃśabhāgī bhavati yasya taddhi jalāśayam..23..
3.60.d:
वहुखाते ततः (नरः) स्नातो गङ्गास्नानमवाप्नुयात्॥
सरस्तु पुण्यं यः कुर्यात्किञ्चित्तस्य जलाशये॥
पुण्यांशभागी भवति यस्य तद्धि जलाशयम्॥23॥
3.60.m: A man who has bathed in a reservoir dug by many would obtain [the fruit of] bathing in the Gaṅgā. / But whoever performs meritorious work on another's reservoir, / he to whom that reservoir belongs becomes a sharer in a portion of the merit.

3.60.s:
prāpnoti tṛptiṃ paramāṃ manuṣyo lokāṃstathāgryānsalilādhipasya ..
jalāśaye'lpe'pi kṛte dvijendrāstasmāttu kāryaṃ salilaṃ nṛloke .. 24 ..
3.297
haṃsa uvāca ..
vṛkṣasaṃropaṇānmartyo mahatphalamupāśnute ..
gulmavallīlatānāṃ ca ropaṇātpuruṣo dvijāḥ ..1..
pratyekaṃ phalamāpnoti godāne yatprakīrtitam ..
agniṣṭomamavāpnoti puṣpavṛkṣasya ropaṇāt .. 2..
pauṇḍarīkamavāpnoti phalavṛkṣasya ropaṇāt ..
ārāmamapi yaḥ kuryātpareṣāṃ nāmakāraṇāt .. 3 ..
tathā haritakārthaṃ ca so'gniṣṭomaphalaṃ labhet ..
puṣpārāmaṃ naraḥ kṛtvā devatārthaṃ manoharam .. 4 ..
devodyāneṣu sarveṣu nandanādiṣu modate ..
yathākāmaṃ vihārī syānnātra kāryā vicāraṇā .. 5 ..
phalārāmaṃ tataḥ kṛtvā vindatyabhyadhikaṃ phalam ..
kṛtvā drumaśatārāmaṃ sośvamedhaphalaṃ labhet .. 6 ..
3.60.d:
प्राप्नोति तृप्तिं परमां मनुष्यो लोकांस्तथाग्र्यान्सलिलाधिपस्य ॥
जलाशयेऽल्पेऽपि कृते द्विजेन्द्रास्तस्मात्तु कार्यं सलिलं नृलोके ॥ 24 ॥
3.297
हंस उवाच ॥
वृक्षसंरोपणान्मर्त्यो महत्फलमुपाश्नुते ॥
गुल्मवल्लीलतानां च रोपणात्पुरुषो द्विजाः ॥1॥
प्रत्येकं फलमाप्नोति गोदाने यत्प्रकीर्तितम् ॥
अग्निष्टोममवाप्नोति पुष्पवृक्षस्य रोपणात् ॥ 2॥
पौण्डरीकमवाप्नोति फलवृक्षस्य रोपणात् ॥
आराममपि यः कुर्यात्परेषां नामकारणात् ॥ 3 ॥
तथा हरितकार्थं च सोऽग्निष्टोमफलं लभेत् ॥
पुष्पारामं नरः कृत्वा देवतार्थं मनोहरम् ॥ 4 ॥
देवोद्यानेषु सर्वेषु नन्दनादिषु मोदते ॥
यथाकामं विहारी स्यान्नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥ 5 ॥
फलारामं ततः कृत्वा विन्दत्यभ्यधिकं फलम् ॥
कृत्वा द्रुमशतारामं सोश्वमेधफलं लभेत् ॥ 6 ॥
3.60.m:
A man attains supreme satisfaction and the foremost worlds of the lord of waters; / even when a small reservoir is made, O best of the twice-born! Therefore water must be provided in the world of mortals.
3.297
Haṃsa said:
From planting trees a mortal enjoys a great reward, / and from planting shrubs, creeping plants, and vines, O twice-born ones, a man
obtains for each one the reward that is proclaimed for the gift of a cow. / From planting a flowering tree he obtains [the fruit of] the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice.
From planting a fruit tree he obtains [the fruit of] the Pauṇḍarīka sacrifice. / And whoever makes a grove for the sake of the name of others,
and for the sake of greenery, he obtains the fruit of the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice. / Having made a delightful flower grove for the deities, a man
rejoices in all the divine pleasure gardens such as Nandana; / he may wander about at his pleasure; there should be no doubt about this.
Having made a fruit orchard, he then attains a still greater fruit. / Having made a grove of a hundred trees, he obtains the reward of the horse sacrifice.

3.60.s:
phalaṃ daśaśatārāme lakṣārāme ca kalpayet ..
campakaṃ mallikāṃ jātīṃ śreṣṭhāḥ puṣpākarā matāḥ .. 7 ..
anyo'dhikamavāpnoti dattvaitānnātra saṃkṣayaḥ ..
gulmeṣu kathitau śreṣṭhau tathobhau bhavyadāḍimau .. 8 ..
pathi śreṣṭhatamau viprā vaṭāśvatthau prakīrtitau ..
nāraṅgadānādbhavati naro rūpasamanvitaḥ .. 9 ..
bījapūrakadānena saubhāgyaṃ mahadāpnuyāt ..
dattvā pālevatāmrau tu tṛptimāpnotyanuttamām .. 3.297.10 ..
āmrākṣoṭapradānena sarvakāmānavāpnuyāt ..
lakṣārāmaṃ tu yaḥ kuryādāmrāṇāmiha mānavaḥ .. 11 ..
devodyāneṣu ramyeṣu krīḍatyamarasannibhaḥ ..
apsarobhiḥ parivṛto na ca tasmānnivartate .. 12 ..
eko'pi ropito vṛkṣaḥ putrakāryakaro bhavet ..
devānprasūnaiḥ prīṇāti chāyayā cātithīṃstathā .. 13 ..
3.60.d:
फलं दशशतारामे लक्षारामे च कल्पयेत् ॥
चम्पकं मल्लिकां जातीं श्रेष्ठाः पुष्पाकरा मताः ॥ 7 ॥
अन्योऽधिकमवाप्नोति दत्त्वैतान्नात्र संक्षयः ॥
गुल्मेषु कथितौ श्रेष्ठौ तथोभौ भव्यदाडिमौ ॥ 8 ॥
पथि श्रेष्ठतमौ विप्रा वटाश्वत्थौ प्रकीर्तितौ ॥
नारङ्गदानाद्भवति नरो रूपसमन्वितः ॥ 9 ॥
बीजपूरकदानेन सौभाग्यं महदाप्नुयात् ॥
दत्त्वा पालेवताम्रौ तु तृप्तिमाप्नोत्यनुत्तमाम् ॥ 3.297.10 ॥
आम्राक्षोटप्रदानेन सर्वकामानवाप्नुयात् ॥
लक्षारामं तु यः कुर्यादाम्राणामिह मानवः ॥ 11 ॥
देवोद्यानेषु रम्येषु क्रीडत्यमरसन्निभः ॥
अप्सरोभिः परिवृतो न च तस्मान्निवर्तते ॥ 12 ॥
एकोऽपि रोपितो वृक्षः पुत्रकार्यकरो भवेत् ॥
देवान्प्रसूनैः प्रीणाति छायया चातिथींस्तथा ॥ 13 ॥
3.60.m:
One should estimate the fruit for a grove of a thousand trees and a grove of a hundred thousand trees. / The campaka, jasmine, and royal jasmine are considered the foremost flower-bearers.
By giving these, another attains even more; there is no diminution in this. / Among shrubs, both the dillenia and pomegranate are stated to be foremost.
Along a road, O brahmins, the banyan and holy fig tree are proclaimed the very best. / From the gift of an orange, a man is endowed with beauty.
By the gift of a citron, he would obtain great good fortune. / Having given an apple and a mango, he attains unsurpassable satisfaction.
By donating a mango and a walnut, he attains all desires. / But the mortal here who makes a grove of a hundred thousand mangoes
plays in charming divine gardens like an immortal, / surrounded by apsarases, and does not return from there.
Even a single tree planted performs the deeds of a son: / it pleases the gods with flowers and guests with shade;

3.60.s:
phalairmanuṣyānprīṇāti nārakyaṃ nāsti pādape ..
api puṣpaphalairhīne drume pānthasya viśramaḥ .. 14 ..
chāyāyāṃ stokakālena bahupuṇyaṃ prayacchati ..
deve varṣati yadvṛkṣātpatrebhyaḥ sravate jalam .. 15 ..

3.60.d:
फलैर्मनुष्यान्प्रीणाति नारक्यं नास्ति पादपे ॥
अपि पुष्पफलैर्हीने द्रुमे पान्थस्य विश्रमः ॥ 14 ॥
छायायां स्तोककालेन बहुपुण्यं प्रयच्छति ॥
देवे वर्षति यद्वृक्षात्पत्रेभ्यः स्रवते जलम् ॥ 15 ॥
तेन तृप्तिमवाप्नोति परलोकगतो ध्रुवम् ॥
तेन नाकमवाप्नोति वृक्षरोपयिता नरः ॥ 16 ॥
सेचनादपि वृक्षस्य रोपितस्य परेण तु ॥
महत्फलमवाप्नोति नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥ 17 ॥
वृक्षायुर्वेदविधिना व्याधितन्तु यथाक्रमम् ॥
नीरुजं मानवः कृत्वा स्वर्गलोकमवाप्नुयात् ॥ 18 ॥
शीतवातातपक्लेशं तथा च्छेदनभेदने ॥
सहन्ते परमं वृक्षास्तद्धि तेषां महत्तपः ॥ 19 ॥
पत्रपुष्पफलैर्नित्यं छायया चैव शाखिनः ॥
परेषामुपयुज्यन्ते तद्धि तेषां महत्तपः ॥ 3.297.20 ॥
तेषां सदा दया कार्या भक्तिः कार्या तथैव च ॥
यस्तेषां भक्तिमान्नित्यं तस्य सा वनदेवता ॥ 21 ॥
3.60.m:
it pleases men with fruits; there is no hellish destination for a tree. / Even in a tree devoid of flowers and fruits, the resting of a traveller
in its shade for a short time confers great merit. / When the rain god rains, whatever water trickles from the leaves of a tree,
by that, one who has gone to the other world certainly obtains satisfaction; / by that, a man who plants a tree attains heaven.
Even from watering a tree planted by another, / he obtains a great fruit; there should be no doubt about this.
Having rendered a diseased [tree] free of disease in due order / according to the rules of arboriculture, a mortal attains the heavenly world.
Trees endure the highest distress from cold, wind, and heat, / as well as cutting and splitting; that indeed is their great austerity.
The branching trees are always useful to others / through leaves, flowers, fruits, and shade; that indeed is their great austerity.
Compassion should always be shown towards them, and devotion should likewise be offered. / For one who is always devoted to them, the goddess of the forest

3.60.d:
तोषमायाति परमं तथा कामान्प्रयच्छति ॥
वानस्पत्यं तथा लोकं देहभेदे समश्नुते ॥ 252 ॥
वानस्पत्ये शुभे लोके सर्वेषामेव शाखिनाम् ॥
शरीरवत्प्रतिष्ठन्ति देवता नात्र संशयः ॥ 23 ॥
याः प्रोक्तास्त्वभिमानिन्यः परां शोभामथास्थिताः ॥
याम्यलोके तथा लोकं वानस्पत्यं प्रकीर्तितम् ॥ 24 ॥
यमलोकमुपासन्ते सर्वास्ता द्रुमदेवताः ॥
द्रुमरोपयितारं च परलोकमुपागतम् ॥ 25 ॥
दिव्येन गीतनृत्येन रमयन्त उपासते ॥
रोपितस्य द्रुमस्येह यथा भवति देवता ॥26॥
याम्ये तु फलदा लोके तथा लोके तु वारुणे ॥
देवता स्यान्महाभागाः कृते पुण्ये जलाशये ॥ 27 ॥
कृते शास्त्रे तथा सम्यग्ब्रह्मलोके तथा द्विजाः ॥
क्षिप्रमेव महाभागा जायन्ते शास्त्रदेवताः ॥ 28 ॥
शास्त्रं जलाशयं वृक्षं सुरवेश्म तथैव च ॥।
मृतस्यापि मनुष्यस्य शरीरमिह कीर्तितम्॥29॥
3.60.m:
attains supreme satisfaction and grants his desires, / and at the dissolution of the body he attains the botanical world.
In the auspicious botanical world, deities of all trees indeed / stand embodied; of this there is no doubt.
Those which are spoken of as the presiding deities assume supreme splendor. / Likewise, the botanical world is proclaimed [to be situated] in the world of Yama.
All those tree deities serve in the world of Yama, / and when the planter of trees has arrived in the other world,
delighting him with celestial song and dance, they attend upon him. / Just as there is a deity here for a planted tree,
who grants fruit in the world of Yama, so in the world of Varuṇa / there will be a deity, O fortunate ones, when a meritorious reservoir is made.
Likewise, when a scripture is properly made, O twice-born ones, in the world of Brahmā, / deities of the scripture are quickly produced, O fortunate ones.
A scripture, a reservoir, a tree, and likewise a temple of the gods / are proclaimed to be the body here even of a deceased man.

3.60.d:
कीर्त्यते येन चान्येन मानवः स्वर्गमाप्नुयात् ॥
तत्तत्कार्यं मनुष्येण स्वर्गमक्षय्यमिच्छता॥3.297.30॥
पुत्राः प्रदिष्टाः पुरुषस्य वृक्षाः स्वयंकृतास्तेषु नरेण भाव्यम् ॥
स्नेहेन नित्यं पुरुषं मृतन्ते कामैस्तु दिव्यैः परितर्पयन्ति ॥ 31 ॥
3.298
हंस उवाच ॥
जलेन नाशमायाति यत्र सम्यद्विजोत्तमाः ॥
जलौघवारणार्थाय तत्र सेतुं करोति यः ॥ 1 ॥
भूमिदाने तु ये लोकाः स तान्प्राप्नोति शाश्वतान् ॥
मार्गसेतुं सुखं कृत्वा वह्निष्टोमफलं लभेत् ॥ 2॥
जलप्रतरणे सेतुं यः करोति नरोत्तमः ॥
स तीर्णः सुखदुःखेभ्यः स्वर्ग लोकं प्रपद्यते ॥ 3 ॥
प्रपां पथि तथा कृत्वा नाकलोके महीयते ॥
प्रपास्थानं शुभं कृत्वा स्थानमाप्नोति शाश्वतम् ॥ 4 ॥
तस्य स्थानात्तथा त्यागात्फलवृद्धिः प्रकीर्तिता ॥
तस्योपलेपनं कृत्वा सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते ॥ 5 ॥
3.60.m:
And whatever else is renowned by which a mortal attains heaven, / every such thing should be done by a man who desires imperishable heaven.
Trees are declared to be sons for a man; they are created by himself; a man should be devoted to them. / They constantly satisfy a dead man with affection through divine desires.
3.298
Haṃsa said:
Where [land] goes to ruin on account of water, O best of the twice-born, / whoever builds a dam there to ward off the flood of water,
he attains those eternal worlds that belong to the gift of land. / Having made an easy causeway on a road, one would obtain the fruit of the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice.
The best of men who constructs a bridge to cross water, / having crossed beyond pleasures and pains, attains the heavenly world.
Likewise, establishing a water-booth on the road, one is honored in heaven. / Making an auspicious site for a water-booth, one attains an eternal abode.
So too, by giving [land] from one's own estate, an increase of merit is declared. / Having plastered and cleaned it, one is freed from all sins.

3.60.d:
दत्त्वा रज्जुमपां स्थाने गोदो भवति मानवः ॥
वारिधानीं तथा दत्त्वा तदेव फलमाप्नुयात् ॥ 6॥
कुम्भप्रदानाद्भवति सदा पूर्णमनोरथः ॥
प्रपायाश्च तथा कृत्वा पुरुषं परिचारकम्॥7॥
सर्वकामसमृद्धस्य यज्ञस्य फलमश्नुते ॥
वर्धमानानि यो दद्यात्प्रपायां द्विजसत्तमाः ॥ 8 ॥
त्रिविधां वृद्धिमाप्नोति तेजसा यशसा श्रिया ॥
लवणस्य प्रदानेन रसानाप्नोति शाश्वतान् ॥ 9 ॥
तत्र हरितदानेन गवां लोकमवाप्नुयात् ॥
फलप्रदानेन तथा वह्निष्टोमफलं लभेत् ॥ 3.298.10 ॥
सक्तूनां च प्रदानेन गोसवस्य फलं नरः ॥
गोरसानां प्रदानेन गवां लोकमवाप्नुयात् ॥ 11 ॥
शय्याश्च विविधाः कृत्वा प्रपायामासनानि च ॥
स्वर्गलोकमवाप्नोति मानुष्ये स्थानमेव च ॥ 12 ॥
कृत्वा निवातं शरणं प्रपास्थाने मनोहरम् ॥
स्वारक्षं लोकमाप्नोति वसूनां नात्र संशयः ॥ 13 ॥
3.60.m:
By giving a rope at a place of water, a human becomes [equal to] a giver of cattle. / Likewise, having given a water vessel, one obtains that very fruit.
From the donation of a jar, one's desires are always fulfilled. / And having appointed a man as an attendant for the water-booth,
one enjoys the fruit of a sacrifice endowed with every desire. / Whoever gives broad dishes at a water-booth, O best of the twice-born,
attains a threefold increase in splendour, fame, and prosperity. / Through the giving of salt, one obtains everlasting savours.
There, by giving greens, one obtains the world of cattle. / Likewise, by the gift of fruit, one obtains the fruit of an agniṣṭoma sacrifice.
By the donation of roasted barley flour, a man [attains] the fruit of a gosava sacrifice. / By the donation of cow-milk products, one obtains the world of cattle.
Having provided various beds and seats at a water-booth, / one attains the heavenly world and indeed a [noble] station in human rebirth.
Having made a delightful shelter free from wind at the site of a water-booth, / one attains the well-guarded world of the Vasus; there is no doubt about this.

3.60.m:
Likewise, having made a fire there to protect people against the cold, / one obtains the brilliance of bodily fire, renown, and good fortune.
By the giving of firewood, one is not overcome by enemies. / Moreover, through the gift of suitable vessels there, one attains heaven.
One attains the world of the moon by providing cold [water]. / And a man [who removes] gravel, clods of earth, stones, and thorns,
clearing them with effort from the path, obtains the fruit of gifting cattle. / Performing massage for the weary, he enjoys that same fruit.
Fanning the exhausted with a palm-leaf fan, / or carrying the weary on his shoulder, a human obtains the fruit of a vājapeya sacrifice.
Carrying an exhausted person with his own mount or vehicle, / he reaches the world of the Sādhyas and enjoys divine pleasures.
Giving food to the exhausted, one obtains eternal desires. / And a man who refreshes the weary with water obtains satiety.

स्वाभ्यां विषमदेशेषु क्षणाद्बहुफलं लभेत् ॥ 21 ॥

मूल्येन वाहयित्वापि परभारं विचक्षणः ॥
तस्य मूल्यस्य दानेन फलं दशगुणं लभेत् ॥ 23 ॥
रक्षणं पथि यः कुर्यात्पान्थानां मानवोत्तमः ॥
प्राप्ताद्वृत्तिमयाद् घोराद्रुद्रलोके महीयते ॥ 24 ॥
नदीतीरेषु सन्तार्य पान्थान्पथि तथा नरः ॥
शीघ्रं तरति दुर्गाणि क्षुरधाराम्̐श्च पर्वतान् ॥ 25 ॥
सदा शौचं तथा नावं यः करोति नदीतटे ॥
अश्वमेधफलं तेन नरः प्राप्नोति कर्मणा ॥ 26 ॥
सभास्थानानि रम्याणि यः करोति विचक्षणः ॥
उद्यानानि विचित्राणि शक्रलोके महीयते ॥27 ॥
3.60.m:
Furnishing an exhausted person in rugged terrain / with shoes and an umbrella of one's own, a human instantly gains great fruit.
And whoever takes a load from one exhausted by a burden and carries it, / by that deed, O foremost of sages, he enjoys the heavenly world.
A wise man who has another's load carried even by paying the fare / obtains tenfold fruit through the giving of that payment.
The best of men who protects travelers on a road / from terrible danger to their livelihood is honored in the world of Rudra.
A man who helps travelers cross at riverbanks along the road / quickly crosses impassable difficulties and razor-edged mountains.
A man who consistently provides cleansing and a boat on a riverbank / attains the fruit of an aśvamedha sacrifice by that deed.
The wise man who creates pleasant assembly places / and variegated gardens is honored in the world of Śakra.

3.60.m:
By providing spectacles, one gains memory and intelligence. / Compassion must be shown to travelers by every possible deed.
The traveler who has set out from his own home is the highest object of compassion. / Wise people should not show partiality towards a traveler, / whether an ascetic or of an order; travelers must be honored in every way.
Having honored a traveler, a man reaches the realm of Puraṃdara / and obtains meritorious divine pleasures in heaven; therefore travelers are most worthy of honor in the world of men.
3.299
Haṃsa said:
The fruit of all meritorious deeds is said by the wise to be fourfold. / Those performed without proper rites, or for the deception of another,
performed by one overcome with anger and greed, one should designate as tāmasika. / But deeds performed out of pride are rājasika.
Those performed here with supreme faith, O twice-born, / with knowledge of the distinct qualities, and performed out of desire for proper procedure, are sāttvika.

3.60.m:
A human always enjoys the fruit of tāmasika deeds in the condition of an animal, / in the state of mixed caste, or in old age,
or in childhood, or in servitude—there should be no doubt about this. / Otherwise, in human life, one receives the fruit of rājasika deeds.
One enjoys the fruit of sāttvika deeds in divinity; of this there is no doubt. / And liberation is declared to be the fruit of deeds performed with the highest virtue.
Of actions to be accomplished through wealth, wealth is remembered to be threefold: / black, speckled, and white, O best of the twice-born.
The fruit of that threefold [wealth] is proclaimed to be threefold. / Whatever is done with black wealth is enjoyed indeed in the condition of an animal.
White wealth for the castes is that which is earned by one's own proper occupation. / Speckled wealth is declared to come from the occupation of the caste immediately adjacent,
and wealth earned by a higher caste through the occupation of a lower is called black. / Nevertheless, I shall declare what is white for the castes, O best of the twice-born.

3.60.m:
For a brahmin, what is obtained through acceptance of gifts, from a sacrificer, and from a pupil / who are endowed with good qualities—that wealth is threefold white.
For a kṣatriya, threefold white wealth is declared to be / that acquired in battle, through tax, and from judicial fines.
For a vaiśya, [wealth acquired] having engaged in agriculture, trade, and cattle-rearing is white. / For a śūdra, that acquired by service to the twice-born is proclaimed pure.
A brāhmaṇa should by no means perform the work of a śūdra, / nor a śūdra the work of a brāhmaṇa; each would cause the fall of the other.
(Neither superior nor inferior work is found for these two, / leaving aside the two intermediate duties, which are common to all and beneficial.
I shall explain the various kinds of wealth of all the classes.) / Wealth acquired by sycophancy, gambling, theft, forgery, and acts of violence,
or by deception, is declared 'black' for everyone. / Wealth gained through service in the crafts, through usury,

and received from one who has been aided, is called 'mottled'. / That which has come by succession, as a gift of love, or obtained with a wife,
is universally declared 'white' wealth for everyone. / Religious merit performed with white wealth yields abundant fruit.
A wise man, having performed meritorious deeds with lawfully acquired wealth, enjoys divine delights in heaven / for a long time, being of great majesty; therefore, one should acquire wealth by lawful means.
3.300 / Haṃsa said: / Gods praise giving, and humans likewise, O twice-born! / Through giving, one obtains whatever desires one wishes for in one's mind.
Seeing wretched beings here dependent on others because they gave no gifts, / a man should establish wealth for the next world by giving gifts to brahmins.
A gift to an animal is equal [in reward to the gift itself], but to cattle it is known to bear great fruit. / That very [gift] is declared to be doubled when given to a person of mixed caste;
it is said to be fourfold to a śūdra, and it becomes eightfold to a vaiśya; / sixteenfold to a kṣatriya, and precisely the same to a nominal brahmin.

3.60.m:
A gift given to one devoted to the study of the Veda is recorded as thirty-two-fold; / a hundredfold to one distinguished therein, and measured as a hundred-thousand-fold to an advanced scholar.
That very [gift] is said to be endless when given to a brahmin who has mastered the Veda. / The domestic priest is a worthy recipient for oneself, but not for another;
one's gift given to a domestic priest is declared imperishable. / Likewise, a man [giving] to an officiating priest, a sacrificial priest, and also to a guru,
need not consider class toward mother and father, / maternal aunt, sister, and likewise paternal aunt,
maternal grandmother, niece, and likewise nephew, / daughter's son, and son-in-law: what is given to them is imperishable.
What is likewise given to one fallen from prosperity is also declared imperishable. / A man who again restores one who has fallen from his position
attains the heavenly realm for a long time through that deed here. / He who reinstates in his own kingdom a king fallen from his realm

स याति शक्रसालोक्यं यावच्छक्राश्चतुर्दश ॥
ततो मानुष्यमासाद्य राजा भवति धार्मिकः ॥ 12 ॥
तस्माद्दानं श्रीविहीनं दातव्यं भूतिमिच्छता ॥
श्रीविहीनेषु यद्दत्तं तदनन्तं प्रकीर्तितम् ॥ 13 ॥
काले पात्रे तथा देशे धनं न्यायागतं तथा ॥
यद्दत्तं ब्राह्मणश्रेष्ठास्तदनन्तं प्रकीर्तितम् ॥ 14 ॥
द्वादशीषु तु यद्दत्तं शुक्लासु तु विशेषतः ॥
श्रवणेन तु युक्तासु तत्रापि द्विजसत्तमाः ॥ 15 ॥
विशेषाद्बुधयुक्तासु पक्षान्तेषु च यत्तथा ॥
तृतीयासु तु शुक्लासु सर्वासु च विशेषतः ॥ 16 ॥
वैशाखशुक्लपक्षे तु विशेषेण च मानदाः ॥
आषाढे कार्तिके चैव फाल्गुने च विशेषतः ॥ 17 ॥
तिस्रस्त्वेताः पौर्णमास्यो दाने विप्रा महाफलाः ॥
व्यतीपातेषु यद्दत्तं जन्मर्क्षे तु द्विजोत्तमाः ॥ 18 ॥
3.60.m:
goes to the realm of Śakra for as long as fourteen Śakras endure; / then, attaining human birth, he becomes a righteous king.
Therefore, a gift should be given to one destitute of prosperity by one desiring prosperity; / what is given to the destitute of prosperity is declared endless.
O best of brahmins, lawfully acquired wealth given / at the proper time, to a worthy recipient, and in the proper place, is proclaimed endless.
What is given on the twelfth days of the lunar fortnight, especially the bright ones, / particularly on those joined with the Śravaṇa asterism, O best of the twice-born,
especially on those joined with Wednesday, and on the days of the new or full moon; / likewise on all the bright third lunar days, and especially
in the bright fortnight of Vaiśākha, O givers of honor; / and especially in Āṣāḍha, Kārtika, and Phālguna—
these three full-moon days yield great fruit for giving, O brahmins. / What is given during Vyatīpāta yogas, and on one's birth constellation, O best of the twice-born,

ग्रहसंक्रमकाले तु त्यागे च मिथुनस्य तु ॥
रत्रेर्महाफलं दत्तन्तेभ्योऽपि स्यान्महाफलम् ॥ 19 ॥
यदा प्रविशते भानुर्मकरं द्विजसत्तमाः ॥
आषाढेऽश्वयुजे पौषे चैत्रे शुक्ले तथैव च ॥ 3.300.20 ॥
द्वादशीप्रभृति प्रोक्तं पुण्यं दिनचतुष्टयम् ॥
मिथुनं च तथा कन्या धन्विनं मीनमेव च ॥ 21 ॥
प्रविष्टे भास्करे पुण्यं प्रत्येकं कथितं द्विजाः ॥
षडशीतिमुखं नाम दाने दिनचतुष्टयम् ॥ 22॥
अच्छिन्ननाड्यां यद्दत्तं पुत्रे जाते द्विजोत्तमाः ॥
संस्कारेषु च पुत्रस्य तदक्षय्यं प्रकीर्तितम् ॥ 23 ॥
चन्द्रे वा यदि वा सूर्ये दृष्टे राहौ महाग्रहे ॥
अक्षयं कथितं दत्तं तत्राप्येकं विशेषतः ॥ 24 ॥
पुष्करेषु प्रयागे च प्रभासे नैमिषे तथा ॥
धर्मारण्ये गयायाञ्च तथैवामरकण्टके ॥ 25 ॥
3.60.m:
at the moment of a planet's ingress, and at the sun's departure from Gemini, / during the night bears great fruit, and even greater fruit may come from them;
when the sun enters Capricorn, O best of the twice-born; / likewise in the bright fortnights of Āṣāḍha, Aśvayuja, Pauṣa, and Caitra,
the four days beginning with the twelfth are proclaimed meritorious. / And when the sun enters Gemini, Virgo,
Sagittarius, and Pisces, O twice-born, / each four-day period called the Ṣaḍaśītimukha is declared meritorious for giving.
What is given when a son is born before the umbilical cord is severed, O best of the twice-born, / and during the sacraments of a son, is declared imperishable.
When the moon or the sun is seized by the great planet Rāhu, / a gift is declared imperishable, especially that one given there.
At Puṣkara, Prayāga, Prabhāsa, Naimiṣa, / Dharmāraṇya, Gayā, and likewise Amarakaṇṭaka;

मानसे च तथा पुण्ये तथैवोत्तरमानस ॥

निम्नगानां च तीरेषु ज्ञेयं बहुफलं हि तत् ॥
दीनान्धकृपणानाथवाग्विहीनेषु यत्तथा ॥ 3.300.30 ॥
विकलेषु तथान्येषु जडवामनपङ्गुषु ॥

यद्दत्तेन च वित्तेन व्यसनादुत्तरेत्पुरः ॥
न स किञ्चिदवाप्नोति व्यसनं मनुजोत्तमः ॥ 34 ॥
स्त्रियं मेषमजं चैव गामश्वं तुरगन्नरम् ॥
एकमेकं तु दातव्यमेकस्य बहवोऽपि वा 35 ॥
एकं बहूनां तद्दत्तं ध्रुवं नरकमृच्छति ॥
आदातुर्नरकाय स्यात्तदा दातुर्द्विजोत्तमाः ॥ 36 ॥
विक्रयं तु समापन्ना यो दत्त्वा जीवदक्षिणाम् ॥
एवं काले च पात्रे च देशे शुद्धागमं धनम् ॥ 37 ॥
दत्त्वा धनमवाप्नोति देवब्राह्मणक्षत्त्रियान् ॥
धनं बहिश्चराः प्राणा धने सर्वं प्रतिष्ठितम् ॥ 38 ॥
धनादन्नं तथान्नेन सर्वो जीवति वै जनः ॥
यावन्ति लोके पुण्यानि तेभ्यो दाता विशिष्यते ॥
दानेन तदवाप्नोति यत्किञ्चिन्मनसेप्सितम् ॥ 39 ॥
दानेन लोके प्रियतामुपैति दानेन नाकं पुरुषः प्रयाति ॥
मानुष्यमासाद्य च दानशीलो भोगानवाप्नोति मनोभिरामान् ॥ 3.300.40 ॥
3.60.m:
A man by whose given wealth someone is delivered from calamity beforehand— / that best of men encounters no calamity whatsoever.
A woman, a ram, a goat, a cow, a horse, a steed, a man: / one by one they should be given to a single recipient, or even many to one.
That which is single given to many surely leads to hell; / it leads to hell for the receiver, and then for the giver, O best of the twice-born.
He who, having given a living being as a sacrificial fee, reduces it to sale— / thus wealth of pure origin given at the proper time, to a worthy recipient, and in the proper place...
By giving wealth, he obtains gods, brahmins, and kṣatriyas. / Wealth is the external vital breath; everything is established in wealth.
From wealth comes food, and by food every creature indeed lives. / Whatever merits there are in the world, the giver surpasses them. / By giving, he attains whatever is desired by his mind.
Through giving, a person attains affection in the world; through giving, he goes to heaven; / and having attained human birth, one who is fond of giving obtains pleasures pleasing to the mind.

3.61.m: Haṃsa said: / O brahmins, an acceptance of gifts should not be made during death impurity or birth impurity; / even then, however, the sacrificial fee that is the gift of fearlessness should be given.

3.61.s:
pratigrahaṃ paṭheduccaiḥ pratigṛhya dvijottamaḥ ..
mandaṃ paṭhettu rājanyādupāṃśu ca tathā viśaḥ .. 12 ..
3.61.d:
प्रतिग्रहं पठेदुच्चैः प्रतिगृह्य द्विजोत्तमः ॥
मन्दं पठेत्तु राजन्यादुपांशु च तथा विशः ॥ 12 ॥
3.61.m: Having accepted [a gift], the best of the twice-born should recite the formula of acceptance aloud; / from a kṣatriya he should recite softly, and in a whisper from a vaiśya;

3.61.s:
manasā tu tathā śūdrātsvastivācanikaṃ tathā ..
soṃkāraṃ brāhmaṇe kuryānniroṃkāraṃ mahīpatau .. 13 ..
3.61.d:
मनसा तु तथा शूद्रात्स्वस्तिवाचनिकं तथा ॥
सोंकारं ब्राह्मणे कुर्यान्निरोंकारं महीपतौ ॥ 13 ॥
3.61.m: and mentally from a śūdra; likewise he should make the pronouncement of blessing: / with ‘Oṃ’ for a brahmin, and without ‘Oṃ’ for a king;

3.61.s:
upāṃśu ca tathā vaiśye svasti śūdre prakīrtitam ..
abhayaṃ sarvadaivatyaṃ bhūmirvai viṣṇudevatā .. 14 ..
3.61.d:
उपांशु च तथा वैश्ये स्वस्ति शूद्रे प्रकीर्तितम् ॥
अभयं सर्वदैवत्यं भूमिर्वै विष्णुदेवता ॥ 14 ॥
3.61.m: whispered for a vaiśya, and ‘svasti’ is declared for a śūdra. / Fearlessness has all deities as its divinity; earth has Viṣṇu as its divinity.

3.61.s:
kanyādānaṃ tathā dāsī prājāpatyāḥ prakīrtitāḥ ..
tathā caikaśaphaṃ sarvaṃ kathitaṃ yamadaivatam .. 15 ..
3.61.d:
कन्यादानं तथा दासी प्राजापत्याः प्रकीर्तिताः ॥
तथा चैकशफं सर्वं कथितं यमदैवतम् ॥ 15 ॥
3.61.m: The gift of a maiden and a female slave are declared to belong to Prajāpati; / likewise, all one-hoofed animals are taught to belong to Yama.

3.61.s:
māhiṣaṃ ca tathā sāmyaṃ coṣṭraṃ vai nairṛtaṃ bhavet ..
raudrī dhenurvinirdiṣṭā cchāgamāgneyamucyate .. 16..
3.61.d:
माहिषं च तथा साम्यं चोष्ट्रं वै नैरृतं भवेत् ॥
रौद्री धेनुर्विनिर्दिष्टा च्छागमाग्नेयमुच्यते ॥ 16॥
3.61.m: A buffalo belongs to Soma, and a camel belongs to Nirṛti; / a milch cow is prescribed for Rudra, and a goat is said to belong to Agni.

3.61.s:
meṣaṃ tu vāruṇaṃ vidyādvarāho vaiṣṇavaḥ smṛtaḥ..
āraṇyāḥ paśavaḥ sarve kathitā vāyudaivatāḥ .. 17 ..
3.61.d:
मेषं तु वारुणं विद्याद्वराहो वैष्णवः स्मृतः॥
आरण्याः पशवः सर्वे कथिता वायुदैवताः ॥ 17 ॥
3.61.m: One should know a sheep belongs to Varuṇa, and a boar is remembered as belonging to Viṣṇu; / all wild beasts are taught to have Vāyu as their deity.

3.61.s:
jalāśayāni sarvāṇi vāridhānī kamaṇḍaluḥ ..
kumbhaṃ ca karakaṃ caiva vāruṇāni dvijottamāḥ .. 18 ..
3.61.d:
जलाशयानि सर्वाणि वारिधानी कमण्डलुः ॥
कुम्भं च करकं चैव वारुणानि द्विजोत्तमाः ॥ 18 ॥
3.61.m: All reservoirs of water, water-pots, the water-jar, / the pitcher, and the water-vessel belong to Varuṇa, O best of the twice-born.

3.61.s:
samudrajāni ratnāni vāruṇāni dvijottamāḥ ..
āgneyaṃ kanakaṃ proktaṃ sarvalohāni cāpyatha .. 19 ..
3.61.d:
समुद्रजानि रत्नानि वारुणानि द्विजोत्तमाः ॥
आग्नेयं कनकं प्रोक्तं सर्वलोहानि चाप्यथ ॥ 19 ॥
3.61.m: Jewels produced in the ocean belong to Varuṇa, O best of the twice-born; / gold is declared to belong to Agni, and all base metals as well.

3.61.s:
prājāpatyāni sasyāni pakvānnamapi ca dvijāḥ ..
jñeyāni sarvagandhāni gāndharvāṇi vicakṣaṇaiḥ .. 3.301.20 ..
3.61.d:
प्राजापत्यानि सस्यानि पक्वान्नमपि च द्विजाः ॥
ज्ञेयानि सर्वगन्धानि गान्धर्वाणि विचक्षणैः ॥ 3.301.20 ॥
3.61.m: Crops belong to Prajāpati, as well as cooked food, O twice-born; / all fragrances should be known by the wise to belong to the Gandharvas.

3.61.s:
bārhaspatyaṃ smṛtaṃ vāsaḥ saumyānyatha rasāni ca ..
pakṣiṇaśca tathā sarve vāyavyā parikīrtitāḥ .. 21 ..
3.61.d:
बार्हस्पत्यं स्मृतं वासः सौम्यान्यथ रसानि च ॥
पक्षिणश्च तथा सर्वे वायव्या परिकीर्तिताः ॥ 21 ॥
3.61.m: A garment is recorded as belonging to Bṛhaspati, and flavors belong to Soma; / and likewise all birds are proclaimed to belong to Vāyu.

3.61.s:
vidyā brāhmī vinirdiṣṭā vidyopakaraṇāni ca ..
sārasvatāni jñeyāni pustakādyāni paṃḍitaiḥ ..22..
3.61.d:
विद्या ब्राह्मी विनिर्दिष्टा विद्योपकरणानि च ॥
सारस्वतानि ज्ञेयानि पुस्तकाद्यानि पंडितैः ॥22॥
3.61.m: Knowledge is prescribed as belonging to Brahmā, and the implements of knowledge— / books and the like—should be known by the learned to belong to Sarasvatī.

3.61.s:
sarveṣāṃ śilpabhāṇḍānāṃ viśvakarmā tu devatā ..
drumāṇāmatha puṣpāṇāṃ śākahāritakaiḥ saha .. 23 ..
3.61.d:
सर्वेषां शिल्पभाण्डानां विश्वकर्मा तु देवता ॥
द्रुमाणामथ पुष्पाणां शाकहारितकैः सह ॥ 23 ॥
3.61.m: Viśvakarman is the deity of all artisan utensils; / of trees and flowers, together with vegetables and greens,

3.61.s:
phalānāmapi sarveṣāṃ tathā jñeyo vanaspatiḥ ..
matsyamāṃsaṃ vinirdiṣṭaṃ prājāpatyaṃ tathaiva ca .. 24 ..
3.61.d:
फलानामपि सर्वेषां तथा ज्ञेयो वनस्पतिः ॥
मत्स्यमांसं विनिर्दिष्टं प्राजापत्यं तथैव च ॥ 24 ॥
3.61.m: and of all fruits as well, Vanaspati should be known [as the deity]; / fish and meat are likewise prescribed as belonging to Prajāpati.

3.61.s:
chatraṃ kṛṣṇājinaṃ śayyā rathamāsanameva ca ..
upānahau tathā yānaṃ yaccānyatprāṇivarjitam ..25..
3.61.d:
छत्रं कृष्णाजिनं शय्या रथमासनमेव च ॥
उपानहौ तथा यानं यच्चान्यत्प्राणिवर्जितम् ॥25॥
3.61.m: An umbrella, a black antelope skin, a bed, a chariot, a seat, / shoes, a conveyance, and whatever else is devoid of life:

3.61.s:
uttānāṅgirase tvetatpratigṛhṇīta mānavaḥ ..
parjanyāya tathā sīraṃ śastravarmadhvajādikam .. 26 ..
3.61.d:
उत्तानाङ्गिरसे त्वेतत्प्रतिगृह्णीत मानवः ॥
पर्जन्याय तथा सीरं शस्त्रवर्मध्वजादिकम् ॥ 26 ॥
3.61.m: a man should accept this [with the formula] ‘To Uttāna Āṅgirasa’; / a plough belongs to Parjanya; weapons, armor, flags, and the like,

3.61.s:
raṇopakaraṇaṃ sarvaṃ kathitaṃ cakradaivatam ..
grahantu sarvadaivatyaṃ yadyaduktaṃ dvijottamāḥ .. 27 ..
3.61.d:
रणोपकरणं सर्वं कथितं चक्रदैवतम् ॥
ग्रहन्तु सर्वदैवत्यं यद्यदुक्तं द्विजोत्तमाः ॥ 27 ॥
3.61.m: all equipment of battle is taught to have the Discus as its deity. / Whatever acceptance of gifts is said to belong to all deities, O best of the twice-born,

3.61.s:
tajjñeyaṃ viṣṇudaivatyaṃ sarvaṃ vā dvijasattamāḥ ..
bhūmeḥ pratigrahaṃ kuryādbhūmiṃ kṛtvā pradakṣiṇam .. 28 ..
3.61.d:
तज्ज्ञेयं विष्णुदैवत्यं सर्वं वा द्विजसत्तमाः ॥
भूमेः प्रतिग्रहं कुर्याद्भूमिं कृत्वा प्रदक्षिणम् ॥ 28 ॥
3.61.m: that, or everything, should be known to have Viṣṇu as its divinity, O excellent twice-born. / One should make the acceptance of land having circumambulated the land.

3.61.s:
kare gṛhya tathā kanyāṃ dāsīdāsau dvijottamāḥ ..
karantu hṛdi vinyasya dharmyo jñeyaḥ pratigrahaḥ .. 29 ..
3.61.d:
करे गृह्य तथा कन्यां दासीदासौ द्विजोत्तमाः ॥
करन्तु हृदि विन्यस्य धर्म्यो ज्ञेयः प्रतिग्रहः ॥ 29 ॥
3.61.m: Taking a maiden, a female slave, or a male slave by the hand, O best of the twice-born, / and placing the hand upon one's heart, the acceptance of gifts should be known to be according to dharma.

3.61.s:
āruhya ca gajasyoktaḥ karṇe cāśvasya kīrtitaḥ ..
tathā caikaśaphānāṃ ca sarveṣāmaviśeṣataḥ .. 3.301.30 ..
3.61.d:
आरुह्य च गजस्योक्तः कर्णे चाश्वस्य कीर्तितः ॥
तथा चैकशफानां च सर्वेषामविशेषतः ॥ 3.301.30 ॥
3.61.m: The acceptance of an elephant is declared by mounting it, and of a horse by [touching] its ear; / and likewise for all single-hoofed animals without distinction.

3.61.s:
pratigṛhṇīta gāṃ pucche hyante kṛṣṇājinaṃ tathā ..
karṇe'jāḥ paśavaścānye grāhyāḥ pucche vicakṣaṇaiḥ .. 31 ..
3.61.d:
प्रतिगृह्णीत गां पुच्छे ह्यन्ते कृष्णाजिनं तथा ॥
कर्णेऽजाः पशवश्चान्ये ग्राह्याः पुच्छे विचक्षणैः ॥ 31 ॥
3.61.m: One should accept a cow by the tail, and a black antelope skin by the border; / goats should be taken by the ear, and other animals by the tail, by the wise.

3.61.s:
pratigrahastvathoṣṭrasya āruhyaiva tathā bhavet ..
bījānāṃ muṣṭimādāya ratnānyādāya sarvataḥ .. 32 ..
3.61.d:
प्रतिग्रहस्त्वथोष्ट्रस्य आरुह्यैव तथा भवेत् ॥
बीजानां मुष्टिमादाय रत्नान्यादाय सर्वतः ॥ 32 ॥
3.61.m: The acceptance of a camel should be made by mounting it; / [a gift] of seeds by taking a handful, and jewels by taking them completely.

3.61.s:
vasuṃ daśāntādādadyātparidhāyātha vā punaḥ ..
āruhyopānahau mantramāruhyaiva ca pāduke .. 33 ..
3.61.d:
वसुं दशान्तादादद्यात्परिधायाथ वा पुनः ॥
आरुह्योपानहौ मन्त्रमारुह्यैव च पादुके ॥ 33 ॥
3.61.m: One should receive a garment by the hem, or having put it on; / shoes and sandals by stepping onto them [and reciting] the mantra.

3.61.s:
īṣādhastu rathaṃ grāhyaṃ chatraṃ daṃḍe tu vācayet ..
drumāṇāmatha sarveṣāṃ mūle nyastakaro dvijāḥ .. 34 ..
3.61.d:
ईषाधस्तु रथं ग्राह्यं छत्रं दंडे तु वाचयेत् ॥
द्रुमाणामथ सर्वेषां मूले न्यस्तकरो द्विजाः ॥ 34 ॥
3.61.m: A chariot should be received beneath the pole, and an umbrella he should recite over by the handle; / of all trees, O twice-born, having placed his hand at the root.

3.61.s:
āyudhāni samādāya tathonmucya vibhūṣaṇam ..
varmadhvajau tathā spṛṣṭvā praviśya ca tathā gṛham ..35..
3.61.d:
आयुधानि समादाय तथोन्मुच्य विभूषणम् ॥
वर्मध्वजौ तथा स्पृष्ट्वा प्रविश्य च तथा गृहम् ॥35॥
3.61.m: Having taken up weapons, and having taken off ornaments; / having touched armor and flags, and having entered a house;

3.61.s:
avatīrya tu sarvāṇi jalasthānāni vai dvijāḥ..
dravyāṇyanyānyathādāya spṛṣṭvā tu brāhmaṇaḥ paṭheta .. 36 ..
3.61.d:
अवतीर्य तु सर्वाणि जलस्थानानि वै द्विजाः॥
द्रव्याण्यन्यान्यथादाय स्पृष्ट्वा तु ब्राह्मणः पठेत ॥ 36 ॥
3.61.m: and having descended into all water places, O twice-born; / having taken or touched other objects, the brahmin should recite [the formula].

3.61.s:
kanyādāne tu ca paṭheddravyāṇāntu pṛthakpṛthak ..
pratigrahe dvijaśreṣṭhāstatraivāntarbhavanti te .. 37 ..
3.61.d:
कन्यादाने तु च पठेद्द्रव्याणान्तु पृथक्पृथक् ॥
प्रतिग्रहे द्विजश्रेष्ठास्तत्रैवान्तर्भवन्ति ते ॥ 37 ॥
3.61.m: In the gift of a maiden, however, he should recite over the objects individually; / in accepting her, O best of the twice-born, they are all included in that very act.

3.61.s:
dravyāṇāmatha sarveṣāṃ dravyasaṃśravaṇānnarāḥ ..
vācayejjalamādāya kareṇātha pratigraham .. 38 ..
3.61.d:
द्रव्याणामथ सर्वेषां द्रव्यसंश्रवणान्नराः ॥
वाचयेज्जलमादाय करेणाथ प्रतिग्रहम् ॥ 38 ॥
3.61.m: Of all articles, men, having heard the mention of the article, / should cause the acceptance of the gift to be recited, having taken water in the hand.

3.61.s:
pratigrahasya yo dharmaṃ na jānāti dvijo vidhim ..
dravyastainyasamāyukto narakaṃ pratipadyate .. 39 ..
3.61.d:
प्रतिग्रहस्य यो धर्मं न जानाति द्विजो विधिम् ॥
द्रव्यस्तैन्यसमायुक्तो नरकं प्रतिपद्यते ॥ 39 ॥
3.61.m: The twice-born who does not know the dharma, the rule of acceptance of gifts, / is joined with theft of property and goes to hell.

3.61.s:
niṣkrīṇāti tu taddravyaṃ brāhmaṇastu pratigrahāt ..
vidhiṃ tu dharmyaṃ vijñāya brāhmaṇastu pratigrahe .. 3.301.40 ..
3.61.d:
निष्क्रीणाति तु तद्द्रव्यं ब्राह्मणस्तु प्रतिग्रहात् ॥
विधिं तु धर्म्यं विज्ञाय ब्राह्मणस्तु प्रतिग्रहे ॥ 3.301.40 ॥
3.61.m: A brahmin redeems that property through acceptance of gifts; / but having understood the lawful rule for acceptance of gifts, a brahmin

3.61.s:
ātmanaḥ śreyasā yogaṃ kuryāddātā tathaiva ca ..
bhuvaṃ dhenumathāśvaṃ ca ratnāni kanakaṃ tathā .. 41 ..
3.61.d:
आत्मनः श्रेयसा योगं कुर्याद्दाता तथैव च ॥
भुवं धेनुमथाश्वं च रत्नानि कनकं तथा ॥ 41 ॥
3.61.m: and likewise a giver should unite themselves with the highest good. / Land, a milk-cow, a horse, jewels, and gold,

3.61.s:
tilāni kuñjaraṃ dadyānnāvijñāya guṇāguṇān ..
ānṛśaṃsyena sarvasya dadyādannaṃ vicakṣaṇaḥ ..42..
3.61.d:
तिलानि कुञ्जरं दद्यान्नाविज्ञाय गुणागुणान् ॥
आनृशंस्येन सर्वस्य दद्यादन्नं विचक्षणः ॥42॥
3.61.m: sesame seeds, and an elephant one should not give without knowing merits and demerits. / Out of compassion a wise man should give food to everyone,

3.61.s:
vāsaśca dadyātsarvasya sarvasādhāraṇe hite ..
vidhiṃ dharmyamavijñāya yastu kuryātpratigraham .. 43 ..
3.61.d:
वासश्च दद्यात्सर्वस्य सर्वसाधारणे हिते ॥
विधिं धर्म्यमविज्ञाय यस्तु कुर्यात्प्रतिग्रहम् ॥ 43 ॥
3.61.m: and he should give clothing to everyone for the common benefit of all. / But he who accepts gifts without knowing the lawful rule

3.61.s:
dātrā saha taratyeva naiva durgāṇyasau dvijāḥ ..
tasmātsarvaprayatnena vidhirjñeyaḥ pratigrahe .. 44 ..
3.61.d:
दात्रा सह तरत्येव नैव दुर्गाण्यसौ द्विजाः ॥
तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन विधिर्ज्ञेयः प्रतिग्रहे ॥ 44 ॥
3.61.m: does not cross difficulties along with the giver, O twice-born. / Therefore, by every effort the rule regarding acceptance of gifts must be known.

3.61.s:
pratigraho yo vidhinā gṛhīto dvayostu yogaṃ parameṇa kuryāt ..
paratra saṃbhṛtya tatheha loke sa śreyase nātra vicāramasti .. .. 45 ..
3.302
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ ..
pṛthakpṛthak tvamācakṣva dānānāṃ phalamuttamam ..
sarvadharmabhṛtāṃ śreṣṭha sarvajñastvaṃ mato hi naḥ .. 1 ..
.. haṃsa uvāca .. ..
abhayasya pradānāddhi nānyaddānaṃ viśiṣyate ..
sarveṣāmeva dānānāṃ prāṇadānaṃ viśiṣyate .. 2 ..
grāhyaṃ prāṇapradānantu caṇḍālātpukkasādapi ..
jīvansarvamavāpnoti jīvandharmaṃ karoti ca .. 3 ..
jīvamānastu puruṣaḥ kāmānāṃ bhājanaṃ bhavet ..
bhājanena tu sarvaṃ vai bhājanatvaṃ vinaśyati .. 4 ..
śarīradharmasarvasvaṃ rakṣaṇāya prayatnataḥ ..
śarīrātsravate dharmaṃ parvatātsalilaṃ yathā .. 5 ..
abhayasya pradānena naraḥ syātsarvakāmadaḥ ..
aśvamedhaphalaṃ tasya yo rakṣeccharaṇāgatam .. 6 ..
3.61.d:
प्रतिग्रहो यो विधिना गृहीतो द्वयोस्तु योगं परमेण कुर्यात् ॥
परत्र संभृत्य तथेह लोके स श्रेयसे नात्र विचारमस्ति ॥ ॥ 45 ॥
3.302
ऋषय ऊचुः ॥
पृथक्पृथक् त्वमाचक्ष्व दानानां फलमुत्तमम् ॥
सर्वधर्मभृतां श्रेष्ठ सर्वज्ञस्त्वं मतो हि नः ॥ 1 ॥
॥ हंस उवाच ॥ ॥
अभयस्य प्रदानाद्धि नान्यद्दानं विशिष्यते ॥
सर्वेषामेव दानानां प्राणदानं विशिष्यते ॥ 2 ॥
ग्राह्यं प्राणप्रदानन्तु चण्डालात्पुक्कसादपि ॥
जीवन्सर्वमवाप्नोति जीवन्धर्मं करोति च ॥ 3 ॥
जीवमानस्तु पुरुषः कामानां भाजनं भवेत् ॥
भाजनेन तु सर्वं वै भाजनत्वं विनश्यति ॥ 4 ॥
शरीरधर्मसर्वस्वं रक्षणाय प्रयत्नतः ॥
शरीरात्स्रवते धर्मं पर्वतात्सलिलं यथा ॥ 5 ॥
अभयस्य प्रदानेन नरः स्यात्सर्वकामदः ॥
अश्वमेधफलं तस्य यो रक्षेच्छरणागतम् ॥ 6 ॥
3.61.m:
An acceptance of gifts taken in accordance with the rule unites both with the highest [good]. / Having brought about [benefit] in the next world as well as in this world, it leads to the highest good; there is no doubt about this.
3.302
The sages said: / Declare to us one by one the supreme fruit of gifts, / O best of all maintainers of dharma, for we consider you omniscient.
Haṃsa said: / Indeed, no other gift is superior to the granting of freedom from fear; / of all gifts, the gift of life is superior.
The gift of life should be received even from a caṇḍāla or a pukkasa. / Living, one attains everything, and living, one performs dharma.
For a living man becomes a vessel for desires; / but through the vessel, indeed, all vessel-ness is preserved [from being lost].
One's entire body and dharma should be preserved with effort. / From the body flows dharma, as water from a mountain.
Through the gift of freedom from fear, a man becomes a granter of all desires. / He who protects one who comes for refuge attains the fruit of an aśvamedha.

3.61.d:
शरणागतं तु सन्त्यज्य यो नरः पुरुषाधमः ॥
बहून्यब्दसहस्राणि नरकं प्रतिपद्यते ॥ 7 ॥
नरकाच्च तथा मुक्तस्तिर्यग्योनिषु जायते ॥
तत्रापि च तथाप्नोति वधबन्धान्यनेकशः ॥ 8 ॥
दैवान्मानुष्यमासाद्य चण्डालत्वमवाप्नुयात् ॥
व्याधिबन्धवधैर्घोरैस्तत्रापि स च युज्यते ॥ 9 ॥
परित्राणं तु यः कुर्याद्भीतस्य शरणैषिणः ॥
स एकः पुरुषो लोके सर्वधर्मभृतां वरः ॥ 3.302.10 ॥
वधभीतस्य यः कुर्यात्परित्राणं नरोत्तमः ॥
शक्रलोकः स्मृतस्तस्य यावदिन्द्राश्चतुर्दश ॥ 11 ॥
तमःप्रवेशभीतस्य परित्राणेन मानवः ॥
ब्रह्मलोकमवाप्नोति नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥ 12 ॥
वधादपि परं पापं चक्षुषा तु वियोजयेत् ॥
पार्थिवेन न तत्कार्यं कदाचिदपि कस्यचित् ॥ ॥ 13 ॥
तमःप्रवेशनं कृत्वा परेषां पुरुषाधमः ॥
अन्धत्वं ध्रुवमाप्नोति यत्रयत्राभिजायते ॥ 14 ॥
3.61.m:
That lowest of men, however, who abandons one who has come for refuge, / goes to hell for many thousands of years.
And released from hell, he is born among animals; / even there he repeatedly meets with slaughter and bondage.
If by chance he attains human birth, he becomes a caṇḍāla; / even there he is afflicted with dread diseases, bonds, and slaughter.
He, however, who affords protection to a frightened seeker of refuge / is the foremost man in the world among all holders of dharma.
That best of men who affords protection to one frightened of slaughter, / for him the world of Śakra is ordained as long as there are fourteen Indras.
By protecting one who is afraid of entering into darkness [of blindness], a man / attains the world of Brahmā; no doubt is to be held in this regard.
To deprive [someone] of eyesight is a greater sin than even slaughter; / that should never be done to anyone by an earthly king.
The lowest of men, having brought about the entry of others into darkness, / definitely attains blindness wherever he is born.

अपि कल्पसहस्राणि तमसा न वियुज्यते ॥
अङ्गच्छेदनभीतस्य कृत्वा त्राणमनिन्दिताः ॥ 15 ॥
रुद्रलोकमवाप्नोति कल्पशेषमिति श्रुतिः ॥
कल्पादिसर्गे भवति ज्ञानयुक्तो नरस्ततः ॥ 16 ॥
कृत्वा बन्धनभीतस्य परित्राणन्नरोत्तमः ॥
सर्वबन्धविनिर्मुक्तो वायुलोके महीयते ॥ 17 ॥
आसेवनाद्धि भीतस्य त्राणं कृत्वा तथा नरः ॥
सर्वदुःखविनिर्मुक्तः साध्यानां लोकमाप्नुयात् ॥ 18 ॥
ताडनाद्यस्तु भीतस्य परित्राणं समाचरेत् ॥
सर्वबन्धविनिर्मुक्तो भृगूणां लोकमश्नुते ॥ 19 ॥
विवासनाच्च भीतस्य त्राणं कृत्वा तथा नरः ॥
स्वर्गलोकमवाप्नोति मानुष्ये स्थानमुत्तमम् ॥ ॥ 3.302.20 ॥
धनापहारभीतस्य त्राणं कृत्वा नरोत्तमः ॥
स्वर्गलोकमवाप्नोति पूजां देवगणात्तथा ॥ 21 ॥
नरः कृतपरित्राणः पुण्यं किञ्चिद्यदाचरेत् ॥
भागी तस्य परित्राता नरः पुण्यस्य कर्मणः ॥ 22 ॥
3.61.m:
Even for thousands of aeons he is not separated from darkness. / Having protected one afraid of mutilation of limbs, O blameless ones,
he attains the world of Rudra for the remainder of the aeon—so states the sacred tradition; / then, at the creation at the beginning of an aeon, that man is endowed with knowledge.
Having protected one who is terrified of bondage, that best of men, / freed from all bonds, is exalted in the world of Vāyu.
Likewise, a man having protected one afraid of enslavement, / freed from all sorrows, attains the world of the Sādhyas.
He who protects one who is afraid of being beaten, / freed from all bonds, enjoys the world of the Bhṛgus.
Likewise, a man having protected one afraid of banishment, / attains heaven and an exalted station in human birth.
Having protected one who is afraid of the theft of wealth, that best of men / attains heaven and worship from the hosts of gods.
Whatever merit a man who has been saved performs, / the man who saved him is a sharer in that meritorious deed.

पशूनाञ्च मृगाणाञ्च पक्षिणाञ्च तथा द्विजाः ॥
तृणद्रुमलतानाञ्च त्राणाद्भवति नाकभाक् ॥ 23 ॥
वधकस्य हस्तगतं पशुं क्रीत्वा नरोत्तमः ॥
नाकलोकमवाप्नोति सुखी सर्वत्र जायते ॥ 24 ॥
यावन्ति पशु रोमाणि तावद्वर्षाणि मानवः ॥
स्वर्गलोकमवाप्नोति यश्च त्राणं करोत्यसौ ॥25॥
अपि कीटपतङ्गस्य त्राणात्सर्वमुपाश्नुते ॥
बहून्यब्दसहस्राणि नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥26॥
चौरग्रस्तं नृपग्रस्तं रिपुग्रस्तं तु मोक्षयेत् ॥
व्यालग्रस्तं तथा विप्राः सोऽश्वमेधफलं लभेत्॥27॥
विषमे तु तथा दुर्गे सलिले वा हुताशने॥
निमग्नं यः परित्रायेत्सोऽश्वमेधफलं लभेत्॥28॥
व्याधितस्यौषधं दत्त्वा प्राणदानफलं लभेत्॥
रोगार्तं परिचर्याथ प्राणदानफलं लभेत् ॥ 29 ॥
उपचारं तथा कृत्वा भिषङ् मूल्यं विना द्विजाः ॥
प्राणदानफलं तस्य नाकलोके महीयते॥3.302.30॥
3.61.m:
And by protecting domestic animals, wild beasts, and birds, O twice-born, / as well as grass, trees, and creepers, one becomes an enjoyer of heaven.
Having purchased an animal fallen into the hand of a slaughterer, that best of men / attains the world of heaven and is born happy everywhere.
For as many hairs as the animal has, for that many years / the man who protects it attains the world of heaven.
Even from saving an insect or a moth one attains everything / for many thousands of years; no doubt is to be held in this regard.
One should free [a person] seized by thieves, seized by a king, or seized by an enemy; / likewise, O priests, [one who frees someone] seized by a beast of prey attains the fruit of an aśvamedha.
He who saves one immersed in rough terrain, in a pit, / in water, or in fire attains the fruit of an aśvamedha.
By giving medicine to a sick person, one attains the fruit of the gift of life; / by caring for one afflicted with illness, one attains the fruit of the gift of life.
Likewise, a physician who renders treatment without taking a fee, O twice-born, / has the fruit of the gift of life and is exalted in the heavenly world.

3.303
॥ हंस उवाच ॥
विद्या कामदुघा धेनुर्विद्या चक्षुरनुत्त्मम् ॥
विद्यादानात्परं दानं न भूतं न भविष्यति ॥ 1 ॥
विद्यावान्सर्वकामानां भाजनं पुरुषो भवेत् ॥
तस्माद्विद्यां हि ददता सर्वं दत्तं भवेदिह ॥ 2 ॥
पराध्यापनतः क्लेशं पुरुषस्तु यदश्नुते ॥
तपस्तत्परमं तस्य ब्रह्मलोकं परं स्मृतम् ॥ 3 ॥
दानानामुत्तमं लोके तपसा च तथोत्तमम् ॥
विद्यादानं महाभागाः सर्वकामफलप्रदम् ॥ 4 ॥
वेददानादवाप्नोति सर्वयज्ञफलं नरः ॥
उपवेदप्रदानेन गन्धर्वैः सह मोदते ॥ 5 ॥
वेदाङ्गानां च दानेन शक्रलोकमवाप्नुयात् ॥
धर्मशास्त्रप्रदानेन धर्मेण सह मोदते ॥ 6 ॥
3.61.m:
Those men who are slain while being protected, [and yet] without fear, go to the world of the lord of the thirty [gods]; / even today those heroes among men do not fall, nor at any time is there a fall for them.
3.303
Haṃsa said: / Knowledge is a wish-yielding cow; knowledge is the unsurpassed eye. / There has not been nor will there be a gift superior to the gift of knowledge.
A man possessed of knowledge becomes a vessel for all desires; / therefore, by one who gives knowledge, indeed, everything is given here.
Whatever hardship a man undergoes from teaching others, / that is his supreme asceticism, and the world of Brahmā is remembered as his supreme [reward].
The gift of knowledge is the highest of gifts in the world, and likewise the highest of austerities, / O fortunate ones, granting the fruit of all desires.
From giving the Veda, a man obtains the fruit of all sacrifices; / by granting an Upaveda, he rejoices together with the Gandharvas.
And by the gift of the auxiliary sciences of the Veda, he would attain the world of Śakra; / by granting the treatises on dharma, he rejoices with Dharma.

3.61.d:
सिद्धान्तानां प्रदानेन मोक्षमाप्नोत्यसंशयम् ॥
शास्त्राणि दत्त्वा चान्यानि नरो नाके महीयते ॥ 7 ॥
विद्यादानादवाप्नोति प्रदानात्पुस्तकस्य च ॥
शिल्पानि शिक्षयेद्यस्तु पौण्डरीकफलं लभेत् ॥ 8 ॥
शिक्षयित्वा धनुर्वेदमश्वमेधफलं लभेत् ॥
शिल्पभाण्डप्रदानेन शिल्पदानफलं लभेत् ॥9 ॥
अहितेषु प्रवृत्तस्य तथा कृत्वा निवारणम् ॥
विद्यादानफलं प्रोक्तं नात्र कार्या विचारणा॥3.303.10॥
पापप्रवृत्तस्य तथा नरः कृत्वा निवारणम् ॥
विद्यादानफलं प्राप्य स्वर्गलोके महीयते ॥ 11 ॥
शिक्षयेत्पुरुषः कर्म कर्मणा येन जीवति ॥
शिक्षयित्वा महाभागाः स्वर्गलोके महीयते ॥ 12 ॥
येन जीवति भाण्डेन तस्य भाण्डस्य दायकः ॥
सर्वकामसमृद्धस्य यज्ञस्य फलमश्नुते ॥ 13॥
अन्तर्वन्तीह दानानि सर्वाण्येव द्विजोत्तमाः ॥
एकं महाफलं ज्ञेयं विद्यादानमनन्तकम् ॥ 14 ॥
3.61.m:
By granting philosophical doctrines, he undoubtedly attains liberation; / and having given other treatises, a man is glorified in heaven.
[Such fruits] he obtains from the gift of knowledge and from granting a manuscript. / But one who teaches crafts would obtain the fruit of a Pauṇḍarīka sacrifice.
Having taught archery, he would obtain the fruit of an Aśvamedha sacrifice; / by granting tools for crafts, he would obtain the fruit of giving a craft.
Likewise, having restrained someone engaged in harmful deeds, / that is declared to be the fruit of the gift of knowledge; no doubt should be entertained here.
Likewise, having restrained someone engaged in sin, / a man, having obtained the fruit of the gift of knowledge, is glorified in the world of heaven.
A man should teach an occupation by which work [another] may live; / having taught it, O fortunate ones, he is glorified in the world of heaven.
The giver of the tools by which tools [another] lives / enjoys the fruit of a sacrifice complete with all desires.
All gifts in this world have an end, O foremost of twice-born; / one should know that the gift of knowledge alone yields great fruit and is endless.

3.61.s:
vidyāṃ yatheṣṭāṃ puruṣasya dattvā mantraṃ śubhaṃ vāpyatha vāpi śilpam ..
śilpasya bhāṇḍaṃ yadi vā dvijendrāḥ prāpnoti lokaṃ manasā tvabhīṣṭam..15..
3.304
haṃsa uvāca ..
brahmadeyāṃ tu yaḥ kanyāṃ puruṣasya prayacchati ..
saptātītānbhaviṣyām̐śca svakule sapta mānavān ..1..
tena kanyāpradānena tārayiṣyatyasaṃśayam ..
lokamāpnoti ca tathā dakṣasyeha prajāpateḥ .. 2 ..
dattvā daivena vidhinā kulaṃ tripuruṣaṃ naraḥ ..
samuddharati durgebhyo dakṣalokaṃ ca gacchati ..3 ..
prājāpatyena vidhinā dattvātmānaṃ samuddharet ..
mahatpuṇyamavāpnoti svargalokaṃ ca gacchati .. 4 ..
bhūkarīndrāśvadānāni godānañca tathaiva ca ..
antarbhavanti vai yasminkiṃ dānamadhikaṃ tataḥ .. 5 ..
dattvā tāṃ varṇahīnāya ghore tamasi majjati ..
bahūnyabdasahasrāṇi tathaivāśucibhuṅnaraḥ..6..
3.61.d:
विद्यां यथेष्टां पुरुषस्य दत्त्वा मन्त्रं शुभं वाप्यथ वापि शिल्पम् ॥
शिल्पस्य भाण्डं यदि वा द्विजेन्द्राः प्राप्नोति लोकं मनसा त्वभीष्टम्॥15॥
3.304
हंस उवाच ॥
ब्रह्मदेयां तु यः कन्यां पुरुषस्य प्रयच्छति ॥
सप्तातीतान्भविष्याम्̐श्च स्वकुले सप्त मानवान् ॥1॥
तेन कन्याप्रदानेन तारयिष्यत्यसंशयम् ॥
लोकमाप्नोति च तथा दक्षस्येह प्रजापतेः ॥ 2 ॥
दत्त्वा दैवेन विधिना कुलं त्रिपुरुषं नरः ॥
समुद्धरति दुर्गेभ्यो दक्षलोकं च गच्छति ॥3 ॥
प्राजापत्येन विधिना दत्त्वात्मानं समुद्धरेत् ॥
महत्पुण्यमवाप्नोति स्वर्गलोकं च गच्छति ॥ 4 ॥
भूकरीन्द्राश्वदानानि गोदानञ्च तथैव च ॥
अन्तर्भवन्ति वै यस्मिन्किं दानमधिकं ततः ॥ 5 ॥
दत्त्वा तां वर्णहीनाय घोरे तमसि मज्जति ॥
बहून्यब्दसहस्राणि तथैवाशुचिभुङ्नरः॥6॥
3.61.m:
Having given to a man knowledge according to his desire, or an auspicious mantra, or indeed a craft, / or tools for a craft, O lords of the twice-born, he attains the world desired in his mind.
3.304
Haṃsa said:
One who gives away a maiden in the Brahma marriage to a man, / seven past and seven future men in his own family
he will undoubtedly deliver by that gift of a maiden; / and likewise he attains the world of Dakṣa Prajāpati here.
Having given [her] according to the Daiva rite, a man delivers / three generations of his family from perils, and goes to the world of Dakṣa.
Having given [her] according to the Prājāpatya rite, he would deliver himself; / he obtains great religious merit and goes to the world of heaven.
Since gifts of land, lordly elephants, and horses, and likewise the gift of cattle / are contained within [this gift], what gift could be greater than it?
Having given her to one of lower caste, he sinks into terrible darkness / for many thousands of years, eating impure things.

3.61.s:
samavarṇāya yo dadyātsa tūktaphalabhāgbhaveta ..
dattvā cādhikavarṇāya dviguṇāṃ triguṇāṃ tathā .. 7 ..
dvijaputramanāthaṃ yaḥ saṃskuryādyaśca karmabhiḥ ..
cūḍopanayanādyaiśca so'śvamedhaphalaṃ labhet .. 8 ..
anāthāṃ kanyakāṃ dattvā sadṛśe vādhike vare ..
dviguṇaṃ phalamāpnoti kanyādāne yadīritam .. 9..
vivāhe samanuprāpte kṛtvaupakaraṇāni ca ..
nākalokamavāpnoti karmasvanyeṣvapi dvijāḥ .. 3.304.10 ..
vastraṃ patramalaṅkāraṃ vivāhārthaṃ prayacchati ..
mahatphalamavāpnoti nākaloke mahīyate .. 11 ..
kanyayā saha yaddattaṃ draviṇaṃ vahnimūlake ..
saphalāddviguṇaṃ tasya phalamuktaṃ purātanaiḥ .. 12 ..
kanyādānādavāpnoti dakṣalokaṃ narottamaḥ ..
viṣṇupūjāsamaṃ puṇyaṃ tatpatyuḥ pūjayā bhavet .. 13 ..
3.61.d:
समवर्णाय यो दद्यात्स तूक्तफलभाग्भवेत ॥
दत्त्वा चाधिकवर्णाय द्विगुणां त्रिगुणां तथा ॥ 7 ॥
द्विजपुत्रमनाथं यः संस्कुर्याद्यश्च कर्मभिः ॥
चूडोपनयनाद्यैश्च सोऽश्वमेधफलं लभेत् ॥ 8 ॥
अनाथां कन्यकां दत्त्वा सदृशे वाधिके वरे ॥
द्विगुणं फलमाप्नोति कन्यादाने यदीरितम् ॥ 9॥
विवाहे समनुप्राप्ते कृत्वौपकरणानि च ॥
नाकलोकमवाप्नोति कर्मस्वन्येष्वपि द्विजाः ॥ 3.304.10 ॥
वस्त्रं पत्रमलङ्कारं विवाहार्थं प्रयच्छति ॥
महत्फलमवाप्नोति नाकलोके महीयते ॥ 11 ॥
कन्यया सह यद्दत्तं द्रविणं वह्निमूलके ॥
सफलाद्द्विगुणं तस्य फलमुक्तं पुरातनैः ॥ 12 ॥
कन्यादानादवाप्नोति दक्षलोकं नरोत्तमः ॥
विष्णुपूजासमं पुण्यं तत्पत्युः पूजया भवेत् ॥ 13 ॥
3.61.m:
One who gives [her] to an equal in caste shares the declared fruit; / and having given [her] to one of higher caste, twice or thrice [that fruit].
One who performs the sacraments for a destitute twice-born boy with rituals / such as tonsure and the sacred thread initiation would obtain the fruit of an Aśvamedha sacrifice.
Having given a destitute maiden to an equal or superior groom, / he obtains twice the fruit that has been proclaimed for the gift of a maiden.
When a marriage has arrived, having provided the preparations, / as well as in other ceremonies, O twice-born, he attains the heavenly world.
[If] he gives clothing, a document, or ornament for the sake of a marriage, / he obtains great fruit and is glorified in the heavenly world.
Whatever wealth is given with the maiden at the foot of the fire, / its fruit is declared by the ancients to be twice the ordinary fruit.
From the gift of a maiden, the best of men attains the world of Dakṣa; / merit equal to the worship of Viṣṇu arises from honoring her husband.

3.61.s:
vimānamāruhya manobhirāmaṃ surāṅganāgītavilāsahṛdyam ..
prāpnoti lokāṃstridaśottamānāṃ kanyāprado nātra vicāraṇāsti ..14 ..
3.305
haṃsa uvāca ..
bhūmirdhātrī vidhātrī ca bhūmau sarvaṃ pratiṣṭhitam ..
bhūmirhi mātā sarvasya sarvakāmapradā varā .. 1 ..
tadudbhūtena haviṣā tṛptimāyānti devatāḥ ..
bhūmirhi dhāraṇī viprāstrailokyasya nigadyate .. 2 ..
bhūmau hi sarvaṃ bhavati bhūmau sarvaṃ pratiṣṭhitam ..
sarvakāmapradaṃ jñeyaṃ bhūmidānaṃ narottama .. 3 ..
hastamātrāṃ tu yo dadyādbhuvaṃ puruṣasattama ..
tenaiva dhruvamāpnoti bhūmidānaphalaṃ naraḥ .. 4 ..
yadutpannamathāśnāti naraḥ saṃvatsaraṃ dvijāḥ ..
ekaṃ gocarmamātraṃ tu bhuvaḥ proktaṃ vicakṣaṇaiḥ .. 5 ..
brāhmaṇāya tato dattvā vasūnāṃ lokamāpnuyāt ..
śākabhūmiṃ tato dattvā lokamāṅgirasaṃ vrajet .. 6 ..
3.61.d:
विमानमारुह्य मनोभिरामं सुराङ्गनागीतविलासहृद्यम् ॥
प्राप्नोति लोकांस्त्रिदशोत्तमानां कन्याप्रदो नात्र विचारणास्ति ॥14 ॥
3.305
हंस उवाच ॥
भूमिर्धात्री विधात्री च भूमौ सर्वं प्रतिष्ठितम् ॥
भूमिर्हि माता सर्वस्य सर्वकामप्रदा वरा ॥ 1 ॥
तदुद्भूतेन हविषा तृप्तिमायान्ति देवताः ॥
भूमिर्हि धारणी विप्रास्त्रैलोक्यस्य निगद्यते ॥ 2 ॥
भूमौ हि सर्वं भवति भूमौ सर्वं प्रतिष्ठितम् ॥
सर्वकामप्रदं ज्ञेयं भूमिदानं नरोत्तम ॥ 3 ॥
हस्तमात्रां तु यो दद्याद्भुवं पुरुषसत्तम ॥
तेनैव ध्रुवमाप्नोति भूमिदानफलं नरः ॥ 4 ॥
यदुत्पन्नमथाश्नाति नरः संवत्सरं द्विजाः ॥
एकं गोचर्ममात्रं तु भुवः प्रोक्तं विचक्षणैः ॥ 5 ॥
ब्राह्मणाय ततो दत्त्वा वसूनां लोकमाप्नुयात् ॥
शाकभूमिं ततो दत्त्वा लोकमाङ्गिरसं व्रजेत् ॥ 6 ॥
3.61.m:
Ascending an aerial chariot charming to the mind, delightful with the song and play of celestial women, / the giver of a maiden attains the worlds of the foremost of the gods; there is no doubt in this.
3.305
Haṃsa said:
The earth is the supporter and the creator, and upon the earth everything is established; / the earth is indeed the mother of all, the excellent granter of all desires.
With the oblation produced from it, the deities attain satisfaction; / for the earth, O brahmins, is declared to be the maintainer of the three worlds.
For everything comes into being upon the earth, upon the earth everything is established; / the gift of land should be known as granting all desires, O best of men.
Even one who gives land merely measuring a cubit, O best of men, / by that alone a man surely attains the fruit of the gift of land.
[The land] whose produce a man consumes for a year, O twice-born, / is declared by the wise to be equal to one hide of land.
Having then given [it] to a brahmin, he would attain the world of the Vasus; / having then given vegetable land, he would go to the world of Āṅgirasa.

3.61.s:
ārāmabhūmiṃ dattvā ca mārutaṃ lokamaśnute ..
jalāśayārthaṃ yo dadyādvāruṇaṃ lokamāpnuyāt .. 7 ..
yasya dattvā tu veśmārthaṃ tasya devasya so'śnute ..
yastatra vidyate nityaṃ loko dvijavarā dhruvam .. 8 ..
udyānabhūmiṃ dattvā ca gandharvaiḥ saha modate ..
ratnākaraṃ tu vai dattvā śakraloke mahīyate ..9..
dattvā kanakabhūmiṃ ca vahniloke mahīyate ..
anyeṣāmākarabhuvaṃ lohānāṃ yaḥ prayacchati .. 3.305.10 ..
tasyāpi matiruddiṣṭā loke hautāśane dvijāḥ ..
dhānyākarabhuvaṃ dattvā nākaloke mahīyate .. 11 ..
añjanākarabhūmiṃ tu yaḥ prayacchati vai dvijāḥ ..
pitṛbhiryamalokasthaḥ pūjyate'sau narottamaḥ .. 12 ..
lavaṇākarabhūmiṃ ca somaloke mahīyate ..
śimbisasyaprarohāṃ tu bhuvaṃ dattvā narottamaḥ .. 13 ..
sādhyānāṃ lokamāpnoti nātra kāryā vicāraṇā ..
indhanākarabhūmiṃ tu nāsatyaiḥ sahitastathā..14..
3.61.d:
आरामभूमिं दत्त्वा च मारुतं लोकमश्नुते ॥
जलाशयार्थं यो दद्याद्वारुणं लोकमाप्नुयात् ॥ 7 ॥
यस्य दत्त्वा तु वेश्मार्थं तस्य देवस्य सोऽश्नुते ॥
यस्तत्र विद्यते नित्यं लोको द्विजवरा ध्रुवम् ॥ 8 ॥
उद्यानभूमिं दत्त्वा च गन्धर्वैः सह मोदते ॥
रत्नाकरं तु वै दत्त्वा शक्रलोके महीयते ॥9॥
दत्त्वा कनकभूमिं च वह्निलोके महीयते ॥
अन्येषामाकरभुवं लोहानां यः प्रयच्छति ॥ 3.305.10 ॥
तस्यापि मतिरुद्दिष्टा लोके हौताशने द्विजाः ॥
धान्याकरभुवं दत्त्वा नाकलोके महीयते ॥ 11 ॥
अञ्जनाकरभूमिं तु यः प्रयच्छति वै द्विजाः ॥
पितृभिर्यमलोकस्थः पूज्यतेऽसौ नरोत्तमः ॥ 12 ॥
लवणाकरभूमिं च सोमलोके महीयते ॥
शिम्बिसस्यप्ररोहां तु भुवं दत्त्वा नरोत्तमः ॥ 13 ॥
साध्यानां लोकमाप्नोति नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥
इन्धनाकरभूमिं तु नासत्यैः सहितस्तथा॥14॥
3.61.m:
And having given orchard land, he enjoys the world of the Maruts; / one who gives [land] for a reservoir would attain the world of Varuṇa.
For whichever god's residence he gives [land], he enjoys [that realm] / which belongs to that deity, being an eternal world, O best of twice-born, surely.
And having given garden land, he rejoices with the Gandharvas; / but having given a mine of jewels, he is glorified in the world of Śakra.
And having given gold-bearing land, he is glorified in the world of Fire. / One who grants land with mines of other metals,
his destination also is declared to be in the world of Fire, O twice-born; / having given land rich in grain, he is glorified in the heavenly world.
One who grants land containing an antimony mine, O twice-born, / that best of men, residing in the world of Yama, is honored by the ancestors.
And [by giving] land with a salt mine, he is glorified in the world of Soma. / But having given land growing leguminous crops, the best of men
attains the world of the Sādhyas; no doubt should be entertained here. / And [by giving] land yielding firewood, [he rejoices] with the Nāsatyas.

3.61.s:
śūkadhānyabhuvaṃ dattvā rudraloke mahīyate ..
kedāra bhūmiṃ dharmajñā yaḥ prayacchati dharmataḥ .. 15 ..
sa mahatpuṇyamāpnoti brahmalokaṃ ca gacchati ..
ikṣubhūmiṃ naro dattvā drākṣābhūmimathāpi ca .. 16 ..
somalokamavāpnoti sarvakāmām̐śca vindati ..
soparā taskarākīrṇā tathā vyāḍavatī ca bhūḥ..17.
na dātavyā dvijaśreṣṭhā yā ca sandhiṣu vai dvijāḥ ..
gulmapuṣpapradāṃ yastu latāṃ vā saṃprayacchati..18..
vimāne nandane so'tha krīḍatyapsarasāṃ gaṇaiḥ..
puṣpadaṃ phaladaṃ vṛkṣaṃ dattvā viprāya bhaktitaḥ..19..
svargalokaparibhraṣṭo nagarādhipatirbhavet..
brāhmaṇāya gṛhaṃ dattvā vasūnāṃ lokamaśnute..3.305.20..
ārāmamatha sodyānaṃ nandane krīḍate vane..
dhanadhānyayutaṃ sphītaṃ gṛhopakaraṇairyutam..21..
3.61.d:
शूकधान्यभुवं दत्त्वा रुद्रलोके महीयते ॥
केदार भूमिं धर्मज्ञा यः प्रयच्छति धर्मतः ॥ 15 ॥
स महत्पुण्यमाप्नोति ब्रह्मलोकं च गच्छति ॥
इक्षुभूमिं नरो दत्त्वा द्राक्षाभूमिमथापि च ॥ 16 ॥
सोमलोकमवाप्नोति सर्वकामाम्̐श्च विन्दति ॥
सोपरा तस्कराकीर्णा तथा व्याडवती च भूः॥17.
न दातव्या द्विजश्रेष्ठा या च सन्धिषु वै द्विजाः ॥
गुल्मपुष्पप्रदां यस्तु लतां वा संप्रयच्छति॥18॥
विमाने नन्दने सोऽथ क्रीडत्यप्सरसां गणैः॥
पुष्पदं फलदं वृक्षं दत्त्वा विप्राय भक्तितः॥19॥
स्वर्गलोकपरिभ्रष्टो नगराधिपतिर्भवेत्॥
ब्राह्मणाय गृहं दत्त्वा वसूनां लोकमश्नुते॥3.305.20॥
आराममथ सोद्यानं नन्दने क्रीडते वने॥
धनधान्ययुतं स्फीतं गृहोपकरणैर्युतम्॥21॥
3.61.m:
Having given land for awned grain, he is glorified in the world of Rudra. / One who, knowing dharma, gives cultivated field land according to dharma,
he attains great merit and goes to the world of Brahmā. / Giving land [yielding] sugarcane, or indeed land [yielding] grapes, a man
attains the world of Soma and obtains all desires. / Land that is alkaline, infested with thieves, or overrun by beasts,
or situated on borders, O best of the twice-born, should not be given, O twice-born. / But he who gives a clump [of plants] bearing flowers, or a creeper,
sports in an aerial chariot in the Nandana [grove] with hosts of apsarases. / Having given with devotion to a brahmin a tree that yields flowers and fruit,
upon descending from heaven he becomes the lord of a city. / Having given a house to a brahmin, he enjoys the world of the Vasus.
Having [given] a grove together with a garden, he sports in the Nandana forest. / Having given a flourishing [house] endowed with wealth and grain, furnished with domestic utensils,

3.61.s:
śayyāsanayutaṃ ramyaṃ gojāśvāviyutaṃ tathā..
gṛhaṃ dattvā dvijendrāya tāvatsvargamupāśnute ..22..
yāvatkalpāvasāne tu kalpādau pārthivo bhavet..
grāmapradaḥ syānnṛpatistathā hyaśanado nṛpaḥ .. 23 ..
samagravasudheśaḥ syāccakravartī ca rājyadaḥ ..
svadattāṃ paradattāṃ vā na hareta vasundharām .. 24 ..
bhūmeraṅgulamātraṃ tu hṛtvā narakamṛcchati ..
bahūnyabdasahasrāṇi dharme'pi puruṣo rataḥ .. 25 ..
viṣṭhākṛmitvamāpnoti pitṛbhiḥ sahitastathā ..

svarāṣṭre pararāṣṭre vā devabrāhmaṇasātkṛtam .. 28 ..
3.61.d:
शय्यासनयुतं रम्यं गोजाश्वावियुतं तथा॥
गृहं दत्त्वा द्विजेन्द्राय तावत्स्वर्गमुपाश्नुते ॥22॥
यावत्कल्पावसाने तु कल्पादौ पार्थिवो भवेत्॥
ग्रामप्रदः स्यान्नृपतिस्तथा ह्यशनदो नृपः ॥ 23 ॥
समग्रवसुधेशः स्याच्चक्रवर्ती च राज्यदः ॥
स्वदत्तां परदत्तां वा न हरेत वसुन्धराम् ॥ 24 ॥
भूमेरङ्गुलमात्रं तु हृत्वा नरकमृच्छति ॥
बहून्यब्दसहस्राणि धर्मेऽपि पुरुषो रतः ॥ 25 ॥
विष्ठाकृमित्वमाप्नोति पितृभिः सहितस्तथा ॥
तस्माद्भूमिं न हिंसेत दद्यादेव विचक्षणः ॥ 26 ॥
भूमिदानात्परं दानं नान्यल्लोकेषु विद्यते ॥
भूमिं युद्धजितां दद्याद्ब्राह्मणेषु महीपतिः ॥ 27 ॥
परं राष्ट्रं समासाद्य प्राग्दत्तं नैव हिंसयेत् ॥
स्वराष्ट्रे परराष्ट्रे वा देवब्राह्मणसात्कृतम् ॥ 28 ॥
3.61.m:
endowed with beds and seats, pleasant, and likewise furnished with cows, goats, horses, and sheep / to an eminent twice-born, he enjoys heaven for that long,
as long as until the end of the aeon, and at the beginning of the [next] aeon he becomes an earthly ruler. / A giver of a village becomes a king, and likewise a giver of food [becomes] a king;
a giver of a kingdom becomes the lord of the whole earth and a universal monarch. / One must not seize land given by oneself or given by another.
Stealing even a finger-breadth of land, a man goes to hell / for many thousands of years, even if devoted to dharma.
He becomes a worm in feces, together with his ancestors. / Therefore a wise man must never violate land; he should only give [it].
There is no other gift in the worlds superior to the gift of land. / An earthly ruler should give land conquered in battle to brahmins.
Having obtained an enemy's realm, he must never destroy what was previously given. / Land deeded to gods and brahmins, whether in one's own realm or an enemy's,

3.61.s:
ciraṃ narakamāpnoti hṛtvā bhūmipatirbhuvam ..
dattā na hiṃsanīyā syādripuṇāpi vasundharā .. 29 ..

3.61.d:
चिरं नरकमाप्नोति हृत्वा भूमिपतिर्भुवम् ॥
दत्ता न हिंसनीया स्याद्रिपुणापि वसुन्धरा ॥ 29 ॥
भूमिहर्ता परं दुःखं प्रेत्य चेह तथाश्नुते ॥
भूमिं क्रीत्वा तु यः कुर्याद्देवब्राह्मणसान्नरः ॥ 3.305.30 ॥
स्वर्गलोकमवाप्नोति पुरुषोऽपि सुदारुणः ॥
षष्टिवर्षसहस्राणि स्वर्गे वसति भूमिदः ॥ 31 ॥
आच्छेत्ता चानुमन्ता च तावन्ति नरके वसेत् ॥
पक्वसस्यां वसुमतीं योऽलङ्कृत्य प्रयच्छति ॥ 32 ॥
कामगेन विमानेन ब्रह्मलोकं स गच्छति ॥
यथा भवति विप्रेन्द्राः फलं भूमौ पुनःपुनः ॥ 33 ॥
तथा भूमिकृतं दानं सस्यैरिव विवर्धते ॥
यस्तु राजा द्विजातिभ्यः सम्यग्भूमिं प्रयच्छति ॥
पुनस्तु जननं प्राप्य राजैव भुवि जायते ॥ 34 ॥
शस्त्रं भद्रासनं वस्त्रं नराश्ववरवारणाः ॥
भूमिदानस्य पुष्पाणि फलं स्वर्गः प्रकीर्तितः ॥ 35॥
3.61.m:
having seized it, an earthly ruler goes to hell for a long time. / Land that has been given must not be violated even by an enemy.
The thief of land experiences supreme sorrow both in the hereafter and here. / But a man who purchases land and assigns it to gods and brahmins,
even a very cruel person, attains the world of heaven. / The giver of land resides in heaven for sixty thousand years;
the one who takes it away and the one who assents reside in hell for as many. / He who, having adorned it, gives earth bearing ripe crops,
goes to the world of Brahmā in an aerial chariot that moves at will. / Just as fruit arises on the earth again and again, O eminent brahmins,
so a gift made of land increases like crops. / But the king who properly gives land to the twice-born / is born again on earth only as a king, having obtained rebirth.
Weapons, a royal throne, garments, men, horses, and excellent elephants / are the flowers of the gift of land; its fruit is proclaimed to be heaven.

3.61.s:
saṃgrāme ye hatāḥ śūrāstathā ye yajñayājinaḥ ..
vaneṣu ye mṛtāste ca nātikrāmanti bhūmidam .. 36 ..
nāsti viṣṇusamastrātā nāsti gaṅgāsamā nadī .. 37..
homamantrastathā nāsti mahāvyāhṛtibhiḥ samaḥ ..
gāyatrīsadṛśo japyo yathā nāsti dvijottamāḥ..38..

vidhirmānasamo nāsti tapo nānaśanātparam ..39..
gururmātṛsamo nāsti nāsti bhāryāsamaḥ sakhā ..
nīcāvamānanādduḥkhādduḥkhaṃ nāsti yathā param .. 3.305.40 ..
yathā ca nāsti lokeṣu sukhaṃ śatrujayādhikam..

bhūmidānātparaṃ nāsti vimānaiḥ kāmagairiha .. 42 ..
devastrīnṛtyabahule vīṇāmurajanādite ..
kiṃkiṇījālanirghoṣe manorathaphaladrume ..43..
3.61.d:
संग्रामे ये हताः शूरास्तथा ये यज्ञयाजिनः ॥
वनेषु ये मृतास्ते च नातिक्रामन्ति भूमिदम् ॥ 36 ॥
नास्ति विष्णुसमस्त्राता नास्ति गङ्गासमा नदी ॥ 37॥
होममन्त्रस्तथा नास्ति महाव्याहृतिभिः समः ॥
गायत्रीसदृशो जप्यो यथा नास्ति द्विजोत्तमाः॥38॥
अन्तर्जले तथा नास्ति मन्त्रोऽन्योऽप्यघमर्षणात् ॥
विधिर्मानसमो नास्ति तपो नानशनात्परम् ॥39॥
गुरुर्मातृसमो नास्ति नास्ति भार्यासमः सखा ॥
नीचावमाननाद्दुःखाद्दुःखं नास्ति यथा परम् ॥ 3.305.40 ॥
यथा च नास्ति लोकेषु सुखं शत्रुजयाधिकम्॥
चक्षुर्ज्ञानसमं नास्ति सुहृद्धर्मसमस्तथा ॥ 41 ॥
भूमिदानात्परं दानं तथा नास्ति द्विजोत्तमाः ॥
भूमिदानात्परं नास्ति विमानैः कामगैरिह ॥ 42 ॥
देवस्त्रीनृत्यबहुले वीणामुरजनादिते ॥
किंकिणीजालनिर्घोषे मनोरथफलद्रुमे ॥43॥
3.61.m:
Those heroes who were slain in battle, and those who performed sacrifices, / and those who died in forests do not surpass the giver of land.
There is no protector equal to Viṣṇu; there is no river equal to the Gaṅgā.
There is likewise no oblation mantra equal to the Great Utterances. / Just as there is no muttered prayer like the Gāyatrī, O best of the twice-born,
and there is no other mantra within water [equal to] the Aghamarṣaṇa, / no rite equal to a mental one, and no austerity higher than fasting;
there is no guru equal to a mother, no companion equal to a wife, / and just as there is no sorrow higher than the sorrow of dishonor by the vile,
and just as there is no happiness in the worlds greater than victory over an enemy, / no eye equal to knowledge, and likewise no friend equal to dharma,
so there is no gift higher than the gift of land, O best of the twice-born. / There is nothing superior to the gift of land by means of aerial chariots moving at will here,
abounding in the dances of divine women, echoing with lutes and drums, / ringing with strings of tinkling bells, with trees yielding desires as fruit.

3.61.s:
mukhyābhirdevarāmābhirvījyamānāstu cāmaraiḥ..

svarge bhuktvā yadā yānti mānuṣyaṃ kālaparyayāt ..

3.61.d:
मुख्याभिर्देवरामाभिर्वीज्यमानास्तु चामरैः॥
संगीयमाना गन्धर्वैः स्तूयमानास्तथैव च ॥44॥
बहून्यब्दसहस्राणि देवभोगांस्तु ते नराः ॥
स्वर्गे भुक्त्वा यदा यान्ति मानुष्यं कालपर्ययात् ॥
भवन्ति सर्वभोगाढ्याः सर्वदुःखविवर्जिताः॥45॥
3.61.m:
Being fanned with chowries by foremost celestial women, / sung to by gandharvas and praised likewise,
those men, having enjoyed divine pleasures in heaven for many thousands of years, / when they enter human existence by the turning of time, / become rich in all pleasures and free from all sorrow,

3.61.s:
vikhyātaśabdāśca janābhirāmāḥ prataptacāmīkarabhūṣitāṅgāḥ ..
sugandhigandhaiśca tathānuliptā bhavanti loke ca sukhairupetāḥ ..46..
3.61.d:
विख्यातशब्दाश्च जनाभिरामाः प्रतप्तचामीकरभूषिताङ्गाः ॥
सुगन्धिगन्धैश्च तथानुलिप्ता भवन्ति लोके च सुखैरुपेताः ॥46॥
3.61.m: of renowned renown, pleasing to the people, their limbs adorned with refined gold, / anointed with sweet-smelling scents, and endowed with joys in the world.

3.62.m:
3.306
Haṃsa said:
Cows are pure and auspicious; the worlds are established in cows. / Dependent on them are sacrifices, the worship of deities and guests,

3.62.s:
balantuṣṭiśca puṣṭiśca tathā śrāddhakriyā dvijāḥ..
nāsau sampannamaśnāti yasya dhenurna vidyate....
tasmātsarvapradānānāṃ gavāṃ dānamanuttamam ..
hīnāṅgīṃ kṣīrapāṃ vṛddhāṃ dugdhadohāṃ nirindriyām..3..

बलन्तुष्टिश्च पुष्टिश्च तथा श्राद्धक्रिया द्विजाः॥
नासौ सम्पन्नमश्नाति यस्य धेनुर्न विद्यते॥॥
तस्मात्सर्वप्रदानानां गवां दानमनुत्तमम् ॥
हीनाङ्गीं क्षीरपां वृद्धां दुग्धदोहां निरिन्द्रियाम्॥3॥
3.62.m: strength, contentment, nourishment, and likewise śrāddha rites, O twice-born. / He who has no milch cow does not eat what is prosperous. / Therefore, of all gifts, the gift of cows is unsurpassed. / [A cow] defective in limbs, drinking her own milk, old, dry of milk, bereft of sense organs,

3.62.s:
vyādhitāṃ viṣamāṃ vyālāṃ tathaiva prapalāyinīm ..
mūlyaistathāpyasaṃśuddhairhṛtāśca dvijapuṅgavāt..4..

व्याधितां विषमां व्यालां तथैव प्रपलायिनीम् ॥
मूल्यैस्तथाप्यसंशुद्धैर्हृताश्च द्विजपुङ्गवात्॥4॥
3.62.m: diseased, treacherous, vicious, or likewise given to fleeing, / or obtained from an eminent twice-born by impure purchase-prices,

3.62.s:
na dātavyā smṛtā dhenurdattvā narakamāpnuyāt ..
brāhmaṇo yastu kurute gorasānāṃ tu vikrayam..5..

न दातव्या स्मृता धेनुर्दत्त्वा नरकमाप्नुयात् ॥
ब्राह्मणो यस्तु कुरुते गोरसानां तु विक्रयम्॥5॥
3.62.m: such a cow is handed down as not to be given; having given her, one would attain hell. / A brahmin who carries out the sale of milk products,

3.62.s:
gavāṃ ca vikrayaṃ viprā viṣamo yastathā gavām..
apātradoṣayuktaśca na deyā tasya cāpyatha..6..

गवां च विक्रयं विप्रा विषमो यस्तथा गवाम्॥
अपात्रदोषयुक्तश्च न देया तस्य चाप्यथ॥6॥
3.62.m: and the sale of cows, O brahmins, or who is harsh toward cows, / and is contaminated by the fault of being an unworthy recipient, to him also [a cow] must not be given.

3.62.s:
naikā bahūnāṃ dātavyā na dvayordvijapuṅgavāḥ..
sā tu vikrayamāpannā dāturnarakadāyinī..7..

नैका बहूनां दातव्या न द्वयोर्द्विजपुङ्गवाः॥
सा तु विक्रयमापन्ना दातुर्नरकदायिनी॥7॥
3.62.m: One must not be given to many, nor to two, O eminent twice-born; / for she, being brought to sale, brings hell to the giver.

3.62.s:
ekaṃ pātramathāsādya deyāstu bahavaḥ smṛtāḥ ..
gavāṃ pradāne yatnena parīkṣyo brāhmaṇo bhavet .. 8 ..
