sakṛtkṛṣṇaladānena svarge varṣaṃ sukhī vaset ..
tathā ca pañcavarṣāṇi svarge dattvaiva māṣakam .. 11 ..
yaḥ suvarṇaṃ suvarṇasya brāhmaṇāya prayacchati ..
nirdoṣaḥ syātsa nāke tu modatyabdaśataṃ dhruvam .. 12 ..
3.62.d:
दत्त्वा च माषकं तस्य पुण्यं फलमुपाश्नुते ॥
सुवर्णमाषकं दत्त्वा सूर्यस्योदयनं प्रति ॥ 6 ॥
हुत्वाग्निं सर्वपापेभ्यो मोक्षमाप्नोत्यसंशयम् ॥
त्रेताग्निव्रतमेतत्तु कीर्तितं तस्य नित्यदा ॥ 7 ॥
दिनमध्यगते सूर्ये हुत्वाग्निं यः प्रयच्छति ॥
तस्याग्निनित्यदाने च महत्फलमुदाहृतम् ॥ 8 ॥
सूर्यस्यास्तमये वह्निं हुत्वा तद्वै प्रयच्छति ॥
पुण्यं महत्समाप्नोति नित्यदानेन वै द्विजाः ॥ 9 ॥
त्रिसन्ध्यं कनकं यस्तु हुत्वा वह्निं प्रयच्छति ॥
न स लिप्येत पापेन पद्मपत्रमिवाम्भसा ॥ 3.310.10 ॥
सकृत्कृष्णलदानेन स्वर्गे वर्षं सुखी वसेत् ॥
तथा च पञ्चवर्षाणि स्वर्गे दत्त्वैव माषकम् ॥ 11 ॥
यः सुवर्णं सुवर्णस्य ब्राह्मणाय प्रयच्छति ॥
निर्दोषः स्यात्स नाके तु मोदत्यब्दशतं ध्रुवम् ॥ 12 ॥
3.62.m:
And having given a māṣaka, he enjoys its holy reward. / Having given a māṣaka of gold at the rising of the sun,
and having offered an oblation into the fire, he attains liberation from all sins without doubt; / this is praised as his perpetual observance of the three sacred fires.
When the sun has reached midday, he who, having offered into the fire, gives it— / a great reward is declared for his perpetual offering into the fire.
At the setting of the sun, having offered into the fire, he indeed gives it; / he attains great merit by this daily gift, O twice-born.
He who offers into the fire and gives gold at the three junctions of the day / is not stained by sin, just as a lotus leaf is not [wetted] by water.
By giving a kṛṣṇala once, he lives happily in heaven for a year; / and having given a māṣaka, he lives in heaven for five years.
He who presents a suvarṇa weight of gold to a brahmin / becomes faultless and rejoices in heaven for a full hundred years.

3.62.s:
ātmatulyaṃ suvarṇasya yaḥ prayacchati vai dvijāḥ ..
sarvapāpavinirmukto yatheṣṭāṅgatimāpnuyāt .. 13 ..
brahmaghno vā surāpo vā steno vā gurutalpagaḥ ..
sarvapātakayukto'pi tena dānena mucyate .. 14 ..
śraddhānāmuttamañcaitaddānānāmuttamottamam ..
rukmaṃ dattvā brāhmaṇāya sukhī sarvatra jāyate .. 15 ..
cirānnākaparibhraṣṭo rūpasaubhāgyasaṃyutaḥ ..
tāsāṃ kule tu susphīte guṇaiḥ sarvairyuto naraḥ .. 16 ..
rukmapātrapradānena putrī bhavati mānavaḥ ..
sarveṣāmeva kāmānāṃ yaśasastridivasya ca .. 17 ..
rūpyado rūpamāpnoti bhogamāpnoti tāmradaḥ ..
lohārakūṭayordānātkupyamāpnotyasaṃśayam .. 18 ..
trapusīsakayordānādvahnivṛddhimavāpnuyāt ..
yatheṣṭaṃ lohapātrañca yaḥ pradadyāddvijātaye .. 19 ..
pātraṃ bhavati kāmānāṃ viśeṣaścāsya lohataḥ ..
śilpabhāṇḍāni yo dadyāllohāni vidhivaddvijāḥ .. 3.310.20 ..
3.62.d:
आत्मतुल्यं सुवर्णस्य यः प्रयच्छति वै द्विजाः ॥
सर्वपापविनिर्मुक्तो यथेष्टाङ्गतिमाप्नुयात् ॥ 13 ॥
ब्रह्मघ्नो वा सुरापो वा स्तेनो वा गुरुतल्पगः ॥
सर्वपातकयुक्तोऽपि तेन दानेन मुच्यते ॥ 14 ॥
श्रद्धानामुत्तमञ्चैतद्दानानामुत्तमोत्तमम् ॥
रुक्मं दत्त्वा ब्राह्मणाय सुखी सर्वत्र जायते ॥ 15 ॥
चिरान्नाकपरिभ्रष्टो रूपसौभाग्यसंयुतः ॥
तासां कुले तु सुस्फीते गुणैः सर्वैर्युतो नरः ॥ 16 ॥
रुक्मपात्रप्रदानेन पुत्री भवति मानवः ॥
सर्वेषामेव कामानां यशसस्त्रिदिवस्य च ॥ 17 ॥
रूप्यदो रूपमाप्नोति भोगमाप्नोति ताम्रदः ॥
लोहारकूटयोर्दानात्कुप्यमाप्नोत्यसंशयम् ॥ 18 ॥
त्रपुसीसकयोर्दानाद्वह्निवृद्धिमवाप्नुयात् ॥
यथेष्टं लोहपात्रञ्च यः प्रदद्याद्द्विजातये ॥ 19 ॥
पात्रं भवति कामानां विशेषश्चास्य लोहतः ॥
शिल्पभाण्डानि यो दद्याल्लोहानि विधिवद्द्विजाः ॥ 3.310.20 ॥
3.62.m:
He who presents [his own] weight in gold, O twice-born, / freed from all sins, attains the destination of his desire.
Whether he is a slayer of a brahmin, a drinker of liquor, a thief, or a violator of the guru's bed, / even if burdened with all sins, he is liberated through that gift.
And this is the highest of faithful acts, the highest among supreme gifts; / having given gold to a brahmin, one becomes happy everywhere.
When after a long time he falls from heaven, endowed with beauty and good fortune, / that man is born in a very prosperous family of theirs, endowed with all virtues.
By giving a gold vessel, a person is blessed with sons, / and attains all desires, renown, and heaven.
The giver of silver attains beauty; the giver of copper attains enjoyment. / From giving iron and brass, one undoubtedly obtains base metal.
From giving tin and lead, one obtains an increase of the digestive fire. / Whoever presents an iron vessel at will to a twice-born,
becomes a vessel of desires, and especially so on account of the iron. / Whoever presents artisans' tools made of iron according to the rule, O twice-born,

3.62.s:
vidyādānaphalaṃ tasya kathitaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ ..
carmadātā naro nityaṃ rakṣāṃ samadhigacchati .. 21 ..
āyudhānāṃ pradānena ripunāśamavāpnuyāt ..
rājaliṅgapradānena rājā bhavati bhūtale .. 22 ..
ratnānāṃ ca pradānena rājaiveha prajāyate ..
ratnadānasya yallokaṃ tadbhuktvā suciraṃ dvijāḥ .. 23 ..
vajradaḥ śakralokantu padmarāgaprado raveḥ ..
sadyo marakataṃ dattvā viṣṇuloke mahīyate .. 24 ..
muktāphalapradānena vāruṇaṃ lokamaśnute ..
vaidūryasya pradānena dvīpānāṃ sapta modate .. 25 ..
ratnānyanyāni dattvā ca rājarājasya ca dvijāḥ ..
sarveṣāmeva ratnānāṃ kanakaṃ śreṣṭhamucyate .. 26..
dhāraṇaṃ kīrtanaṃ dānaṃ kanakasya praśasyate ..
duḥsvapraśamanaṃ dānaṃ duriṣṭasya ca nāśanam .. 27 ..
paraṃ pāpaharaṃ jñeyamalakṣmīśamanaṃ tathā ..
dattvā suvarṇaṃ lokeṣu yatheṣṭeṣu ca modate ..28..
3.62.d:
विद्यादानफलं तस्य कथितं नात्र संशयः ॥
चर्मदाता नरो नित्यं रक्षां समधिगच्छति ॥ 21 ॥
आयुधानां प्रदानेन रिपुनाशमवाप्नुयात् ॥
राजलिङ्गप्रदानेन राजा भवति भूतले ॥ 22 ॥
रत्नानां च प्रदानेन राजैवेह प्रजायते ॥
रत्नदानस्य यल्लोकं तद्भुक्त्वा सुचिरं द्विजाः ॥ 23 ॥
वज्रदः शक्रलोकन्तु पद्मरागप्रदो रवेः ॥
सद्यो मरकतं दत्त्वा विष्णुलोके महीयते ॥ 24 ॥
मुक्ताफलप्रदानेन वारुणं लोकमश्नुते ॥
वैदूर्यस्य प्रदानेन द्वीपानां सप्त मोदते ॥ 25 ॥
रत्नान्यन्यानि दत्त्वा च राजराजस्य च द्विजाः ॥
सर्वेषामेव रत्नानां कनकं श्रेष्ठमुच्यते ॥ 26॥
धारणं कीर्तनं दानं कनकस्य प्रशस्यते ॥
दुःस्वप्रशमनं दानं दुरिष्टस्य च नाशनम् ॥ 27 ॥
परं पापहरं ज्ञेयमलक्ष्मीशमनं तथा ॥
दत्त्वा सुवर्णं लोकेषु यथेष्टेषु च मोदते ॥28॥
3.62.m:
to him the fruit of the gift of knowledge is declared—there is no doubt here. / A man who gives leather always attains protection.
By the gift of weapons one achieves the destruction of enemies. / By the gift of royal insignia one becomes a king on earth.
And by the gift of precious gems one is born indeed as a king here [on earth]. / Having enjoyed for a very long time the world that belongs to the gift of gems, O twice-born,
the giver of diamond [goes] to the world of Śakra, the giver of ruby to the Sun's. / Having given an emerald, one is immediately honoured in the world of Viṣṇu.
By giving a pearl one attains the realm of Varuṇa. / By giving cat's eye one rejoices in seven continents.
And having given other gems, [one attains the realm] of the king of kings, O twice-born. / Of all gems, gold is said to be the foremost.
Wearing, praising, and giving gold are commended. / The gift alleviates nightmares and destroys the ill-sacrificed;
it should be known as supremely sin-destroying and pacifying misfortune. / Having given gold, one rejoices in worlds desired at will,

3.62.s:
vimānenārkavarṇena haṃsayuktena bhāsvatā ..
devarāmāgaṇāḍhyena kāmagena vihāyasā.....
bhuktvā divi ciraṃ bhogānmānuṣye sukhamāpnuyāt ..
agnerapatyaṃ prathamaṃ suvarṇaṃ bhūrvaiṣṇavī brahmasutāśca gāvaḥ ..
sarvaṃ hi dattaṃ bhavatīha tena yaḥ kāñcanaṃ gāñca mahīñca dadyāt .. 3.310.30 ..
3.62.d:
विमानेनार्कवर्णेन हंसयुक्तेन भास्वता ॥
देवरामागणाढ्येन कामगेन विहायसा॥॥।
भुक्त्वा दिवि चिरं भोगान्मानुष्ये सुखमाप्नुयात् ॥
अग्नेरपत्यं प्रथमं सुवर्णं भूर्वैष्णवी ब्रह्मसुताश्च गावः ॥
सर्वं हि दत्तं भवतीह तेन यः काञ्चनं गाञ्च महीञ्च दद्यात् ॥ 3.310.30 ॥
3.62.m: in an aerial chariot shining like the sun, yoked with swans, / filled with hosts of celestial women, travelling through the sky at will. / Having long enjoyed pleasures in heaven, he obtains happiness in human existence. / Gold is the firstborn child of Agni; the earth belongs to Viṣṇu, and cows are daughters of Brahmā; / everything is indeed given here by him who gives gold, a cow, and land.

3.63.s:
3.311
haṃsa uvāca ..
narastvāsanadānena sthānaṃ sarvatra vindati ..
śayyādānena cāpnoti bhāryāṃ brāhmaṇasattamāḥ .. 1 ..
3.63.d:
3.311
हंस उवाच ॥
नरस्त्वासनदानेन स्थानं सर्वत्र विन्दति ॥
शय्यादानेन चाप्नोति भार्यां ब्राह्मणसत्तमाः ॥ 1 ॥
3.63.m: 3.311 / Haṃsa said: / By the gift of a seat a man obtains a high position everywhere. / By the gift of a bed, O best of brahmins, he obtains a wife.

3.63.s:
dattvā dvijāya śayanaṃ svāstīrṇaṃ sottaracchadam ..
kule mahati sambhūtāṃ rūpadraviṇasaṃyutām ..2..
3.63.d:
दत्त्वा द्विजाय शयनं स्वास्तीर्णं सोत्तरच्छदम् ॥
कुले महति सम्भूतां रूपद्रविणसंयुताम् ॥2॥
3.63.m: Having given to a twice-born a couch well spread and provided with an upper coverlet, / [he gains a wife] born in a great family, endowed with beauty and wealth,

3.63.s:
tathā pakṣavatīṃ bhavyāṃ prāpnoti vaśagāṃ tathā ..
anenaiva pradānena bhāryā patimavāpnuyāt .. 3 ..
3.63.d:
तथा पक्षवतीं भव्यां प्राप्नोति वशगां तथा ॥
अनेनैव प्रदानेन भार्या पतिमवाप्नुयात् ॥ 3 ॥
3.63.m: having powerful relatives, auspicious, and obedient to him. / By this very gift a woman obtains a husband.

3.63.s:
vitānakapradānena sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate ..
chatradaśca tathā viprā nātra kāryā vicāraṇā .. 4..
3.63.d:
वितानकप्रदानेन सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते ॥
छत्रदश्च तथा विप्रा नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥ 4॥
3.63.m: By the gift of a canopy one is freed from all sins. / And so also the giver of an umbrella, O wise brahmins; no doubt should be entertained here.

3.63.s:
chatraṃ śataśalākaṃ tu dattvaivātapavāraṇam ..
sarvatāpavini rmuktaḥ svargaloke mahīyate .. 5 ..
3.63.d:
छत्रं शतशलाकं तु दत्त्वैवातपवारणम् ॥
सर्वतापविनि र्मुक्तः स्वर्गलोके महीयते ॥ 5 ॥
3.63.m: Having given an umbrella with a hundred ribs to keep off the sun, / completely freed from all torment, he is honoured in heaven.

3.63.s:
yāmyaṃ mārgaṃ tathā yāti sukhena dvijasattamāḥ ..
upānahe tathā dattvā ślakṣṇe snehasamanvite .. 6 ..
3.63.d:
याम्यं मार्गं तथा याति सुखेन द्विजसत्तमाः ॥
उपानहे तथा दत्त्वा श्लक्ष्णे स्नेहसमन्विते ॥ 6 ॥
3.63.m: And he travels the path of Yama with ease, O best of the twice-born. / Likewise, having given shoes that are smooth and treated with oil,

3.63.s:
rathamaśvatarī yuktaṃ tridivaṃ pratipadyate..
sarvapāpavinirmukto yāmyamārgaṃ sukhaṃ vrajet .. 7 ..
3.63.d:
रथमश्वतरी युक्तं त्रिदिवं प्रतिपद्यते॥
सर्वपापविनिर्मुक्तो याम्यमार्गं सुखं व्रजेत् ॥ 7 ॥
3.63.m: he enters heaven in a chariot yoked with she-mules; / freed from all sins, he treads the path of Yama with ease.

3.63.s:
tālavṛntapradānena sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate ..
pādukānāṃ pradānena gatimāpnoti śobhanām .. 8 ..
3.63.d:
तालवृन्तप्रदानेन सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते ॥
पादुकानां प्रदानेन गतिमाप्नोति शोभनाम् ॥ 8 ॥
3.63.m: By giving a palm-leaf fan one is freed from all sins. / By giving sandals one attains an auspicious path.

3.63.s:
pādapīṭhapradānena sthānaṃ sarvatra vindati ..
sthānameva tathāpnoti daṇḍaṃ dattvā dvijātaye .. 9 ..
3.63.d:
पादपीठप्रदानेन स्थानं सर्वत्र विन्दति ॥
स्थानमेव तथाप्नोति दण्डं दत्त्वा द्विजातये ॥ 9 ॥
3.63.m: By giving a footstool one finds a standing everywhere. / One likewise obtains a standing by giving a staff to a twice-born.

3.63.s:
yajñopavītadānena vastradānaphalaṃ labhet ..
uṣṇīṣadānasya tathā phalametadudāhṛtam .. 3.311.10 ..
3.63.d:
यज्ञोपवीतदानेन वस्त्रदानफलं लभेत् ॥
उष्णीषदानस्य तथा फलमेतदुदाहृतम् ॥ 3.311.10 ॥
3.63.m: By giving a sacred thread one receives the fruit of the gift of clothing. / The fruit of the gift of a turban has likewise been described thus.

3.63.s:
dantakāṣṭhapradānena saubhāgyaṃ mahadāpnuyāt ..
mṛttikāyāḥ pradānena śuciḥ sarvatra jāyate .. 11 ..
3.63.d:
दन्तकाष्ठप्रदानेन सौभाग्यं महदाप्नुयात् ॥
मृत्तिकायाः प्रदानेन शुचिः सर्वत्र जायते ॥ 11 ॥
3.63.m: By giving a tooth-stick one obtains great good fortune. / By the gift of clay one becomes pure everywhere.

3.63.s:
śaucasnānodakaṃ dattvā virogastvabhijāyate ..
roganāśamavāpnoti tathābhyaṅgapradaḥ sadā .. 12 ..
3.63.d:
शौचस्नानोदकं दत्त्वा विरोगस्त्वभिजायते ॥
रोगनाशमवाप्नोति तथाभ्यङ्गप्रदः सदा ॥ 12 ॥
3.63.m: Having given water for purification and bathing, one is born free from disease. / The giver of oil for anointing always attains freedom from illness.

3.63.s:
tathaivauṣadhadānena roganāśamupāśnute ..
sthānīyāni sugandhīni dattvā saubhāgyamaśnute .. 13 ..
3.63.d:
तथैवौषधदानेन रोगनाशमुपाश्नुते ॥
स्थानीयानि सुगन्धीनि दत्त्वा सौभाग्यमश्नुते ॥ 13 ॥
3.63.m: Likewise, by giving medicine one obtains freedom from illness. / Having given fragrant toilet articles, one enjoys good fortune.

3.63.s:
anulepanadānena rūpavānabhijāyate ..
kāyāgnidīptaṃ prākāśyaṃ gatiñcaiva tathottamām .. 14 ..
3.63.d:
अनुलेपनदानेन रूपवानभिजायते ॥
कायाग्निदीप्तं प्राकाश्यं गतिञ्चैव तथोत्तमाम् ॥ 14 ॥
3.63.m: By giving ointment one is born handsome, / radiant with the body's fire alight, luminous, and of highest status.

3.63.s:
yastu saṃsādhanārthāya brāhmaṇāya prayacchati ..
sa yāti vahnisālokyaṃ śatrunāśaṃ ca vindati .. 15 ..
3.63.d:
यस्तु संसाधनार्थाय ब्राह्मणाय प्रयच्छति ॥
स याति वह्निसालोक्यं शत्रुनाशं च विन्दति ॥ 15 ॥
3.63.m: Whoever gives [toiletries] to a brahmin for the sake of adornment, / goes to the same world as the Fire-god and attains the destruction of enemies.

3.63.s:
taijasāni tu pātrāṇi dattvā salavaṇāni ca ..
pātratāmeti kāmānāṃ lāvaṇyaṃ cāpnuyānmahat .. 16 ..
3.63.d:
तैजसानि तु पात्राणि दत्त्वा सलवणानि च ॥
पात्रतामेति कामानां लावण्यं चाप्नुयान्महत् ॥ 16 ॥
3.63.m: Having given metal vessels filled with salt, / he becomes a vessel of his desires and obtains great charm.

3.63.s:
taijasāni tu pātrāṇi satailāni prayacchataḥ ..
ārogyamuttamaṃ proktaṃ lāvaṇyamapi cottamam .. 17 ..
3.63.d:
तैजसानि तु पात्राणि सतैलानि प्रयच्छतः ॥
आरोग्यमुत्तमं प्रोक्तं लावण्यमपि चोत्तमम् ॥ 17 ॥
3.63.m: For him who gives metal vessels filled with oil, / excellent health is declared, and also supreme charm.

3.63.s:
taijasāni tu pātrāṇi samadhūni prayacchataḥ ..
lāvaṇyamuttamaṃ proktaṃ saubhāgyamapi cottamam .. .. 18 ..
3.63.d:
तैजसानि तु पात्राणि समधूनि प्रयच्छतः ॥
लावण्यमुत्तमं प्रोक्तं सौभाग्यमपि चोत्तमम् ॥ ॥ 18 ॥
3.63.m: For him who gives metal vessels filled with honey, / supreme charm is declared, and also supreme good fortune.

3.63.s:
naraścandanadānena sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate ..
tathaivāgurudānena yaśasā bhuvi rājate .. 19 ..
3.63.d:
नरश्चन्दनदानेन सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते ॥
तथैवागुरुदानेन यशसा भुवि राजते ॥ 19 ॥
3.63.m: By giving sandalwood a man is freed from all sins. / Likewise, by giving agallochum he shines with renown on earth.

3.63.s:
saubhāgyakārakaṃ proktaṃ pradānaṃ kuṅkumasya tu ..
tathā karpūradānena sarvānkāmānavāpnuyāt .. 3.311.20 ..
3.63.d:
सौभाग्यकारकं प्रोक्तं प्रदानं कुङ्कुमस्य तु ॥
तथा कर्पूरदानेन सर्वान्कामानवाप्नुयात् ॥ 3.311.20 ॥
3.63.m: The gift of saffron is declared to bring good fortune. / Likewise, by the gift of camphor one obtains all desires.

3.63.s:
mṛgacarmapradānena yaśasā bhuvi rājate ..
dattvā jātīphalaṃ viprāḥ saphalāṃ vindate kriyām .. .. 21 ..
3.63.d:
मृगचर्मप्रदानेन यशसा भुवि राजते ॥
दत्त्वा जातीफलं विप्राः सफलां विन्दते क्रियाम् ॥ ॥ 21 ॥
3.63.m: By giving a deerskin one shines with renown on earth. / Having given nutmeg, O brahmins, one finds one's work fruitful.

3.63.s:
snānānāṃ mukhavāsānāṃ dhūpānāṃ ca pradāyakāḥ ..
loke prayānti priyatāṃ bhavanti ca sugandhinaḥ .. 22 ..
3.63.d:
स्नानानां मुखवासानां धूपानां च प्रदायकाः ॥
लोके प्रयान्ति प्रियतां भवन्ति च सुगन्धिनः ॥ 22 ॥
3.63.m: Those who give bath-preparations, mouth-perfumes, and incense / become beloved in the world and fragrant in body.

3.63.s:
dattvā pūgaphalānviprāḥ saphalāṃ vindate kriyām ..
tāmbūlasya pradānena saubhāgyamapi vindati .. 23 ..
3.63.d:
दत्त्वा पूगफलान्विप्राः सफलां विन्दते क्रियाम् ॥
ताम्बूलस्य प्रदानेन सौभाग्यमपि विन्दति ॥ 23 ॥
3.63.m: Having given areca nuts, O brahmins, one finds one's work fruitful. / By the gift of betel one also gains good fortune.

3.63.s:
samudrajānāṃ bhāṇḍānāṃ śaṅkhādīnāṃ pradāyakaḥ ..
pātrī bhavati kāmānāṃ yaśasaśca na saṃśayaḥ .. 24 ..
3.63.d:
समुद्रजानां भाण्डानां शङ्खादीनां प्रदायकः ॥
पात्री भवति कामानां यशसश्च न संशयः ॥ 24 ॥
3.63.m: A giver of sea-born vessels, conches and the like, / becomes a worthy vessel of desires and renown—there is no doubt.

3.63.s:
kaṅkatasya pradānena parāṃ vācaṃ pramuñcati ..
śayyāpradāno lokeṣu tathā sthānakaraṃ param .. 25 ..
3.63.d:
कङ्कतस्य प्रदानेन परां वाचं प्रमुञ्चति ॥
शय्याप्रदानो लोकेषु तथा स्थानकरं परम् ॥ 25 ॥
3.63.m: By giving a comb one pours forth supreme eloquence. / The gift of a bed in this world also brings supreme rank.

3.63.s:
arthine yadabhīṣṭaṃ syātsvalpaṃ vā yadi vā bahu ..
taddattvā puṇyamāpnoti rājasūyāśvamedhayoḥ .. 26 ..
3.63.d:
अर्थिने यदभीष्टं स्यात्स्वल्पं वा यदि वा बहु ॥
तद्दत्त्वा पुण्यमाप्नोति राजसूयाश्वमेधयोः ॥ 26 ॥
3.63.m: Whatever is desired by a petitioner, whether little or much, / by giving it one obtains the merit of the Rājasūya and Aśvamedha [sacrifices].

3.63.s:
kimcchikaiḥ pūjakairbrāhmaṇānāṃ lokaṃ gatvā brahmaṇo brāhmaṇebhyaḥ ..
devairvipraiḥ pūjyamānaḥ sukhī syāttasmāddeyaṃ prārthitaṃ brāhmaṇebhyaḥ .. 27 ..
3.312
.. haṃsa uvāca .. ..
nṛvāhānpuruṣo yastu dvije samyakprayacchati ..
aśvamedhaphalaṃ tasya kathitaṃ dvijasattamāḥ .. 1 ..
śibikāyāḥ pradānena vahniṣṭomaphalaṃ tathā ..
dāsaṃ karmakaraṃ dattvā gosavasya phalaṃ labhet .. 2 ..
sa yāti śakrasālokyaṃ yastu yodhaṃ prayacchati ..
yastu karmakarīṃ dāsīṃ brāhmaṇāya prayacchati .. 3 ..
lokāstu subhagāstasya vasūnāṃ samudāhṛtāḥ ..
taruṇīṃ rūpasampannāṃ dāsīṃ yastu prayacchati .. 4 ..
sopsarobhirmudāyuktaḥ krīḍate nandane vane ..
uṣṭraṃ vā gardabhaṃ viprā yo yacchati dvijātaye ..5..
alakāṃ sa samāsādya yakṣendraiḥ saha modate ..
dānānāmuttamaṃ proktaṃ pradānaṃ turagasya tu ..6 ..
3.63.d:
किम्च्छिकैः पूजकैर्ब्राह्मणानां लोकं गत्वा ब्रह्मणो ब्राह्मणेभ्यः ॥
देवैर्विप्रैः पूज्यमानः सुखी स्यात्तस्माद्देयं प्रार्थितं ब्राह्मणेभ्यः ॥ 27 ॥
3.312
॥ हंस उवाच ॥ ॥
नृवाहान्पुरुषो यस्तु द्विजे सम्यक्प्रयच्छति ॥
अश्वमेधफलं तस्य कथितं द्विजसत्तमाः ॥ 1 ॥
शिबिकायाः प्रदानेन वह्निष्टोमफलं तथा ॥
दासं कर्मकरं दत्त्वा गोसवस्य फलं लभेत् ॥ 2 ॥
स याति शक्रसालोक्यं यस्तु योधं प्रयच्छति ॥
यस्तु कर्मकरीं दासीं ब्राह्मणाय प्रयच्छति ॥ 3 ॥
लोकास्तु सुभगास्तस्य वसूनां समुदाहृताः ॥
तरुणीं रूपसम्पन्नां दासीं यस्तु प्रयच्छति ॥ 4 ॥
सोप्सरोभिर्मुदायुक्तः क्रीडते नन्दने वने ॥
उष्ट्रं वा गर्दभं विप्रा यो यच्छति द्विजातये ॥5॥
अलकां स समासाद्य यक्षेन्द्रैः सह मोदते ॥
दानानामुत्तमं प्रोक्तं प्रदानं तुरगस्य तु ॥6 ॥
3.63.m:
Having gone to the world of Brahmā through those who honour brahmins by giving to brahmins whatever they wish, / honoured by gods and brahmins, he becomes happy; therefore, what is requested should be given to brahmins.
3.312 / Haṃsa said: / A man who duly gives human-drawn vehicles to a twice-born, / for him the fruit of an aśvamedha is declared, O best of the twice-born.
By the gift of a palanquin, likewise, [one obtains] the fruit of an agniṣṭoma; / having given a servant who does work, one obtains the fruit of a gosava.
He goes to dwelling in the same world as Śakra who gives a warrior; / but he who gives a female servant who does work to a brahmin,
his worlds are declared to be charming, belonging to the Vasus. / But he who gives a youthful female servant endowed with beauty,
he sports with apsarases filled with joy in the Nandana forest. / O brahmins, he who gives a camel or a donkey to a twice-born,
having reached Alakā, rejoices together with the lords of yakṣas. / The giving of a horse is declared the highest of gifts.

3.63.s:
vaḍavāyāḥ pradānena tathā bahuphalaṃ smṛtam ..
turaṅgaṃ ye prayacchaṃti sūryalokaṃ vrajanti te .. 7 ..
yāvanti tasya romāṇi tāvadvarṣaśatāni ca ..
śuklaṃ turaṅgamaṃ dattvā phalaṃ daśaguṇaṃ labhet .. 8 ..
gauryathā kapilā śreṣṭhā tathaiva turagasya tu ..
turaṅgamaṃ saparyāṇaṃ sālaṅkāraṃ prayacchati .. 9 ..
puṇḍarīkaphalaṃ proktaṃ nātra kāryā vicāraṇā ..
caturbhisturagairyuktaṃ sarvopakaraṇairyutam .. 3.312.10 ..
rathaṃ dvijāye dattvā rājasūyaphalaṃ labhet ..
pradāya kariṇīṃ samyagetadeva phalaṃ labhet .. 11 ..
kuñjarasya pradānena svargaloke mahīyate ..
rājā bhavati lokesminyaśovikramasaṃyutaḥ .. 12 ..
suvarṇakakṣyaṃ mātaṅgaṃ dattvā viprāya vai dvijāḥ ..
rājasūyāśvamedhābhyāṃ phalaṃ vindatyasaṃśayam.. 13 ..
3.63.d:
वडवायाः प्रदानेन तथा बहुफलं स्मृतम् ॥
तुरङ्गं ये प्रयच्छंति सूर्यलोकं व्रजन्ति ते ॥ 7 ॥
यावन्ति तस्य रोमाणि तावद्वर्षशतानि च ॥
शुक्लं तुरङ्गमं दत्त्वा फलं दशगुणं लभेत् ॥ 8 ॥
गौर्यथा कपिला श्रेष्ठा तथैव तुरगस्य तु ॥
तुरङ्गमं सपर्याणं सालङ्कारं प्रयच्छति ॥ 9 ॥
पुण्डरीकफलं प्रोक्तं नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥
चतुर्भिस्तुरगैर्युक्तं सर्वोपकरणैर्युतम् ॥ 3.312.10 ॥
रथं द्विजाये दत्त्वा राजसूयफलं लभेत् ॥
प्रदाय करिणीं सम्यगेतदेव फलं लभेत् ॥ 11 ॥
कुञ्जरस्य प्रदानेन स्वर्गलोके महीयते ॥
राजा भवति लोकेस्मिन्यशोविक्रमसंयुतः ॥ 12 ॥
सुवर्णकक्ष्यं मातङ्गं दत्त्वा विप्राय वै द्विजाः ॥
राजसूयाश्वमेधाभ्यां फलं विन्दत्यसंशयम्॥ 13 ॥
3.63.m:
By the gift of a mare, likewise, abundant fruit is remembered. / Those who give a horse go to the world of the sun.
As many hairs as it has, for so many hundreds of years. / Having given a white horse, one obtains ten times that fruit.
Just as a kapilā cow is foremost, even so is it among horses. / [If] he gives a horse with a saddle and with ornaments,
the fruit of a puṇḍarīka sacrifice is declared; no doubt should be made here. / Yoked with four horses and endowed with all equipment,
having given a chariot to a twice-born, one obtains the fruit of a rājasūya. / Duly giving a female elephant, one obtains this very fruit.
By the gift of an elephant, one is glorified in heaven; / in this world he becomes a king endowed with fame and valour.
Having given an elephant with golden girths to a brahmin, O twice-born, / he attains the fruit of both the rājasūya and aśvamedha, without doubt.

3.63.s:
caturbhiḥ kuñjarairyuktaṃ rathaṃ dattvā dvijātaye ..
samagrabhūmi dānasya phalaṃ prāpnotyasaṃśayam .. 14..
bhūmiḥ saśailā savanā satoyā dattā hi loke bhavatīha tena ..
iṣṭām̐śca lokānpuruṣaḥ prayāti sampūjyamānastridaśairmahātmā .. 15 ..
3.313
haṃsa uvāca ..
dānānāmuttamaṃ loke vastradānaṃ prakīrtitam ..
vāso hi sarvadaivatyaṃ sarvaprāyojyamaśnute ..1 ..
vastradātā suveśaḥ syādrūpadraviṇasaṃyutaḥ ..
yukto lāvaṇyasaubhāgyairvirogaśca tathā dvijāḥ .. 2 ..
nīlaṃ raktaṃ tathā jīrṇaṃ na deyaṃ brāhmaṇasya tu ..
deyaṃ varañcāṅgirasaṃ kṣaumaṃ dattvā bṛhaspateḥ ..3.
dattvā kārpāsikaṃ vastraṃ svargaloke mahīyate ..
dattvā saromaṃ tadapi phalaṃ daśaguṇaṃ bhavet .. 4..
āvikaṃ vasanaṃ dattvā bhṛgūṇāṃ lokamāpnuyāt ..
chāgaṃ dattvā cāṅgirasaṃ kṣaumaṃ dattvā bṛhaspateḥ .. 5 ..
3.63.d:
चतुर्भिः कुञ्जरैर्युक्तं रथं दत्त्वा द्विजातये ॥
समग्रभूमि दानस्य फलं प्राप्नोत्यसंशयम् ॥ 14॥
भूमिः सशैला सवना सतोया दत्ता हि लोके भवतीह तेन ॥
इष्टाम्̐श्च लोकान्पुरुषः प्रयाति सम्पूज्यमानस्त्रिदशैर्महात्मा ॥ 15 ॥
3.313
हंस उवाच ॥
दानानामुत्तमं लोके वस्त्रदानं प्रकीर्तितम् ॥
वासो हि सर्वदैवत्यं सर्वप्रायोज्यमश्नुते ॥1 ॥
वस्त्रदाता सुवेशः स्याद्रूपद्रविणसंयुतः ॥
युक्तो लावण्यसौभाग्यैर्विरोगश्च तथा द्विजाः ॥ 2 ॥
नीलं रक्तं तथा जीर्णं न देयं ब्राह्मणस्य तु ॥
देयं वरञ्चाङ्गिरसं क्षौमं दत्त्वा बृहस्पतेः ॥3.
दत्त्वा कार्पासिकं वस्त्रं स्वर्गलोके महीयते ॥
दत्त्वा सरोमं तदपि फलं दशगुणं भवेत् ॥ 4॥
आविकं वसनं दत्त्वा भृगूणां लोकमाप्नुयात् ॥
छागं दत्त्वा चाङ्गिरसं क्षौमं दत्त्वा बृहस्पतेः ॥ 5 ॥
3.63.m:
Having given to a twice-born a chariot yoked with four elephants, / he obtains the fruit of the gift of the entire earth, without doubt.
By him in this world, indeed, the earth with its mountains, forests, and waters has been given; / and that great-souled man goes to the desired worlds, worshipped by the gods.
3.313 / Haṃsa said: / The gift of clothing is proclaimed the highest of gifts in the world; / for clothing belongs to all deities and obtains applicability to all.
The giver of clothing becomes well-attired, endowed with beauty and wealth, / endowed with charm and good fortune, and free from disease, O twice-born.
Blue, [impure] red, and worn-out [cloth] must not be given to a brahmin. / An excellent [cloth should be] given, [such as one worthy of] the descendants of Aṅgiras, or having given linen [one attains the world] of Bṛhaspati.
Having given a garment of cotton, one is glorified in heaven; / having given one that is woolen, the fruit becomes tenfold.
Having given sheep's wool clothing, one attains the world of the Bhṛgus; / having given goat's wool, [the world] of the descendants of Aṅgiras; having given linen, [the world] of Bṛhaspati;

3.63.s:
vasūnāṃ lokamāpnoti kuśakauśeyavāsasī. ..
krimijañca tato dattvā somaloke mahīyate .. 6 ..
agniṣṭomamavāpnoti dattvaiva mṛgalomikām ..
dattvā valkalajaṃ vāso vasūnāṃ lokamāpnuyāt .. 7 ..
sumerakadalyādīnāṃ dattvā caiva tathājinam ..
vāravāṇaṃ śirastrāṇaṃ hastatrāṇaṃ tathaiva ca .. 8 ..
pādatrāṇaṃ ca dadataḥ pṛthagyaphalaṃ smṛtam ..
vastradānaṃ pavitrantu pitṝṇāmapi tāraṇam ..9..
kausuṃbharaktaṃ dattvā tu saubhāgyaṃ mahadāpnuyāt ..
dānātkuṅkumaraktasya lāvaṇyaṃ mahadāpnuyāt ..3.313.10 ..
raṅgairanyairanīlaiśca raktaṃ dattvā sukhī bhavet ..
yathāyathā tu vastrasya bhavatīha maharghatā .. 11 ..
yathāyathā śubhratā ca tathā puṇyaphalaṃ labhet..
anyeṣāmapi dānānāmetadeva prakīrtitam .. 12 ..
3.63.d:
वसूनां लोकमाप्नोति कुशकौशेयवाससी॥।
क्रिमिजञ्च ततो दत्त्वा सोमलोके महीयते ॥ 6 ॥
अग्निष्टोममवाप्नोति दत्त्वैव मृगलोमिकाम् ॥
दत्त्वा वल्कलजं वासो वसूनां लोकमाप्नुयात् ॥ 7 ॥
सुमेरकदल्यादीनां दत्त्वा चैव तथाजिनम् ॥
वारवाणं शिरस्त्राणं हस्तत्राणं तथैव च ॥ 8 ॥
पादत्राणं च ददतः पृथग्यफलं स्मृतम् ॥
वस्त्रदानं पवित्रन्तु पितॄणामपि तारणम् ॥9॥
कौसुंभरक्तं दत्त्वा तु सौभाग्यं महदाप्नुयात् ॥
दानात्कुङ्कुमरक्तस्य लावण्यं महदाप्नुयात् ॥3.313.10 ॥
रङ्गैरन्यैरनीलैश्च रक्तं दत्त्वा सुखी भवेत् ॥
यथायथा तु वस्त्रस्य भवतीह महर्घता ॥ 11 ॥
यथायथा शुभ्रता च तथा पुण्यफलं लभेत्॥
अन्येषामपि दानानामेतदेव प्रकीर्तितम् ॥ 12 ॥
3.63.m:
he attains the world of the Vasus [by giving] garments of kuśa grass and silk; / and having given that which is born of worms, he is glorified in the world of Soma.
He attains [the fruit of] an agniṣṭoma having given [a garment] of deer-hair; / having given a garment made of bark, one attains the world of the Vasus.
And likewise, having given the deer-skins of sumera, kadalī, and the like, / an armour-coat, a helmet, and a pair of hand-guards,
as well as footwear, a distinct sacrifice's fruit is remembered for the giver. / The gift of clothing is purifying and rescues even the ancestors.
Having given cloth dyed with safflower, one attains great good fortune; / from the gift of cloth dyed with saffron, one attains great charm.
Having given cloth dyed with other colours that are not blue, one becomes happy. / In whatever manner the preciousness of the garment increases in this world,
and in whatever manner its whiteness [increases], thus he obtains the fruit of merit. / For other gifts as well, this very [principle] is proclaimed.

3.63.s:
sarvado vastradaḥ prokto yataḥ sarvatra vastravān ..
pūjāmāpnoti dharmajñāstaddhi tasmādviśiṣyate .. 13 ..
vastradaḥ suciraṃ kālaṃ bhuktvā devasukhāndivi ..
vimānenārkavarṇena haṃsayuktena bhāsvatā .. 14 ..
mānuṣyamāsādya bhavatyarogaḥ śaucānvitaḥ saukhyaparo vinītaḥ ..
janābhirāmaśca tathā suveśaḥ pūjyaśca loke viduṣāṃ sadaiva .. 15 ..
3.314
haṃsa uvāca ..
dhānyānāmuttamaṃ dānaṃ kathitaṃ dvijapuṅgavāḥ ..
dhānyebhyo'pi paraṃ dhānyaṃ raktaśāliḥ prakīrtitaḥ .. 1 ..
raktaśāliṃ naro dattvā sūryaloke mahīyate ..
dattvā tathā sugandhām̐śca gandharvaiḥ saha modate .. 2 ..
kalamānāṃ pradānena śakraloke mahīyate ..
mahāśāleḥ pradānena vasūnāṃ lokamāpnuyāt .. 3 ..
kāṣṭhaśāliṃ tathā dattvā alakāyāṃ prasīdati ..
vrīhīnāṃ cānyadhānyānāṃ dānātsvargamavāpnuyāt .. 4 ..
3.63.d:
सर्वदो वस्त्रदः प्रोक्तो यतः सर्वत्र वस्त्रवान् ॥
पूजामाप्नोति धर्मज्ञास्तद्धि तस्माद्विशिष्यते ॥ 13 ॥
वस्त्रदः सुचिरं कालं भुक्त्वा देवसुखान्दिवि ॥
विमानेनार्कवर्णेन हंसयुक्तेन भास्वता ॥ 14 ॥
मानुष्यमासाद्य भवत्यरोगः शौचान्वितः सौख्यपरो विनीतः ॥
जनाभिरामश्च तथा सुवेशः पूज्यश्च लोके विदुषां सदैव ॥ 15 ॥
3.314
हंस उवाच ॥
धान्यानामुत्तमं दानं कथितं द्विजपुङ्गवाः ॥
धान्येभ्योऽपि परं धान्यं रक्तशालिः प्रकीर्तितः ॥ 1 ॥
रक्तशालिं नरो दत्त्वा सूर्यलोके महीयते ॥
दत्त्वा तथा सुगन्धाम्̐श्च गन्धर्वैः सह मोदते ॥ 2 ॥
कलमानां प्रदानेन शक्रलोके महीयते ॥
महाशालेः प्रदानेन वसूनां लोकमाप्नुयात् ॥ 3 ॥
काष्ठशालिं तथा दत्त्वा अलकायां प्रसीदति ॥
व्रीहीनां चान्यधान्यानां दानात्स्वर्गमवाप्नुयात् ॥ 4 ॥
3.63.m:
The giver of clothing is declared to be the giver of everything, since everywhere he who has clothes / receives honour, O knowers of dharma; therefore, indeed, it is superior.
The giver of clothing, having enjoyed divine pleasures in heaven for a very long time, / by means of a shining aerial chariot having the colour of the sun and yoked with swans,
attains human birth and becomes free from disease, pure, devoted to happiness, modest, / pleasing to people, well-attired, and always worthy of worship among the wise in the world.
3.314 / Haṃsa said: / The gift of grains is declared the highest, O bulls among the twice-born; / and even above all grains, red rice is proclaimed [supreme].
A man, having given red rice, is glorified in the world of the sun; / and having given fragrant [rice], he rejoices with the gandharvas.
By the gift of kalama rice, he is glorified in the world of Śakra; / by the gift of mahāśāli rice, he attains the world of the Vasus.
Having likewise given kāṣṭhaśāli rice, he is happy in Alakā; / from the gift of vrīhi and other grains, he attains heaven.

3.63.s:
yava pradānena naraḥ śakraloke mahīyate ..
tathā godhūmadānena vasūnāṃ lokamāpnuyāt .. 5 ..
priyo bhavati lokasya priyaṅguṃ yaḥ prayacchati ..
dadāti yastu śyāmākaṃ tasya prīyanti devatāḥ .. 6 ..
anyeṣāṃ śūkadhānyānāṃ pradānābhirato naraḥ ..
svargalokamavāpnoti nātra kāryā vicāraṇā .. 7 ..
mudgadaḥ śakralokantu yamalokantu māṣadaḥ ..
yatheṣṭaṃ lokamāpnoti tathā viprāstilapradaḥ .. 8 ..
ṣaṣṭikānāṃ pradānena lokaṃ nairṛtakaṃ labhet ..
sacīṇacaṇakaṃ dattvā lokaṃ vāruṇamāpnuyāt .. 9 ..
vāyavyañca masūrāṇi rājamāṣāṇi dhānadam ..
anyeṣāṃ śiṃbidhānyānāṃ dānātsvargamavāpnuyāt .. 3.314.10 ..
ikṣumṛdvīkayordānātparaṃ saubhāgyamāpnuyāt ..
guḍapradastathārogyaṃ sitādaḥ kāmamīpsitam .. 11 ..
phāṇitasya pradānena parāṃ tṛptimavāpnuyāt ..
khaṇḍapradaśca saubhāgyaṃ sarvānkāmānmadhupradaḥ .. 12 ..
3.63.d:
यव प्रदानेन नरः शक्रलोके महीयते ॥
तथा गोधूमदानेन वसूनां लोकमाप्नुयात् ॥ 5 ॥
प्रियो भवति लोकस्य प्रियङ्गुं यः प्रयच्छति ॥
ददाति यस्तु श्यामाकं तस्य प्रीयन्ति देवताः ॥ 6 ॥
अन्येषां शूकधान्यानां प्रदानाभिरतो नरः ॥
स्वर्गलोकमवाप्नोति नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥ 7 ॥
मुद्गदः शक्रलोकन्तु यमलोकन्तु माषदः ॥
यथेष्टं लोकमाप्नोति तथा विप्रास्तिलप्रदः ॥ 8 ॥
षष्टिकानां प्रदानेन लोकं नैरृतकं लभेत् ॥
सचीणचणकं दत्त्वा लोकं वारुणमाप्नुयात् ॥ 9 ॥
वायव्यञ्च मसूराणि राजमाषाणि धानदम् ॥
अन्येषां शिंबिधान्यानां दानात्स्वर्गमवाप्नुयात् ॥ 3.314.10 ॥
इक्षुमृद्वीकयोर्दानात्परं सौभाग्यमाप्नुयात् ॥
गुडप्रदस्तथारोग्यं सितादः काममीप्सितम् ॥ 11 ॥
फाणितस्य प्रदानेन परां तृप्तिमवाप्नुयात् ॥
खण्डप्रदश्च सौभाग्यं सर्वान्कामान्मधुप्रदः ॥ 12 ॥
3.63.m:
By the gift of barley, a man is glorified in the world of Śakra; / likewise, by the gift of wheat, he attains the world of the Vasus.
He who gives priyaṅgu becomes dear to the world; / he who gives śyāmāka, with him the deities are pleased.
A man intent on the gift of other bearded grains / attains the world of heaven; no doubt should be made here.
The giver of mung beans [attains] the world of Śakra, but the giver of black gram [attains] the world of Yama; / likewise, O brahmins, the giver of sesame seeds attains whatever world he desires.
By the gift of sixty-day rice, one obtains the world of Nirṛti; / having given common millet and chickpea, one attains the world of Varuṇa.
By [giving] lentils [one attains] the world of Vāyu, and by black-eyed peas that of the Bestower of Wealth; / from the gift of other pod-bearing grains one attains heaven.
From the gift of sugarcane and grapes one attains supreme good fortune; / the giver of jaggery likewise [gains] health, and the giver of white sugar his desired wish.
By giving boiled sugarcane juice one attains supreme satisfaction; / the giver of candied sugar [attains] good fortune, and the giver of honey all desires.

3.63.s:
ghṛtado jīvitaṃ dīrghaṃ cārogyaṃ tailadastathā..
sarvānkāmānavāpnoti lavaṇaṃ yaḥ prayacchati .. 13 ..
saktudastṛptimāpnoti sikatādastathā śriyam ..
akīrtitānāmanyeṣāṃ dānātsvargamavāpnuyāt .. 14 ..
pakvānnadānātphaladaṃ nṛloke śuṣkānnamuktaṃ hi tadāpya yasmāt..
yajanti yajñaiḥ satataṃ dvijendrāstasmācca tatpuṇyatamaṃ pradiṣṭam .. 15 ..
3.315
.. haṃsa uvāca ..
sarveṣāmeva dānānāmannadānaṃ viśiṣyate ..
annadānātparaṃ dānaṃ na bhūtaṃ na bhaviṣyati ..1..
nātra pātraparīkṣā syānna kālaniyamastathā ..
na ca deśaḥ parīkṣyo'tra deyamannaṃ sadaiva tat..2..
śvabhyaśca śvapacebhyaśca patitebhyastathaiva ca ..
krimikīṭapataṅgānāṃ deyamannaṃ sadaiva tu ..3..
annaṃ hi jīvitaṃ loke prāṇāścānnanibandhanāḥ ..
annadaḥ prāṇado loke sarvadaśca tathānnadaḥ .. 4..
3.63.d:
घृतदो जीवितं दीर्घं चारोग्यं तैलदस्तथा॥
सर्वान्कामानवाप्नोति लवणं यः प्रयच्छति ॥ 13 ॥
सक्तुदस्तृप्तिमाप्नोति सिकतादस्तथा श्रियम् ॥
अकीर्तितानामन्येषां दानात्स्वर्गमवाप्नुयात् ॥ 14 ॥
पक्वान्नदानात्फलदं नृलोके शुष्कान्नमुक्तं हि तदाप्य यस्मात्॥
यजन्ति यज्ञैः सततं द्विजेन्द्रास्तस्माच्च तत्पुण्यतमं प्रदिष्टम् ॥ 15 ॥
3.315
॥ हंस उवाच ॥
सर्वेषामेव दानानामन्नदानं विशिष्यते ॥
अन्नदानात्परं दानं न भूतं न भविष्यति ॥1॥
नात्र पात्रपरीक्षा स्यान्न कालनियमस्तथा ॥
न च देशः परीक्ष्योऽत्र देयमन्नं सदैव तत्॥2॥
श्वभ्यश्च श्वपचेभ्यश्च पतितेभ्यस्तथैव च ॥
क्रिमिकीटपतङ्गानां देयमन्नं सदैव तु ॥3॥
अन्नं हि जीवितं लोके प्राणाश्चान्ननिबन्धनाः ॥
अन्नदः प्राणदो लोके सर्वदश्च तथान्नदः ॥ 4॥
3.63.m:
The giver of ghee [attains] long life, and the giver of oil likewise health; / he who gives salt obtains all desires.
The giver of roasted barley flour obtains satisfaction, and the giver of sand-sugar likewise prosperity; / from the gift of others not mentioned one attains heaven.
In the world of mortals, dry grain is said to bring greater fruit than the gift of cooked food; for having received it, / foremost twice-born continually sacrifice with sacrifices; therefore it is declared most meritorious.
3.315
Haṃsa said:
Among all gifts, the gift of food is pre-eminent; / no gift has ever been superior to the gift of food, nor will there ever be.
Here there should be no examination of the recipient, nor a rule of time, / nor is place to be examined here; food is always to be given.
To dogs, outcasts, and likewise to fallen outcasts, / and to worms, insects, and winged creatures, food is always to be given.
For food is life in this world, and the vital breaths are bound to food; / in this world the giver of food is the giver of life, and thus the giver of food gives all.

3.63.s:
bhuktvā tathā ca yasyānnaṃ santatiḥ syāddvijottamāḥ ..
jñātavyaṃ brāhmaṇaśreṣṭhā yasyānnaṃ tasya santatiḥ..5..
dātavyaṃ sarvavarṇebhyo bhoktavyaṃ brāhmaṇasya ca ..
yasyānnenodarasthena brāhmaṇo mriyate dvijāḥ ..6..
tāntu yonimavāpnoti nātra kāryā vicāraṇā ..
bhakṣyadaḥ svargamāpnoti śakralokantu bhojyadaḥ .. 7 ..
lehyadopsarasāṃ lokaṃ vasūnāmapi coṣyadaḥ ..
vāruṇaṃ lokamāpnoti tathā pānaprado naraḥ .. 8 ..
pānakāni sugandhīni śītalāni prayacchataḥ ..
sarvakāmasamṛddhaḥ syānnātra kāryā vicāraṇā .. 9 ..
paramānnapradānena tṛptirbhavati śāśvatī ..
pipāsamāno mriyate gavāṃ loke mahīyate ..3.315.10..
yo dadyādaparikliṣṭamannamadhvani vartate ..
śrāntāyādṛṣṭapūrvāya tasya puṇya phalaṃ mahat .. 11 ..
sahasrapariveṣyantu narakaṃ sa na gacchati ..
vimānenārkavarṇena svargaloke mahīyate .. 12..
3.63.d:
भुक्त्वा तथा च यस्यान्नं सन्ततिः स्याद्द्विजोत्तमाः ॥
ज्ञातव्यं ब्राह्मणश्रेष्ठा यस्यान्नं तस्य सन्ततिः॥5॥
दातव्यं सर्ववर्णेभ्यो भोक्तव्यं ब्राह्मणस्य च ॥
यस्यान्नेनोदरस्थेन ब्राह्मणो म्रियते द्विजाः ॥6॥
तान्तु योनिमवाप्नोति नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥
भक्ष्यदः स्वर्गमाप्नोति शक्रलोकन्तु भोज्यदः ॥ 7 ॥
लेह्यदोप्सरसां लोकं वसूनामपि चोष्यदः ॥
वारुणं लोकमाप्नोति तथा पानप्रदो नरः ॥ 8 ॥
पानकानि सुगन्धीनि शीतलानि प्रयच्छतः ॥
सर्वकामसमृद्धः स्यान्नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥ 9 ॥
परमान्नप्रदानेन तृप्तिर्भवति शाश्वती ॥
पिपासमानो म्रियते गवां लोके महीयते ॥3.315.10॥
यो दद्यादपरिक्लिष्टमन्नमध्वनि वर्तते ॥
श्रान्तायादृष्टपूर्वाय तस्य पुण्य फलं महत् ॥ 11 ॥
सहस्रपरिवेष्यन्तु नरकं स न गच्छति ॥
विमानेनार्कवर्णेन स्वर्गलोके महीयते ॥ 12॥
3.63.m:
And when offspring are born to one who has eaten another's food, O best of the twice-born, / it should be understood, O foremost brahmins, that the offspring belongs to him whose food it was.
It should be given to all classes, and [food] of a brahmin should be eaten; / O twice-born, if a brahmin dies with a man's food inside his belly,
he attains that very womb [of the giver's class]; no doubt should be entertained on this matter. / The giver of solid food attains heaven, and the giver of cooked dishes the world of Śakra.
The giver of lickable food [attains] the world of the Apsarases, and the giver of suckable food that of the Vasus; / likewise, the man who gives drinks attains the world of Varuṇa.
For one who offers fragrant, cool drinks, / there will be abundance in all desires; no doubt should be entertained on this matter.
By giving milk-rice pudding there is eternal satisfaction; / if one dies while wishing to drink, he is glorified in the world of cows.
He who gives unstinted food on the road / to a weary person never seen before—great is the fruit of his merit.
Even if he has served food a thousand times [to sinners], he does not go to hell; / in an aerial chariot shining like the sun, he is glorified in heaven.

3.63.s:
apahanyāttathā viprā ekasyārttasya yatkṣudhā ..
tenāsau karmaṇā pretya mahatphalamupāśnute..13..
yadyadiṣṭatamaṃ loke yaścāsya dayitaṃ gṛhe..
tattadguṇavate deyaṃ tadevākṣayyamicchatā.. 14 ..
dānānyanekāni phalañca teṣāṃ bahuprakāraṃ puruṣaḥ samīkṣya ..
śraddhānvito brāhmaṇasātprakuryādbhūyastadevāptamanā nṛloke .. 15 ..
3.63.d:
अपहन्यात्तथा विप्रा एकस्यार्त्तस्य यत्क्षुधा ॥
तेनासौ कर्मणा प्रेत्य महत्फलमुपाश्नुते॥13॥
यद्यदिष्टतमं लोके यश्चास्य दयितं गृहे॥
तत्तद्गुणवते देयं तदेवाक्षय्यमिच्छता॥ 14 ॥
दानान्यनेकानि फलञ्च तेषां बहुप्रकारं पुरुषः समीक्ष्य ॥
श्रद्धान्वितो ब्राह्मणसात्प्रकुर्याद्भूयस्तदेवाप्तमना नृलोके ॥ 15 ॥
3.63.m:
Likewise, O brahmins, if one removes the hunger of even a single afflicted person, / by that deed he enjoys a great fruit after death.
Whatever is most desirable in the world, and whatever is dear to him in his house, / that very thing should be given to a virtuous person by one desiring it to become imperishable.
Having observed the manifold gifts and their fruit of many kinds, / a man endowed with faith should bestow them upon brahmins, and, contented in mind, he shall obtain the same repeatedly in the human world.

3.64.s:
3.316
.. ṛṣaya ūcuḥ ..
kasya dānasya kaḥ pātraṃ tadvadasva mahāmate ..
kasmindeśe tathā kāle kiñcid dattaṃ mahāphalam .. 1 ..
3.64.d:
3.316
॥ ऋषय ऊचुः ॥
कस्य दानस्य कः पात्रं तद्वदस्व महामते ॥
कस्मिन्देशे तथा काले किञ्चिद् दत्तं महाफलम् ॥ 1 ॥
3.64.m:
3.316
The sages said:
Who is the worthy recipient for which gift? Tell that, O great-minded one! / In which place and at what time does something given yield great fruit?

3.64.s:
.. haṃsa uvāca .. ..
na dānaṃ yaśase dadyānna dadyānnopakāriṇe ..
na nṛtyagītaśīlebhyo nāstikebhyaśca dhārmikaḥ .. 2 ..
3.64.d:
॥ हंस उवाच ॥ ॥
न दानं यशसे दद्यान्न दद्यान्नोपकारिणे ॥
न नृत्यगीतशीलेभ्यो नास्तिकेभ्यश्च धार्मिकः ॥ 2 ॥
3.64.m:
Haṃsa said:
A righteous person should not give a gift for fame, nor to one who has not benefited him, / nor to those who indulge in dance and song, nor to atheists.

3.64.s:
pāpaśīle na dātavyaṃ kadācidapi kiñcana ..
pāpaśīle tu yaddattaṃ taddātudoṣamāvahet .. 3 ..
3.64.d:
पापशीले न दातव्यं कदाचिदपि किञ्चन ॥
पापशीले तु यद्दत्तं तद्दातुदोषमावहेत् ॥ 3 ॥
3.64.m: Nothing should ever be given to a person of sinful conduct; / whatever is given to a person of sinful conduct brings demerit to the giver.

3.64.s:
dhanadastena pāpena śīghrameveha yujyate ..
tasmātprāpya dhanaṃ puṇyaṃ puṇyaśīlaṃ samācaret .. 4 ..
3.64.d:
धनदस्तेन पापेन शीघ्रमेवेह युज्यते ॥
तस्मात्प्राप्य धनं पुण्यं पुण्यशीलं समाचरेत् ॥ 4 ॥
3.64.m: The giver of wealth is soon joined with that sin here; / therefore, having obtained wealth, he should act virtuously through righteous conduct.

3.64.s:
dhanadastena puṇyena yogamāpnotyasaṃśayam ..
annadānena kartavyaṃ pātrāvekṣaṇamaṇvapi .. 5 ..
3.64.d:
धनदस्तेन पुण्येन योगमाप्नोत्यसंशयम् ॥
अन्नदानेन कर्तव्यं पात्रावेक्षणमण्वपि ॥ 5 ॥
3.64.m: By that merit the giver of wealth attains union [with the divine] without doubt. / In the gift of food, no scrutiny whatsoever of the recipient should be made.

3.64.s:
annaṃ sarvatra dātavyaṃ dharmakāmena vai dvijāḥ ..
sadoṣepi tu nirdoṣaṃ saguṇetiguṇāvaham .. 6 ..
3.64.d:
अन्नं सर्वत्र दातव्यं धर्मकामेन वै द्विजाः ॥
सदोषेपि तु निर्दोषं सगुणेतिगुणावहम् ॥ 6 ॥
3.64.m: Food is to be given everywhere by one desiring dharma, O twice-born; / even if [given] to a flawed person it is faultless, and if to a virtuous one, it brings manifold virtue.

3.64.s:
tasmātsarvaprayatnena deyamannaṃ sadaiva tu ..
vidyādhyayanasaktānāmannadānaṃ mahāphalam .. 7 ..
3.64.d:
तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन देयमन्नं सदैव तु ॥
विद्याध्ययनसक्तानामन्नदानं महाफलम् ॥ 7 ॥
3.64.m: Therefore, by every effort, food should always be given; / the gift of food to those intent on the study of sacred knowledge brings great fruit.

3.64.s:
śubhānāmapyathānyeṣāṃ karmaṇāṃ dvijapuṅgavāḥ ..
yasyānnamupayuñjāno naraḥ karmāṇi sādhayet .. 8 ..
3.64.d:
शुभानामप्यथान्येषां कर्मणां द्विजपुङ्गवाः ॥
यस्यान्नमुपयुञ्जानो नरः कर्माणि साधयेत् ॥ 8 ॥
3.64.m: And likewise for other auspicious deeds, O foremost twice-born; / eating whose food a man accomplishes deeds,

3.64.s:
karma sādhayataḥ puṇyamannadātā tathāśnute ..
dattvā nṛpatibhītānāṃ dhanināñca tathā dhanam .. 9 ..
3.64.d:
कर्म साधयतः पुण्यमन्नदाता तथाश्नुते ॥
दत्त्वा नृपतिभीतानां धनिनाञ्च तथा धनम् ॥ 9 ॥
3.64.m: the giver of food partakes in the merit of him who accomplishes the deed. / By giving wealth to those terrified of the king and to wealthy persons,

3.64.s:
taskarebhyaśca bhītānāṃ phalamakṣayamaśnute ..
yiyakṣatā tathā dattaṃ vyasane haṃtumicchatā .. 3.316.10 ..
3.64.d:
तस्करेभ्यश्च भीतानां फलमक्षयमश्नुते ॥
यियक्षता तथा दत्तं व्यसने हंतुमिच्छता ॥ 3.316.10 ॥
3.64.m: and to those terrified of thieves, one enjoys imperishable fruit. / Likewise, what is given to one wishing to sacrifice or wishing to avert calamity,

3.64.s:
duḥkhānvitānāṃ dīnānāñcākṣayaṃ tatprakīrtitam ..
vivāhamekhalābandhapratiṣṭhādiṣu karmasu ..11..
3.64.d:
दुःखान्वितानां दीनानाञ्चाक्षयं तत्प्रकीर्तितम् ॥
विवाहमेखलाबन्धप्रतिष्ठादिषु कर्मसु ॥11॥
3.64.m: or to those afflicted with sorrow and wretched, is proclaimed imperishable; / in ceremonies such as marriage, investiture of the girdle, and consecration,

3.64.s:
āpanneṣu ca yaddattaṃ tadakṣayyamudāhṛtam ..
yajñopakaraṇaṃ dravyaṃ kṣattriye dvijapuṅgavāḥ .. 12 ..
3.64.d:
आपन्नेषु च यद्दत्तं तदक्षय्यमुदाहृतम् ॥
यज्ञोपकरणं द्रव्यं क्षत्त्रिये द्विजपुङ्गवाः ॥ 12 ॥
3.64.m: and whatever is given to those in distress, that is declared imperishable. / An article serving as sacrificial equipment should be given to a kṣatriya, O foremost twice-born,

3.64.s:
puṇyopayogi tadvaiśye śūdre śilpopajīvinam ..
yasyopayogi yaddravyaṃ deyaṃ tasyaiva tadbhavet .. 13 ..
3.64.d:
पुण्योपयोगि तद्वैश्ये शूद्रे शिल्पोपजीविनम् ॥
यस्योपयोगि यद्द्रव्यं देयं तस्यैव तद्भवेत् ॥ 13 ॥
3.64.m: what is useful for merit to a vaiśya, and what serves his craft to a śūdra living by craftsmanship; / whatever article is useful to someone should be given to that very person.

3.64.s:
yenayena ca bhāṇḍena yasya vṛttirudāhṛtā ..
tattu tasyaiva dātavyaṃ puṇyakāmena dhīmatā .. 14 ..
3.64.d:
येनयेन च भाण्डेन यस्य वृत्तिरुदाहृता ॥
तत्तु तस्यैव दातव्यं पुण्यकामेन धीमता ॥ 14 ॥
3.64.m: Whatever vessel or tool is declared to be the livelihood of someone, / that should be given to him alone by a wise person desiring merit.

3.64.s:
daṇḍaṃ kṛṣṇājinañcaiva tathā viprāḥ kamaṇḍalum ..
cīraṃ puṇyamavāpnoti dattvaitāṃ brahmacāriṇe .. 15 ..
3.64.d:
दण्डं कृष्णाजिनञ्चैव तथा विप्राः कमण्डलुम् ॥
चीरं पुण्यमवाप्नोति दत्त्वैतां ब्रह्मचारिणे ॥ 15 ॥
3.64.m: Staff, black antelope skin, and water pot, O brahmins, / and bark garments—by giving these to a celibate student, one attains merit.

3.64.s:
vastraṃ śayyāsanaṃ dhānyaṃ dravyaṃ veśma paricchadam ..
gṛhasthāya tu taddattaṃ jñeyaṃ bahuphalaṃ sadā .. 16 ..
3.64.d:
वस्त्रं शय्यासनं धान्यं द्रव्यं वेश्म परिच्छदम् ॥
गृहस्थाय तु तद्दत्तं ज्ञेयं बहुफलं सदा ॥ 16 ॥
3.64.m: Cloth, a bed and seat, grain, goods, a house, and household furnishings— / what is given of these to a householder is to be known as always bringing great fruit.

3.64.s:
nīvāravalkalaṃ śākaṃ phalamūlaṃ ca gorasam ..
vānaprasthāya taddattamanantaṃ parikīrtitam .. 17 ..
3.64.d:
नीवारवल्कलं शाकं फलमूलं च गोरसम् ॥
वानप्रस्थाय तद्दत्तमनन्तं परिकीर्तितम् ॥ 17 ॥
3.64.m: Wild rice, bark garments, vegetables, fruit, roots, and cow's milk— / what is given of these to a forest-dweller is proclaimed to be endless.

3.64.s:
bhikṣāpradānaṃ yataye pātradānaṃ tathā hitam ..
saubhāgyadravya tāmbūlaraktavastrādikaṃ striyaḥ .. 18 ..
3.64.d:
भिक्षाप्रदानं यतये पात्रदानं तथा हितम् ॥
सौभाग्यद्रव्य ताम्बूलरक्तवस्त्रादिकं स्त्रियः ॥ 18 ॥
3.64.m: The giving of alms is beneficial for an ascetic, as is the gift of a begging bowl; / articles of auspiciousness, betel, red garments, and the like for a woman.

3.64.s:
strīṇāṃ pradānaṃ dātavyaṃ bhartṛhaste tu nānyathā ..
proktaṃ saṃgrahaṇaṃ hyetadguptaṃ bhartuḥ prayacchataḥ .. 19 ..
3.64.d:
स्त्रीणां प्रदानं दातव्यं भर्तृहस्ते तु नान्यथा ॥
प्रोक्तं संग्रहणं ह्येतद्गुप्तं भर्तुः प्रयच्छतः ॥ 19 ॥
3.64.m: A gift for women is to be given into the hand of her husband, not otherwise; / for giving it secretly from the husband is declared to be adultery.

3.64.s:
annaṃ pratiśrayaṃ cobhau pānthe dattaṃ mahāphalam ..
vivāhādikriyākāle tatkriyāsiddhikārakam .. 3.316.20 ..
3.64.d:
अन्नं प्रतिश्रयं चोभौ पान्थे दत्तं महाफलम् ॥
विवाहादिक्रियाकाले तत्क्रियासिद्धिकारकम् ॥ 3.316.20 ॥
3.64.m: Food and shelter, both given to a traveller, bear great fruit. / At the time of rites such as marriage, it brings about the accomplishment of that rite.

3.64.s:
yaḥ prayacchati dharmajñāḥ sośvamedhamavāpnuyāt..
āturebhyo dhanaṃ dattvā dānaṃ bahuphalaṃ labhet .. 21 ..
3.64.d:
यः प्रयच्छति धर्मज्ञाः सोश्वमेधमवाप्नुयात्॥
आतुरेभ्यो धनं दत्त्वा दानं बहुफलं लभेत् ॥ 21 ॥
3.64.m: He who gives [them], O knowers of dharma, obtains an horse sacrifice. / Giving wealth to the sick, one obtains a gift of manifold fruit.

3.64.s:
bāle krīḍanakaṃ dattvā miṣṭamannaṃ tathaiva ca ..
phalaṃ manoharaṃ vāpi agniṣṭomaphalaṃ labhet ..22 ..
3.64.d:
बाले क्रीडनकं दत्त्वा मिष्टमन्नं तथैव च ॥
फलं मनोहरं वापि अग्निष्टोमफलं लभेत् ॥22 ॥
3.64.m: Giving a toy to a child, and sweet food as well, / or lovely fruit, one obtains the fruit of an Agniṣṭoma sacrifice.

3.64.s:
miṣṭānnaṃ mānavo dattvā miṣṭānnāni tu kāṃkṣatām..
akṣayaṃ phalamāpnoti svargalokaṃ ca gacchati .. 23 ..
3.64.d:
मिष्टान्नं मानवो दत्त्वा मिष्टान्नानि तु कांक्षताम्॥
अक्षयं फलमाप्नोति स्वर्गलोकं च गच्छति ॥ 23 ॥
3.64.m: A man, giving sweet food to those who long for sweet foods, / attains inexhaustible fruit and goes to heaven.

3.64.s:
śrīvihīne tathā dattvā bhojanaṃ dvijasattamāḥ ..
vastraṃ śubhaṃ vā dharmajñāḥ puṇyaṃ mahadupāśnute .. 24 ..
3.64.d:
श्रीविहीने तथा दत्त्वा भोजनं द्विजसत्तमाः ॥
वस्त्रं शुभं वा धर्मज्ञाः पुण्यं महदुपाश्नुते ॥ 24 ॥
3.64.m: Likewise, giving a meal to one bereft of fortune, O best of the twice-born, / or beautiful clothing, O knowers of dharma, he partakes of great merit.

3.64.s:
kṛpāsthānaparo viprā vidyutaḥ puruṣaḥ śriyā ..
tasyānukampā katarvyā satāṃ vartmani tiṣṭhataḥ .. 25 ..
3.64.d:
कृपास्थानपरो विप्रा विद्युतः पुरुषः श्रिया ॥
तस्यानुकम्पा कतर्व्या सतां वर्त्मनि तिष्ठतः ॥ 25 ॥
3.64.m: A man who is fallen from fortune, O brahmins, is a supreme object of pity. / Compassion should be shown to him by one who walks the path of the good.

3.64.s:
kārye samudyamaṃ kṛtvā pareṣāṃ samupasthite ..
akṣayaṃ phalamāpnoti nātra kāryā vicāraṇā ..26 ..
3.64.d:
कार्ये समुद्यमं कृत्वा परेषां समुपस्थिते ॥
अक्षयं फलमाप्नोति नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥26 ॥
3.64.m: Exerting oneself in an affair of others that has arisen, / one obtains inexhaustible fruit; here no doubt should be held.

3.64.s:
yavasānāṃ pradānena dhenumatsu dvijātiṣu ..
lavaṇānāñca dharmajñā phalamakṣayamaśnute ..27..
3.64.d:
यवसानां प्रदानेन धेनुमत्सु द्विजातिषु ॥
लवणानाञ्च धर्मज्ञा फलमक्षयमश्नुते ॥27॥
3.64.m: By giving fodder and salt to twice-born men / possessing cattle, O knowers of dharma, one enjoys inexhaustible fruit.

3.64.s:
prasaveṣu tadā dattaṃ vyasanānyubhaye tataḥ ..
taddānamakṣayaṃ proktaṃ puruṣasya vipaścitaḥ ..28..
3.64.d:
प्रसवेषु तदा दत्तं व्यसनान्युभये ततः ॥
तद्दानमक्षयं प्रोक्तं पुरुषस्य विपश्चितः ॥28॥
3.64.m: Given during childbirths, and then in both kinds of distress, / that gift of a wise man is declared to be inexhaustible.

3.64.s:
dattvā brāhmaṇaśārdūlā jalamātramathārthine ..
phalamakṣayamāpnoti nātra kāryā vicāraṇā ..29..
3.64.d:
दत्त्वा ब्राह्मणशार्दूला जलमात्रमथार्थिने ॥
फलमक्षयमाप्नोति नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥29॥
3.64.m: Giving merely water to a petitioner, O tigers among brahmins, / one obtains inexhaustible fruit; here no doubt should be held.

3.64.s:
kleśaṃ vinā dattamathārthine tu dānaṃ hi loke phaladaṃ niruktam ..
abhyarthitenātha tato na kāryā vimānanā tvarthijanasya śaktyā..3.316.30..
3.317
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ ..
dānaṃ bahuphalaṃ kāle yasminyatparikīrtitam ..
tattvamasmākamācakṣva tvaṃ hi sarvaviducyase .. 1..
haṃsa uvāca ..
saṃvatsare tathā dānaṃ tilasya ca mahāphalam ..
paripūrve tathā dānaṃ yavānāṃ dvijasattamāḥ .. 2 ..
iḍāpūrvennavastrāṇāṃ dhānyānāṃ cānupūrvake ..
udāsaṃvatsare dānaṃ rajatasya mahāphalam ..3..
uttare tvayane proktaṃ vastradānaṃ phalapradam ..
snānānulepanādīnāṃ vasante dvijapuṅgavāḥ..4..
pānakānāṃ tathā grīṣme chatrāṇāṃ tadanantare ..
śaradyannasya dharmajñā vastrāṇāmapi haimane..5..
vahnidānaṃ naraḥ kṛtvā sūryasyodayanaṃ prati ..
śiśire satataṃ vahniṃ tarpayitvā tathā tilaiḥ ..6 ..
3.64.d:
क्लेशं विना दत्तमथार्थिने तु दानं हि लोके फलदं निरुक्तम् ॥
अभ्यर्थितेनाथ ततो न कार्या विमानना त्वर्थिजनस्य शक्त्या॥3.316.30॥
3.317
ऋषय ऊचुः ॥
दानं बहुफलं काले यस्मिन्यत्परिकीर्तितम् ॥
तत्त्वमस्माकमाचक्ष्व त्वं हि सर्वविदुच्यसे ॥ 1॥
हंस उवाच ॥
संवत्सरे तथा दानं तिलस्य च महाफलम् ॥
परिपूर्वे तथा दानं यवानां द्विजसत्तमाः ॥ 2 ॥
इडापूर्वेन्नवस्त्राणां धान्यानां चानुपूर्वके ॥
उदासंवत्सरे दानं रजतस्य महाफलम् ॥3॥
उत्तरे त्वयने प्रोक्तं वस्त्रदानं फलप्रदम् ॥
स्नानानुलेपनादीनां वसन्ते द्विजपुङ्गवाः॥4॥
पानकानां तथा ग्रीष्मे छत्राणां तदनन्तरे ॥
शरद्यन्नस्य धर्मज्ञा वस्त्राणामपि हैमने॥5॥
वह्निदानं नरः कृत्वा सूर्यस्योदयनं प्रति ॥
शिशिरे सततं वह्निं तर्पयित्वा तथा तिलैः ॥6 ॥
3.64.m:
A gift given without distress to a supplicant is indeed declared fruitful in the world; / therefore, when asked, one should not dishonour a supplicant, according to one's capacity.
The ṛṣis said: / What gift is proclaimed as bearing great fruit at what time— / tell us that in truth, for you are called all-knowing.
Haṃsa said: / In a Saṃvatsara, the gift of sesame yields great fruit; / in a Parivatsara, likewise, the gift of barley, O best of the twice-born;
in an Iḍāvatsara, of food and garments, and in an Anuvatsara, of grains; / in an Udāvatsara, the gift of silver yields great fruit.
During the northern course [of the sun], the gift of clothing is declared to bestow fruit; / in the spring, O bulls among the twice-born, [the gift] of bathing, unguents, and the like;
likewise, in the summer, of drinks, and immediately after, of umbrellas; / in autumn, O knowers of dharma, of food, and in winter, of garments.
A man, giving fire towards the rising of the sun / and continually gratifying fire with sesame seeds in the cool season,

3.64.s:
kulmāṣaṃ saghṛtaṃ dattvā yathāśaktyā dvijātiṣu ..
kāyāgnidīptiṃ prākāśyaṃ śatrunāśañca vindati ..7..
saktūnsitākhaṇḍayutāṃstrapusorvārukānvitān ..
jalakumbhoparikṛtānakṣayaṃ phalamaśnute ..8..
madhyāhne prāvṛṣi snātaḥ satataṃ dvijapuṅgavāḥ ..
tilapradānānmāghe tu prāpyalokaṃ sa gacchati .. 9..
priyaṅguṃ phālgune dattvā priyo bhavati bhūtale ..
caitre citrāṇi vastrāṇi saubhāgyaṃ mahadaśnute..3.317.10..
apūpānāṃ pradānena vaiśākhe svargamaśnute ..
chatradānaṃ tathā jyeṣṭhe sarvānkāmānupāśnute ..
dattvā copānahau svargañcāṣāḍhe dhruvamaśnute ..11..
śrāvaṇe vastradānasya kīrtitaṃ sumahatphalam ..
proṣṭhapāde tathā māsi pradānātphāṇitasya ca .. 12 ..
āśvine ghṛtadānena rūpavānabhi jāyate ..
kārtike dīpadānena sarvatraujasyamaśnuyāt .. 13 ..
3.64.d:
कुल्माषं सघृतं दत्त्वा यथाशक्त्या द्विजातिषु ॥
कायाग्निदीप्तिं प्राकाश्यं शत्रुनाशञ्च विन्दति ॥7॥
सक्तून्सिताखण्डयुतांस्त्रपुसोर्वारुकान्वितान् ॥
जलकुम्भोपरिकृतानक्षयं फलमश्नुते ॥8॥
मध्याह्ने प्रावृषि स्नातः सततं द्विजपुङ्गवाः ॥
तिलप्रदानान्माघे तु प्राप्यलोकं स गच्छति ॥ 9॥
प्रियङ्गुं फाल्गुने दत्त्वा प्रियो भवति भूतले ॥
चैत्रे चित्राणि वस्त्राणि सौभाग्यं महदश्नुते॥3.317.10॥
अपूपानां प्रदानेन वैशाखे स्वर्गमश्नुते ॥
छत्रदानं तथा ज्येष्ठे सर्वान्कामानुपाश्नुते ॥
दत्त्वा चोपानहौ स्वर्गञ्चाषाढे ध्रुवमश्नुते ॥11॥
श्रावणे वस्त्रदानस्य कीर्तितं सुमहत्फलम् ॥
प्रोष्ठपादे तथा मासि प्रदानात्फाणितस्य च ॥ 12 ॥
आश्विने घृतदानेन रूपवानभि जायते ॥
कार्तिके दीपदानेन सर्वत्रौजस्यमश्नुयात् ॥ 13 ॥
3.64.m:
and giving gruel with clarified butter according to his capacity to twice-born men, / gains brightness of the bodily fire, radiance, and the destruction of enemies.
Roasted grain flour mixed with pieces of white sugar, accompanied by cucumbers and gourds, / placed upon a water pot—he enjoys inexhaustible fruit.
Having bathed at midday continually during the rainy season, O bulls among the twice-born, / or by giving sesame seeds in Māgha, he goes having reached [that] world.
Giving panic seed in Phālguna, he becomes beloved on the surface of the earth; / [giving] multicoloured clothes in Caitra, he enjoys great good fortune.
By giving sweet cakes in Vaiśākha, he enjoys heaven; / likewise, by giving an umbrella in Jyeṣṭha, he obtains all desires; / and giving shoes in Āṣāḍha, he surely enjoys heaven.
A very great fruit is celebrated for the gift of clothing in Śrāvaṇa; / likewise, from the gift of treacle in the month of Proṣṭhapada;
by giving clarified butter in Āśvina, he is born handsome; / by giving a lamp in Kārtika, he would attain vigour everywhere.

3.64.s:
lavaṇaṃ mārgaśīrṣe tu dattvā saubhāgyamaśnute ..
pauṣe kanakadānena parāṃ puṣṭiṃ tathaiva ca .. 14 ..
puṣpāṇāṃ ca site pakṣe dānaṃ lakṣmīkaraṃ smṛtam ..
phalānāṃ ca tathā dānaṃ kṛṣṇapakṣe mahāphalam..15..
lavaṇājyaguḍopetamapūpaṃ sūryavāsare ..
sahiraṇyaṃ naro dattvā na rogaistvabhibhūyate ..16 ..
evaṃvidhaṃ cendudine dadatsaubhāgyamāpnuyāt ..
kāṣṭhadānaṃ bhaumadine śatrunāśamavāpnuyāt .. 17 ..
bodhe krīḍanakānāñca dānaṃ bāleṣu śasyate ..
jīvāhni vastradānena parāṃ puṣṭiṃ samaśnute .. 16 ..
sarvatra ratimāpnoti śukre dattvā ratistriyam ..
abhyaṅgaṃ sauradivase dattvā jīvitamāpnuyāt ..19..
kṛttikāsu suvarṇasya dānaṃ bahuphalaṃ smṛtam ..
raktavastrasya rohiṇyāṃ saumyabhe lavaṇasya ca.3.317.20..
3.64.d:
लवणं मार्गशीर्षे तु दत्त्वा सौभाग्यमश्नुते ॥
पौषे कनकदानेन परां पुष्टिं तथैव च ॥ 14 ॥
पुष्पाणां च सिते पक्षे दानं लक्ष्मीकरं स्मृतम् ॥
फलानां च तथा दानं कृष्णपक्षे महाफलम्॥15॥
लवणाज्यगुडोपेतमपूपं सूर्यवासरे ॥
सहिरण्यं नरो दत्त्वा न रोगैस्त्वभिभूयते ॥16 ॥
एवंविधं चेन्दुदिने ददत्सौभाग्यमाप्नुयात् ॥
काष्ठदानं भौमदिने शत्रुनाशमवाप्नुयात् ॥ 17 ॥
बोधे क्रीडनकानाञ्च दानं बालेषु शस्यते ॥
जीवाह्नि वस्त्रदानेन परां पुष्टिं समश्नुते ॥ 16 ॥
सर्वत्र रतिमाप्नोति शुक्रे दत्त्वा रतिस्त्रियम् ॥
अभ्यङ्गं सौरदिवसे दत्त्वा जीवितमाप्नुयात् ॥19॥
कृत्तिकासु सुवर्णस्य दानं बहुफलं स्मृतम् ॥
रक्तवस्त्रस्य रोहिण्यां सौम्यभे लवणस्य च.3.317.20॥
3.64.m:
Giving salt in Mārgaśīrṣa, he enjoys good fortune; / in Pauṣa, by the gift of gold, [he attains] supreme nourishment likewise.
The gift of flowers in the bright fortnight is traditionally held to produce prosperity; / and the gift of fruits in the dark fortnight bears great fruit.
Giving on Sunday a cake provided with salt, clarified butter, and molasses, / along with gold, a man is not overcome by diseases.
Giving the same kind on Monday, he would obtain good fortune; / giving firewood on Tuesday, he would obtain the destruction of enemies.
The gift of toys to children is praised on Wednesday; / on Thursday, by the gift of clothing, he fully enjoys supreme nourishment.
He attains pleasure everywhere by giving an attractive woman on Friday; / giving an oil-bath on Saturday, he would obtain long life.
Under Kṛttikā, the gift of gold is remembered to bear much fruit; / of red cloth under Rohiṇī, and of salt under the constellation of Soma;

3.64.s:
kṛsarasya tathārdrāyāṃ cāditye rajatasya ca ..
ghṛtasya ca tathā puṣye gandhānāmatha sarpabhe .. 21 ..
tilānāñca maghāyoge priyaṅgorbhagadaivate ..
āryamṇe cāpyapūpānāṃ sāvitre pāyasasya ca .. 22 ..

aindrāgne caiva lohānāṃ maitre mālyaphalasya ca ..23..

himasya madhuyuktasya dānamāpye mahāphalam .. 24 ..

dhānyasya vāsave viprā vāruṇe cauṣadhasya ca ..25..
ajapāde ca bījānāṃ sasyānāṃ tadanantare ..
gorasānāṃ tathā pauṣṇe snānānāmatha cāśvine .. .. 26 ..

3.64.d:
कृसरस्य तथार्द्रायां चादित्ये रजतस्य च ॥
घृतस्य च तथा पुष्ये गन्धानामथ सर्पभे ॥ 21 ॥
तिलानाञ्च मघायोगे प्रियङ्गोर्भगदैवते ॥
आर्यम्णे चाप्यपूपानां सावित्रे पायसस्य च ॥ 22 ॥
चित्रायां चित्रवस्त्राणां सक्तूनां वायुदैवते ॥
ऐन्द्राग्ने चैव लोहानां मैत्रे माल्यफलस्य च ॥23॥
छत्रस्य च तथा शाके मूले मूलफलस्य च ॥
हिमस्य मधुयुक्तस्य दानमाप्ये महाफलम् ॥ 24 ॥
विश्वेश्वरेन्नदानस्य श्रवणे वसनस्य च ॥
धान्यस्य वासवे विप्रा वारुणे चौषधस्य च ॥25॥
अजपादे च बीजानां सस्यानां तदनन्तरे ॥
गोरसानां तथा पौष्णे स्नानानामथ चाश्विने ॥ ॥ 26 ॥
तिलानाञ्च तथा दानं भरणीषु महाफलम् ॥
प्रतिपद्यथ पुष्पाणां द्वितीयायां घृतस्य च ॥ 27 ॥

3.64.s:
tṛtīyāyāṃ tu vastrāṇāṃ caturthyāṃ kanakasya tu ..
pañcamyāntu phalānāṃ vai ṣaṣṭhyāṃ snānasya mānadāḥ ..28..
saptamyāṃ cāpyapūpānāmaṣṭamyāñca guḍasya ca ..
kulmāṣasya navamyāntu daśamyāṃ rajatasya ca .. 29 ..
ekādaśyāṃ suvarṇasya dvādaśyāṃ vasanasya ca ..
trayodaśyāṃ sugandhānāṃ sitāyāstadanantaram .. 3.317.30 ..
3.64.d:
तृतीयायां तु वस्त्राणां चतुर्थ्यां कनकस्य तु ॥
पञ्चम्यान्तु फलानां वै षष्ठ्यां स्नानस्य मानदाः ॥28॥
सप्तम्यां चाप्यपूपानामष्टम्याञ्च गुडस्य च ॥
कुल्माषस्य नवम्यान्तु दशम्यां रजतस्य च ॥ 29 ॥
एकादश्यां सुवर्णस्य द्वादश्यां वसनस्य च ॥
त्रयोदश्यां सुगन्धानां सितायास्तदनन्तरम् ॥ 3.317.30 ॥

3.64.s:
dānañca paramānnasya pañcadaśyāṃ mahāphalam ..
vaiśākhaśuklapakṣe tu tṛtīyāyāṃ dvijottamāḥ .. 31 ..
3.64.d:
दानञ्च परमान्नस्य पञ्चदश्यां महाफलम् ॥
वैशाखशुक्लपक्षे तु तृतीयायां द्विजोत्तमाः ॥ 31 ॥
3.64.m: and on the fifteenth, the gift of payasa yields great fruit. / On the third [day] in the bright fortnight of Vaiśākha, O best of the twice-born,

3.64.s:
yaddadāti naraśreṣṭhāstattadakṣayyamaśnute ..
viśeṣeṇa tathā dānamakṣatānāṃ mahāphalam .. 32 ..
3.64.d:
यद्ददाति नरश्रेष्ठास्तत्तदक्षय्यमश्नुते ॥
विशेषेण तथा दानमक्षतानां महाफलम् ॥ 32 ॥
3.64.m: Whatever [a man] gives, O best of men, he enjoys that as imperishable; / so especially the gift of unbroken rice grains yields great fruit.

3.64.s:
māghe śravaṇasaṃyuktā yuktā syāddvādaśī yadā ..
tiladānaṃ mahatpuṇyaṃ vināpi śravaṇena tu .. 33 ..
3.64.d:
माघे श्रवणसंयुक्ता युक्ता स्याद्द्वादशी यदा ॥
तिलदानं महत्पुण्यं विनापि श्रवणेन तु ॥ 33 ॥
3.64.m: When in the month of Māgha the twelfth day coincides with Śravaṇa, / the gift of sesame seeds brings great religious merit, and even without [the asterism of] Śravaṇa as well.

3.64.s:
māsi bhādrapade śukle navamyāṃ dvijapuṅgavāḥ ..
godhūmabhaktāṃ saguḍāṃ dattvā puṇyamavāpnuyāt .. 34 ..
3.64.d:
मासि भाद्रपदे शुक्ले नवम्यां द्विजपुङ्गवाः ॥
गोधूमभक्तां सगुडां दत्त्वा पुण्यमवाप्नुयात् ॥ 34 ॥
3.64.m: In the bright fortnight of the month of Bhādrapada, on the ninth day, O foremost of the twice-born, / having given boiled wheat with molasses, one obtains religious merit.

3.64.s:
etāni dānāni ca kālayoge proktāni puṇyāni mayā dvijendrāḥ ..
deyāni sarvāṇi vināpi yogādyogena puṇyaṃ tvadhikaṃ niruktam .. 35 ..
3.64.d:
एतानि दानानि च कालयोगे प्रोक्तानि पुण्यानि मया द्विजेन्द्राः ॥
देयानि सर्वाणि विनापि योगाद्योगेन पुण्यं त्वधिकं निरुक्तम् ॥ 35 ॥
3.64.m: These meritorious gifts have been explained by me according to temporal conjunction, O chiefs of the twice-born; / they should all be given even without the conjunction, but the merit is declared to be greater by the conjunction.

ṛṣaya ūcuḥ ..
vrataṃ nakṣatrasatrākhyaṃ sadānaṃ kathayasva naḥ ..

haṃsa uvāca ..

3.64.d:
इति श्रीविष्णुधर्मोत्तरे तृ0 ख0 मार्कण्डेयवज्रसंवादे मुनीन्प्रति हंसगीतासु कालयोगे दानविधिवर्णनो नाम सप्तदशाधिकत्रिशततमोऽध्यायः॥। 317 ॥
3.318
ऋषय ऊचुः ॥
व्रतं नक्षत्रसत्राख्यं सदानं कथयस्व नः ॥
सर्वधर्मभृतां श्रेष्ठ प्रत्यक्षामलदर्शन ॥ 1 ॥
हंस उवाच ॥
कृत्तिकासु महाभागाः पायसेन स सर्पिषा ॥
संतर्प्य ब्राह्मणान्साधूम्̐ल्लोकान्प्राप्नोत्यनुत्तमान् ॥ 2 ॥
रोहिण्यां प्रथितैर्मासैर्माषैरन्नेन सर्पिषा ॥
पयोनुपानं दातव्यं चानृणार्थं द्विजातये ॥ 3 ॥
दोग्ध्रीं दत्त्वा सवत्सां तु नक्षत्रे सोमदैवते ॥
गच्छेत मानुषाम्̐ल्लोकान्स्वर्गवासमनुत्तमम् ॥ 4 ॥
आर्द्रायां कृसरं दत्त्वा तैलमिश्रमुपोषितः ॥
नरस्तरति दुर्गाणि क्षुरधारांस्तु पर्वतान् ॥ 5 ॥
पूपान्पुनर्वसौ दत्त्वा तथैवान्नञ्च शोभनम् ॥
यशस्वी रूपसंपन्नो बह्वन्नो जायते कुले ॥ 6 ॥
3.64.m:
Thus ends the three hundred and seventeenth chapter, entitled 'Description of the Rule of Giving at Auspicious Times', in the Haṃsagītā addressed to the sages, in the dialogue between Mārkaṇḍeya and Vajra, in the third book of the illustrious Viṣṇudharmottara.
The sages said: / Tell us the observance called Nakṣatrasattra together with gifts, / O foremost of all upholders of dharma, whose clear vision is manifest.
Haṃsa said: / During Kṛttikā, O fortunate ones, having satisfied virtuous brahmins / with milk-rice and clarified butter, one attains unsurpassed worlds.
On Rohiṇī, cooked black-gram grains with food and clarified butter / should be given, with milk as after-drink, to a twice-born man, in order to become free from debt.
Having given a milch cow with her calf under the asterism ruled by Soma, / one goes to human worlds [and then to] an unsurpassed dwelling in heaven.
Having fasted and given kṛsara mixed with oil during Ārdrā, / a man crosses impassable places and mountains of razor blades.
Having given cakes during Punarvasu and likewise excellent food, / one is born famous, endowed with beauty, possessing abundant food, in a noble family.

3.64.s:
puṣye tu kanakaṃ dattvā kṛtaṃ vākṛtameva ca ..
anālokeṣu lokeṣu somavatsa virājate .. 7 ..

sa sarvabhayanirmuktaḥ śubhaṃ cāpyadhigacchati .. 8 ..

pradāya putrapaśumāniha pretya ca modate .. 9 ..

bhakṣyaṃ phāṇitasaṃyuktaṃ dattvā saubhāgyamṛcchati ..3.318.10..
ghṛtakṣīrasamāyuktaṃ vidhivatṣāṣṭikaudanam ..
uttarāviṣaye dattvā svagarloke mahīyate .. 11 ..

3.64.d:
पुष्ये तु कनकं दत्त्वा कृतं वाकृतमेव च ॥
अनालोकेषु लोकेषु सोमवत्स विराजते ॥ 7 ॥
अश्लेषासु च यो रूप्यं वृषभं वा प्रयच्छति ॥
स सर्वभयनिर्मुक्तः शुभं चाप्यधिगच्छति ॥ 8 ॥
मघासु तिलपूर्णानि वर्णमानानि मानवः ॥
प्रदाय पुत्रपशुमानिह प्रेत्य च मोदते ॥ 9 ॥
फाल्गुनीपूर्वसमये ब्राह्मणानामुपोषितः ॥
भक्ष्यं फाणितसंयुक्तं दत्त्वा सौभाग्यमृच्छति ॥3.318.10॥
घृतक्षीरसमायुक्तं विधिवत्षाष्टिकौदनम् ॥
उत्तराविषये दत्त्वा स्वगर्लोके महीयते ॥ 11 ॥
यद्यत्प्रदीयते दानं चोत्तराविषये नरैः ॥
महाफलमतीतञ्च भवतीति विनिश्चयः ॥ 12 ॥
हस्ते हस्तिरथं दत्त्वा चतुर्युक्तमुपोषितः ॥
नरस्तरति दुर्गाणि क्षुरधारांश्च पर्वतान् ॥ 13 ॥
चित्रायां वृषभं दत्त्वा पुण्यगन्धांश्च मानवः ॥
चरत्यप्सरसां लोके रमते नन्दने वने ॥ 14 ॥
3.64.m:
Having given gold during Puṣya, whether wrought or unwrought, / he shines like the moon in worlds free from darkness.
And he who gives silver or a bull under Āśleṣā, / being freed from all fear, attains welfare as well.
Under Maghā, having given vessels measured by weight filled with sesame seeds, / a man rejoices here and in the hereafter, possessed of sons and cattle.
Having fasted at the time of Pūrva-phālgunī and given to brahmins / edible food mixed with treacle, he obtains good fortune.
Having given, according to rule, sixty-day rice mixed with clarified butter and milk / under Uttarā, he is honored in the heavenly world.
Whatever gift is given by men under Uttarā, / it becomes of great, extraordinary fruit; such is the certainty.
Having fasted and given an elephant-drawn chariot yoked with four [elephants] under Hasta, / a man crosses impassable places and mountains of razor blades.
Having given a bull and sacred fragrances under Citrā, / a man moves about in the world of the apsarases and sports in the Nandana forest.

svātīṣvatha dhanaṃ dattvā yadiṣṭatamamātmanaḥ ..
prāpnoti lokānsa śubhānihaiva ca mahadyaśaḥ .. 15 ..
viśākhāyāmanaḍvāhaṃ dhenuṃ dattvā ca dugdhadām ..
saprāsaṅgaṃ ca śakaṭaṃ sadhānyaṃ vastrasaṃmitam .. 16 ..
pitṝṃśca devānprīṇāti prāpya cānantyamaśnute ..
na ca durgāṇyavāpnoti svagarlokaṃ ca gacchati .. 17 ..
dattvā yathoktaṃ viprebhyo vṛttimiṣṭāṃ sa vindati ..
narakādīṃśca sa kleśānna prāpnotīti niścayaḥ .. 16 ..
anurādhāsu prāvāraṃ vastrāntaramupoṣitaḥ ..
dattvā yugaśataṃ cāpi naraḥ svarge mahīyate .. 19 ..
kālaśākaṃ tu viprebhyo dattvā martyaḥ samūlakam ..
jyeṣṭhāyāmṛddhimiṣṭāñca gatimiṣṭāñca gacchati..3.318.20..
mūle mūlaphalaṃ dattvā brāhmaṇebhyaḥ samāhitaḥ..
sa pitṝnprīṇayatyeva gatimiṣṭāñca gacchati .. 21 ..
3.64.d:
स्वातीष्वथ धनं दत्त्वा यदिष्टतममात्मनः ॥
प्राप्नोति लोकान्स शुभानिहैव च महद्यशः ॥ 15 ॥
विशाखायामनड्वाहं धेनुं दत्त्वा च दुग्धदाम् ॥
सप्रासङ्गं च शकटं सधान्यं वस्त्रसंमितम् ॥ 16 ॥
पितॄंश्च देवान्प्रीणाति प्राप्य चानन्त्यमश्नुते ॥
न च दुर्गाण्यवाप्नोति स्वगर्लोकं च गच्छति ॥ 17 ॥
दत्त्वा यथोक्तं विप्रेभ्यो वृत्तिमिष्टां स विन्दति ॥
नरकादींश्च स क्लेशान्न प्राप्नोतीति निश्चयः ॥ 16 ॥
अनुराधासु प्रावारं वस्त्रान्तरमुपोषितः ॥
दत्त्वा युगशतं चापि नरः स्वर्गे महीयते ॥ 19 ॥
कालशाकं तु विप्रेभ्यो दत्त्वा मर्त्यः समूलकम् ॥
ज्येष्ठायामृद्धिमिष्टाञ्च गतिमिष्टाञ्च गच्छति॥3.318.20॥
मूले मूलफलं दत्त्वा ब्राह्मणेभ्यः समाहितः॥
स पितॄन्प्रीणयत्येव गतिमिष्टाञ्च गच्छति ॥ 21 ॥
3.64.m:
Then having given wealth under Svātī, whatever is dearest to himself, / he attains auspicious worlds and great renown right here.
Under Viśākhā, having given a draft bull, a cow yielding milk, / and a cart equipped with a yoke-pole, filled with grain and covered with cloth,
he pleases the ancestors and the gods, and having attained it, he enjoys eternity; / he does not encounter impassable places, and goes to the heavenly world.
Having given as prescribed to the brahmins, he finds a desirable livelihood, / and he does not meet with afflictions such as hell; such is the certainty.
Having fasted and given a mantle with an inner garment under Anurādhā, / a man is honored in heaven for a hundred yugas.
Having given black greens with roots to brahmins under Jyeṣṭhā, / a mortal goes to desired prosperity and to a desired destination.
Having given roots and fruits with a composed mind to brahmins under Mūla, / he indeed pleases the ancestors and goes to a desired destination.

वस्त्ररश्मिनवं सद्यः प्रेत्य राज्यं प्रपद्यते ॥

पूर्वाभाद्रपदायोगे राजमाषान्प्रदाय च ॥ ॥ 28॥
3.64.m:
Then, having fasted under Pūrvā-Āṣāḍhā and given bowls of curd / to a brahmin who has mastered the Vedas and is endowed with conduct and noble birth,
having passed away, he is born in a family possessing many herds of cows. / Having given a water jar with clarified butter and abundant honey and treacle
under Uttarā-Āṣāḍhā, he enjoys all the worlds. / Having given milk flooded with honey and clarified butter in the conjunction with Abhijit,
and ever [giving] armor to wise men, he is honored in the heavenly world. / Having given a blanket lined with cloth under Śravaṇa,
he goes in a white vehicle to unobstructed heavenly worlds. / Having given with a composed mind a vehicle yoked with cattle under Dhaniṣṭhā,
brand-new with cloth reins, after death he immediately attains kingship. / Having given perfumes with aloe and sandalwood in the conjunction with Śatabhiṣaj,
he attains the worlds of the apsarases and eternal fragrances after death. / And having given black-eyed peas in the conjunction with Pūrvā-Bhādrapadā,

3.64.d:
सर्वभक्ष्यफलोपेतं स वै प्रेत्य सुखी भवेत् ॥
औरभ्रं तूत्तरायोगे यस्तु मांसं प्रयच्छति ॥29॥
स पितॄन्प्रीणयत्येव प्रेत्य चानन्त्यमश्नुते ॥
कांस्योपदोहनां धेनुं रेवत्यां यः प्रयच्छति ॥ 3.318.30 ॥
स प्रेत्य कामानादाय दातारमुपतिष्ठते ॥
रथमश्वसमायुक्तं दत्त्वाश्विन्यां नरोत्तमः ॥ 31 ॥
हस्त्यश्वरथसम्पन्नं वर्चस्वी जायते कुले ॥
भरणीषु द्विजातिभ्यस्तिलधेनुं प्रदाय वै ॥
गाः सुप्रसूताश्चाप्नोति नरः प्रेत्य यशस्तथा ॥ 32 ॥
नक्षत्रसत्त्रं कथितं मयैतद्यथेष्टलोकाभिगमाय पुंसाम् ॥
कृत्वा सकृन्नाकगतस्तु कल्पमास्ते मुखं देवपतिर्यथासौ ॥ 33 ॥

3.64.m:
endowed with all edible food and fruits, he will indeed be happy after death. / But he who gives the meat of a sheep in the conjunction with Uttarā[-Bhādrapadā],
he indeed pleases the ancestors and enjoys eternity after death. / He who gives a cow with a bronze milking vessel under Revatī,
that [gift], having assumed [the form of all] desires, attends upon the giver after death. / Having given a chariot yoked with horses under Aśvinī, the best of men
is born radiant in a family endowed with elephants, horses, and chariots. / Having given a sesame-cow to the twice-born under Bharaṇī, / a man obtains cows that have calved well and renown after death.
This Nakṣatrasattra has been declared by me for men's attainment of their desired worlds; / having performed it once, one who has gone to heaven dwells [there] happily for an aeon, like the lord of the gods.
The sages said: / Tell us once again, O best of the twice-born, the fruit of gifts / according to the temporal conjunction, O you whose clear vision is manifest.

3.64.d:
॥ हंस उवाच ॥ ॥
संप्राप्य चैत्रमासस्य शुक्लां पञ्चदशीं नरः ॥
चित्रं वस्त्रयुगं दत्त्वा सोपवासो द्विजातये ॥2 ॥
ब्राह्मणांश्चापरं विप्राः सौभाग्यं महदाप्नुयात् ॥
वैशाख्यां पौर्णमास्यान्तु ब्राह्मणान्सप्त पञ्च वा ॥ 3 ॥
क्षौद्रयुक्तैस्तिलैः कृष्णैर्वाचयेद्यदि वेतरैः ॥
प्रीयतां धर्मराजेति यद्वा मनसि वर्त्तते ॥ 4 ॥
यावज्जीवकृतात्पापात्तत्क्षणादेव मुच्यते ॥
तस्मिन्नेव तथा काले सखुरं कृष्णमार्गणम् ॥ 5 ॥
तिलैः प्रच्छाद्य वासोभिः सर्वरत्नैरलंकृतम् ॥
तपस्यन्ते च दातव्यो मही सवनकानना ॥ 6 ॥
कृष्णाजिने तिलान्कृत्वा हिरण्यमधुसर्पिषा ॥
ददाति यस्तु विप्राय सर्वं तरति दुष्कृतम् ॥ 7 ॥
सोपवासस्तथा ज्येष्ठे पूर्णे तु शशलक्ष्मणे ॥
उपानहौ तथा च्छत्रं दत्त्वात्यन्तसुखी भवेत् ॥ 8 ॥
3.64.m:
Haṃsa said: / Having reached the bright fifteenth day of the month of Caitra, / a man who fasts, having given a pair of colorful garments to a twice-born man,
and [feeding] brahmins, O brahmins, he will attain great good fortune. / On the full moon of Vaiśākha, however, [he should invite] five or seven brahmins
and have [them] recite with black sesame seeds mixed with honey, or with other [sesame seeds], / saying, "May the King of Dharma be pleased!" or whatever is in his heart.
He is freed that very instant from the sins committed throughout his life. / At that very time, likewise, [presenting] a black antelope-skin complete with hooves,
covered with sesame seeds and garments, and adorned with every [kind of] jewel— / and at the end of winter [such a gift] should be given, [or] the earth together with groves and forests.
He who places sesame seeds upon a black antelope-skin, along with gold, honey, and clarified butter, / and gives it to a brahmin, crosses over all wrongdoing.
Likewise, fasting in Jyeṣṭha when the hare-marked [moon] is full, / and giving shoes and a parasol, he becomes exceedingly happy.

आषाढ्यामन्नदानस्य प्राप्नोत्यन्नं नरो बहु ॥
जलधेनुप्रदानेन श्रावण्यां स्वर्गमाप्नुयात् ॥ 9 ॥
गोदानं प्रोष्ठपादे तु पौर्णमास्यां महाफलम् ॥
आश्वयुज्यं कांस्यपात्रां घृतपूर्णं द्विजातये ॥ 3.319.10 ॥
सुवर्णञ्च तथा दत्त्वा दीप्तिमांस्त्वभिजायते ॥
कार्तिक्यां चन्द्रवर्णाभमन्यवर्णमथापि वा ॥ 11 ॥
रत्नैर्गन्धैस्तथा धान्यैर्बीजैर्वस्त्रैस्तथैव च ॥
कृत्वा युक्तमथोक्षाणं दत्त्वा दीपान्समन्त्रतः ॥ 52 ॥
चन्द्रोदये नरो दत्त्वा सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते ॥
कान्तारे यममार्गे तु तेनासौ व्रजते सुखम् ॥ 13 ॥
सर्वाणि चास्य भोगानि तत्र चासौ प्रयच्छति ॥
मार्गशीर्षे तथा मासे पूर्णे शिशिरदीधितौ ॥ 14 ॥
महारजतयुक्तेन वाससा द्विज पुङ्गवान् ॥
आच्छाद्य कांस्यपात्रस्थं प्रस्थं कृत्वा समाहितः ॥15 ॥
3.64.m:
From the gift of food on the Āṣāḍha full moon, a man obtains abundant food. / By the gift of a water-cow on the Śrāvaṇa full moon, he attains heaven.
The gift of a cow on the full moon of Proṣṭhapada brings great reward. / On the full moon of Āśvayuja, [giving] a bell-metal vessel filled with clarified butter to a twice-born,
and likewise giving gold, he is born endowed with splendor. / In Kārttika, [giving] an ox of the color of the moon or of another color,
having adorned it with gems, scents, grains, seeds, and garments, / and presenting lamps with the appropriate mantras,
a man giving [these] at moonrise is freed from all sins; / he then journeys with ease along the dreadful path of Yama,
and [that gift] provides him with all pleasures there. / Likewise in the month of Mārgaśīrṣa, when the cool-rayed [moon] is full,
having covered the foremost twice-born with cloth dyed with safflower, / and having concentrated his mind, preparing a prastha [measure] placed in a bell-metal vessel,

3.64.d:
लवणस्य तु मुख्यस्य चूर्णितस्य द्विजोत्तमाः ॥
दत्त्वा सुवर्णनाभन्तु तस्मिन्नेव द्विजातये ॥ 16 ॥
सौभाग्यरूपलावण्ययुक्तो भवति मानवः ॥
गौरसर्षपकल्केन पौष्यामुत्साहितो नरः ॥ 17 ॥
गव्यस्याज्यस्य कुम्भेन सोभिषिक्तस्त्वनन्तरम् ॥
विरूक्षितस्तथा स्नातः सर्वबीजौषधीजलैः ॥ 18 ॥
गन्धरत्नफलोपेतैर्घृतेन तदनन्तरम् ॥
स सुवर्णं मुखं दृष्ट्वा तत्प्रदद्याद्द्विजातये ॥ 19 ॥
घृतेन स्नपितं विष्णुं शक्त्या सम्पूजयेत्ततः ॥
घृतञ्च जुहुयाद्वह्नौ घृतं दद्याद्द्विजातये ॥ 3.319.20 ॥
कर्त्रे वस्त्रयुगं दद्यात्सोपवासः समाहितः ॥
कर्मणानेन धर्मज्ञाः पुष्टिमाप्नोत्यनुत्तमाम् ॥ 21 ॥
माघ्यां कृत्वा तिलैः श्राद्धं सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते ॥
स्वास्तीर्णं शयनं दत्त्वा फाल्गुन्यां ब्राह्मणस्य तु ॥ 22 ॥
3.64.m:
of excellent powdered salt, O best of the twice-born, / and giving it along with a navel of gold to a twice-born on that very day,
a man becomes endowed with good fortune, beauty, and charm. / On the full moon of Pauṣa, an energetic man, [anointed] with a paste of white mustard seeds,
is then sprinkled with a pot of cow's clarified butter; / having rubbed off the oil and bathed with waters containing all seeds and herbs,
accompanied by scents, jewels, and fruits, he should immediately thereafter / look at his face in clarified butter together with gold and give it to a twice-born.
He should then worship Viṣṇu, who has been bathed in clarified butter, according to his capacity, / and offer clarified butter into the fire and give clarified butter to a twice-born.
Fasting and composed, he should present a pair of garments to the officiating priest. / By this rite, O knowers of dharma, he attains unsurpassed prosperity.
Having performed a śrāddha with sesame seeds on the full moon of Māgha, he is freed from all sins. / By giving a well-spread couch to a brahmin on the Phālguna full moon,

3.64.d:
रूपद्रविणसंयुक्तां भार्यां पक्षवतीं तथा ॥
नरः प्राप्नोति धर्मज्ञः पुष्टिमाप्नोत्यनुत्तमाम् ॥ 23 ॥
तथा नार्यपि भर्तारं नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥
पौर्णमासीषु चैतासु मासर्क्षसहितासु च ॥ 24 ॥
एतेषामेव दानानां फलं दशगुणं भवेत् ॥
महत्पूर्वासु चैतासु फलमक्षय्यमश्नुते ॥ 25 ॥
द्वादश्यां चैत्रशुक्लस्य चित्रवस्त्रप्रदो नरः ॥
अक्षयं फलमाप्नोति नाकलोके च गच्छति ॥ 26 ॥
वैशाखमासे द्वादश्यां रुक्मदानात्तथैव च ॥
छत्रोपानहयोर्दानाज्ज्येष्ठे मासि द्विजोत्तमाः ॥ 27 ॥
स्वास्तीर्णं शयनं दत्त्वा प्रीणयेद्भोगिशायिनम् ॥
आषाढ शुक्लद्वादश्यां श्वेतद्वीपे महीयते ॥ 28 ॥
श्रावणे वस्त्रदानेन विष्णुलोके महीयते ॥
गोदः प्रयाति गोलोकं मासि भाद्रपदे द्विजाः ॥ 29 ॥
3.64.m:
a man who knows dharma obtains a wife endowed with beauty and wealth, / blessed with an excellent family, and attains unsurpassed prosperity.
Likewise, a woman [obtains such] a husband; here no doubt should be entertained. / On these full moons, when conjoined with the lunar mansion belonging to that month,
the fruit of these very gifts becomes tenfold; / and on those [full moons] that have the mahat prefix, he enjoys imperishable fruit.
On the twelfth lunar day of the bright fortnight of Caitra, a man who gives multi-colored garments / obtains imperishable reward and goes to the heavenly realm.
In the month of Vaiśākha on the twelfth lunar day, from the gift of gold, / and in the month of Jyeṣṭha from the gift of a parasol and shoes, O best of the twice-born,
[and] by offering a well-spread couch, he pleases the one who reclines on the serpent; / on the twelfth day of the bright fortnight of Āṣāḍha, he is exalted in Śvetadvīpa.
In Śrāvaṇa, by the gift of garments, he is exalted in the world of Viṣṇu. / A giver of a cow goes to Goloka in the month of Bhādrapada, O twice-born.

3.64.d:

3.64.d:
दानान्यथैतानि मया द्विजेन्द्रा। प्रोक्तानि काले तु नरश्च दत्त्वा ॥

3.320
ऋषय ऊचुः ॥
पुण्ययज्ञक्रियाः प्रोक्ता ये नरा धनसंयुताः ॥
तथा मध्यमवृत्तानां दानानि विविधानि च ॥ 1 ॥
कथितान्यल्पवृत्तानां दानानि विविधानि च ॥
ये नरा वित्तरहितास्तेषां धर्मक्रियां वद ॥ 2 ॥
हंस उवाच ॥
उपवासक्रिया तेषां परमं धर्मकारणम् ॥
वित्तान्वितानाञ्च तथा प्रशस्ता सा महाफला ॥ 3 ॥
सायं प्रातस्तु भुञ्जानो नान्तरातूदकम्पिबन् ॥
षड्भिर्वर्षैर्नरो लोकं प्राप्नोति मनसेप्सितम् ॥ 4॥
शुभानामुत्तमं चैतद्धन्यं नित्यकृतं भवेत् ॥
यथेष्टलोकदं पुण्यं मानुष्येपि महाफलम् ॥ 5॥
उपवासं नरः कुर्वन्मासिमासि द्विजोत्तमाः ॥
उषित्वा सुचिरं लोके मानुष्ये जायते यदा ॥ 6 ॥
3.64.m:
These gifts have thus been proclaimed by me, O chiefs among the twice-born; and having bestowed them at the proper time, / a man attains the desires cherished in his heart; therefore they extol the great offering.
3.320 / The sages said: / Meritorious sacrificial rites have been declared for those men who possess wealth, / as well as various kinds of gifts for those of middling livelihood.
Various kinds of gifts have also been stated for those of meager livelihood. / For those men who are destitute of wealth, declare the practice of dharma.
The Swan said: / The practice of fasting is their supreme cause of dharma; / likewise, for those endowed with wealth, it is praised as having great fruit.
A man who eats only in the evening and morning, not drinking water in between, / attains after six years the world desired by his mind.
And this, best among auspicious deeds, when performed continually becomes fortunate; / it grants any desired world, is meritorious, and yields great fruit even in human birth.
A man who undertakes a fast month after month, O foremost of the twice-born, / after dwelling for a very long time in that world, when he is born in human existence,

3.64.d:
तदा भवति दीर्घायुर्धनवान्रूपसंयुतः ॥
पक्षेपक्षे तथा कुर्वन्द्विगुणं फलमश्नुते ॥ 7 ॥
मासेमासे त्रिरात्रन्तु यः कुर्यान्मानवोत्तमः ॥
गाणपत्यमवाप्नोति स्वर्गलोकपरिच्युतः ॥ 8 ॥
पक्षेपक्षे त्रिरात्रन्तु कृत्वा भवति पार्थिवः ॥
स्वर्गलोकात्परिभ्रष्टः सुचिरेण महाबलः ॥ 9 ॥
द्विजस्त्रिरात्रं कुर्वीत न तु शूद्रः कथञ्चन ॥
षष्ठकालाशनं तस्य तपः परमिहोच्यते ॥ 3.320.10 ॥
शूद्रस्त्रिरात्रं कुरुते विषये यस्य भूपतेः ॥
तस्य सीदति तद्राष्ट्रं व्याधिदुर्भिक्षतस्करैः ॥ 11 ॥
तपः कुर्वीत शूद्रस्तु चैकद्विदिवसान्तरम् ॥
यथाशक्ति द्विजश्रेष्ठास्तेन कामानुपाश्नुते ॥ 12 ॥
अतः परन्तु वर्णानां मासेमासे द्विजोत्तमाः ॥
एक कालाशनानान्तु शृणुध्वं फलमुत्तमम् ॥ 13 ॥
3.64.m:
he then becomes long-lived, wealthy, and endowed with beauty. / Performing it fortnight by fortnight in the same way, he enjoys double the fruit.
A best of men who observes a three-night fast month after month, / after falling from the heavenly world, attains the status of a leader of a troop.
Having observed a three-night fast fortnight by fortnight, he becomes a king; / after a very long time, fallen from the heavenly world, he becomes exceedingly powerful.
A twice-born may undertake a three-night fast, but never a śūdra; / eating at every sixth mealtime is declared here to be his supreme austerity.
In the realm of whichever king a śūdra undertakes a three-night fast, / his kingdom suffers from disease, famine, and thieves.
A śūdra should perform austerity with an interval of one or two days, / according to his capacity, O best of the twice-born; through that he obtains his desires.
Beyond this, O foremost of the twice-born, hear the supreme fruit / of the classes who eat only once a day month after month.
